>   "text": "173\n BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                       Technical Specifications\n\n\n\n                                   iii.  While the mechanical device is in operation no workmen shall be allowed\n                       to enter the building being demolished;\n\n                        iv. The device shall be so located as to avoid falling debris; and\n\n                     v. The device when being used shall not cause any damage to adjacent\n                        structure, power line, other services, etc.\n\n       3.7    Protection of the public\n\n       Protection of the public before and during demolition is important and the following points\n       should be kept in mind:\n\n       a) Every sidewalk or road adjacent to the work shall be closed or protected. All main\n           roads, which are open to the public shall be kept open to the public clear and\n          unobstructed at all times.\n       b)  Children and public shall be kept out of the building and the adjoining yards.\n        c)   If the structure to be demolished is more than two-storied or 7.5 m high, measured\n          from the sidewalk or street which cannot be closed or safely diverted, and the\n           horizontal distance from the inside edge of the side walk to the structure is 4.5 m or\n            less, a substantial side walk shed shall be constructed over the entire length of the\n          sidewalk adjacent to the structure of sufficient width with a view to accommodating\n           the pedestrian  traffic without causing congestion. The sidewalk shall be lighted\n             sufficiently to ensure safety at all times.\n       d) The structure to be demolished/dismantled must have barricades, which shall be of\n            plain MS Sheet of 16 gauge fixed with steel frame, painting, with synthetic enamel\n           paint of approved color, quality and brand, writing letter and logo of metro including\n         maintenance of the same, duly cleaning the same frequently, arrangement for blinker\n             light as per requirement. During demolition barricades has to be kept continuously.\n         Removal of barricade will not be permitted till completion of demolition, dismantling\n            of properties.\n       e) A toe board at least 1 m high above the roof of the side walk shed shall be provided\n         on the outside edge and ends of the sidewalk shed. Such boards may be vertical or\n            inclined outward at not more than 45 degrees.\n           f)  Except where the roof of a side walk shed solidly abuts the structure, the face of the\n          sidewalk shed towards the building shall be completely closed by providing sheeting\n                  / planking to prevent falling material penetrating into the shed.\n       g) The roof of the sidewalk shed shall be capable of sustaining a load of 730 kg/m2.\n          Only in exceptional cases, say due to lack of other space, the storing of the material\n         on a sidewalk shed may be permitted in which case the shed shall be designed for a\n          load of 1460 kg/m2. Roof of sidewalk shed shall be designed taking into account the\n          impact of the falling debris. By frequent removal of loads it shall be ensured that the\n        maximum load, at any time, on the roof of the shed is not more than 600 kg/m2. The\n           height of the sidewalk shed shall be such as to give minimum clearance of 2.4 m.\n       h) Sidewalk shed openings, for loading purposes, shall be kept closed at all times except\n           during actual loading operations.\n            i)  The deck flooring of the sidewalk shed shall consist of plank of not less than 50 mm\n           thickness closely laid and deck made watertight.\n            j)   All members of the shed shall be adequately braced and connected to resist\n          displacement of members or distortion of framework.\n        k) When the horizontal distance from the inside edge of the sidewalk to the structure is\n         more than 4.5 m and less than 7.5 m, a sidewalk shed or fence may be built or in their\n          place a substantial railing shall be constructed on the inside of the sidewalk or\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 23 of 37",

>   "text": "175\n BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                       Technical Specifications\n\n\n       3.10   Demolition of walls\n\n       3.10.1 Procedure.   The following procedure shall be followed when demolishing walls:\n\n        a) While walls or sections of masonry are being demolished  it shall be ensured that\n           they are not allowed to fall as a single mass on the floors of the building so as not to\n          exceed the safe carrying capacity of the floor; wherever practicable, they may fall\n         away from the floors on to catch platforms. Overloading of floors shall be prevented\n          by removing the accumulating debris through chutes or by other means immediately.\n         The floor shall be inspected by the Authority before undertaking demolition work and\n                     if the same is found incapable of carrying the load of debris, necessary precautions\n             shall be taken to prevent any unexpected collapse of the floor.\n        b)  Walls shall be removed part by part. Stages shall be provided for the men to work\n           on, if the walls are very thin and dangerous to work by standing over them.\n         c) No section of the wall whose height is more than 15 times the thickness, shall be\n           permitted to stand without lateral bracing unless such a wall is in good condition and\n         was originally designed to stand without such lateral bracing or support.\n        d)  Structural or load supporting members on any floor shall not be removed or cut until\n                all the storey above that floor have been demolished and removed.\n        e)  Before demolishing any interior or exterior wall within 3 m of the opening in the floor\n           immediately below, such opening shall be substantially planked over, unless access\n               is denied to workmen to that portion of the floor immediately below the opening, in\n           the floor of the storey being demolished, where any debris passing through the\n          opening may fall.\n            f)  In framed structures, if the structure is properly designed to the standards and to the\n            specifications in such cases the frame may be left in position during demolition of\n          masonry work. Where this is done all beams, girders, etc., shall be cleared of all\n           loose materials as the demolition of masonry work progresses downward provided it\n               is still strong enough to stand as an independent structure.\n\n        g) The structure to be demolished/dismantled must have barricades, which shall be of\n             plain MS Sheet of 16 gauge fixed with steel frame, painting, with synthetic enamel\n            paint of approved color, quality and brand, writing letter and logo of metro including\n          maintenance of the same, duly cleaning the same frequently, arrangement for blinker\n              light as per requirement. During demolition barricades has to be kept continuously.\n         Removal of barricade will not be permitted till completion of demolition, dismantling\n             of properties.\n        h) Walkways shall be provided to enable workmen to reach or leave their work on any\n            scaffold or wall. Such walkways shall neither be less than 3 planks wide, nor less\n           than 0.8 m in width.\n             i)   After completion of each day’s work, all walls shall be left stable to avoid any danger\n             of getting overturned.\n             j)  Foundation walls which serve as retaining walls to support the earth or adjoining\n             structure, shall not be demolished until such an adjoining structure has been under\n           pinned or braced and the earth removed by sheet piling or sheathing.\n\n       3.10.2 Catch platforms\n      Catch platforms shall be provided in case of demolition of exterior walls in multi-storey\n        buildings. The following details may be considered:\n\n       a) Catch platforms shall generally be provided for multi-storied buildings more than 20\n    m high to prevent injuries to the worker and to the public when exterior walls are being\n       demolished.\n       b)    Such platforms shall be constructed and maintained not more than three storey\n      below the storey from which the exterior wall is being demolished. When demolition has\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 25 of 37",

>   "text": "172\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n                     (j)  Construction sheds and toolboxes should be so located as to protect workers from\n                    injuries of falling objects, wall, etc.\n                (k) A warning device should be installed in the area to be used to warn the workers, in\n               case of danger.\n                     (l)  Screens shall be placed, where necessary, to prevent flying pieces from injuring the\n                   fellow workmen.\n            (m) No demolition work shall be carried out during storm or heavy rain.\n               (n) No demolition work shall be carried out at night especially when the building or\n                   structure to be demolished is in an inhabited area.\n               (o)  All necessary safety appliances shall be issued to the workmen and their use\n                  explained. It shall be ensured that the workers are using all the safety appliances\n                  while at work. The safety appliances should be as follows:\n\n                     (1)    Safety helmets as per IS 2925: 1984;\n                     (2)    Goggles made of celluloid lens to be worn at the time of demolition of floors,\n                             walls, tearing of plaster, etc., especially when equipment like jack hammers\n                         are used for demolition work, to protect the eyes from flying pieces, dust,\n                                    dirt, etc. that may be blown up by wind.\n                     (3)    Leather or rubber gloves to be worn during demolition of RCC work or\n                       removing steel work, where the hands of workers are likely to be injured.\n                     (4)    Safety belts while working  at higher level to prevent  falling from the\n                             structure.\n\n                (p) First-aid equipment shall be available at all demolition works of any magnitude. Also,\n               by prior arrangement, a qualified doctor be available at call.\n               (q) When there is a possibility of fire breaking out, appropriate portable first-aid fire\n                 appliances (see IS 2190: 1992) shall be kept at hand.\n                  (r)  The removal of a member may weaken the side wall of an adjoining structure and to\n                 prevent possible damage, these walls  shall be supported  until such time as\n               permanent protection is provided.  In case of any danger is anticipated to the\n                  adjoining structure, the same shall be got vacated to avoid any danger to human life.\n                (s)  Ladders, when used, shall conform to IS 3696 (Part 2): 1991. Ladders or their side\n                      rails shall extend not less than 1.0 m above the floor or platform to which the ladder\n                 gives access. All ladders shall be secured against slipping out at the bottom and\n                  against movement in any direction at the top.\n                   (t)   All exterior wall openings which extend down to the floor level shall be barricaded to\n               a height not less than 1 m above the floor level. All floor openings and shafts not\n               meant as material chutes shall be floored over and endorsed with ground rails and\n                 toe boards.\n               (u)  All existing fixtures/services required during demolition operations shall be well\n                 protected with substantial covering to the satisfaction of the Authority.\n                (v) When demolition is to be done by mechanical means such as weight ball and power\n                  shovels, the following additional precautions are necessary:\n\n                                              i. The area shall be barricaded for a minimum distance of 1 ½ times the\n                            height of the wall.\n\n                                               ii. The structure to be demolished/dismantled must have barricades, which\n                               shall be of plain MS Sheet of 16 gauge fixed with steel frame, painting,\n                             with synthetic enamel paint of approved color, quality and brand, writing\n                                  letter and logo of metro including maintenance of the same, duly cleaning\n                           the same frequently, arrangement for blinker light as per requirement.\n                          During demolition barricades has to be kept continuously. Removal of\n                           barricade will not be permitted till completion of demolition, dismantling of\n                             properties\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 22 of 37",

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4A#Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 4A: Specifications for Demolition/Dismantling Works|Vol 2 Part 4A]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 27 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4a_demolition/demolition_clauses.json#/source_page_context/4`)

>   "text": "174\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n               roadway along the entire length of demolition side of the property with movable bars\n               as may be necessary for the proper prosecution of the work.\n                       l)  Where workers entrances to the building being demolished are not completely\n                 protected by sidewalk sheds, all such entrances shall be protected by canopies\n                extending from the face of the building to a point not less than 2.5 m from it. In such\n              a case, overhead projection shall be at least 0.6 m wider than the building entrance\n                  or opening and every canopy shall be as strong as the sidewalk shed.\n\n             3.8   Sequence of demolition operations: The sequence of demolition shall generally\n           be as given below:\n\n              a) The demolition shall always proceed systematically storey by storey in descending\n             order and the demolition of upper floors shall be completely over before any of the\n             supporting members or other important portion on the lower floor  is disturbed. No\n            unnecessary work shall go on below when the demolition is in progress above. When\n          some work is to be done at the lower level, adequate protection shall be provided for all\n             the workmen so engaged.\n              b) The requirements of (a) shall not prohibit the demolition of structures by sections, if\n          means are taken to prevent injuries to persons or damage to property.\n               c)     Roofs (or floors), generally, be demolished first before demolishing the supporting\n              walls structural elements.\n              d)      All glazed sash, glazed doors and windows etc., shall be removed before the\n              demolition of roofs and walls starts. All fragile and loose fixtures shall be removed. Lath\n           and loose plaster be stripped off throughout the entire structure. This is advantageous\n           because it reduces glass breakage and also eliminates a large amount of dust producing\n              material before more substantial parts of the building are removed.\n              e) The structure to be demolished/dismantled must have barricades, which shall be of\n               plain MS Sheet of 16 gauge fixed with steel frame, painting, with synthetic enamel paint\n               of approved  color,  quality and brand,  writing  letter and logo  of metro  including\n            maintenance of the same, duly cleaning the same frequently, arrangement for blinker\n                 light as per requirement. During demolition barricades has to be kept continuously.\n           Removal of barricade will not be permitted  till completion of demolition, dismantling of\n              properties\n\n             3.9    Demolition of floors. For demolition of floors the following procedure may be\n               followed:\n\n              a) A slit in width not exceeding 300 mm shall be cut at the first stage for the entire length\n               of the slab along which it spans. The opening shall thereafter be increased to the desired\n             width by suitable installments.\n              b)     Planks of sufficient strength not less than 50 mm thick and 250 mm wide shall be\n             provided at a spacing not greater than 0.4 m. These planks shall be so placed as to give\n           workmen firm support to guard against any unexpected collapse.\n               c)     Stringers of ample strength shall be installed to support the planks where\n            necessary and the ends of stringers shall be supported by floor beams, girders and not\n            by floor slab alone.\n              d)    When floors are being removed, no workmen shall be allowed to work in the area,\n                directly underneath and such area shall be barricaded to prevent access to it.\n              e)    The demolition of the floor in question shall be started only after the surrounding\n            area for a distance of 6 m have been entirely cleared of persons, and the debris and other\n            unnecessary material removed.\n                    f)     Planks used for temporary protection shall be sound and at least 50 mm thick.\n           They shall be laid close together with ends overlapping at least 100 mm over solid bearing\n               to prevent tipping under load.\n\n\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 24 of 37",

>   "text": "176\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n            progressed to within three storey of ground level, catch platforms will not be considered\n             necessary.\n               c)     Catch platforms shall not be less than 1.5 m in width measured in a horizontal\n               direction from the face of the structure and shall consist of outriggers supported not more\n             than 3 m apart. Planks shall be laid tight together, without openings between them and\n             the walls. Catch platforms shall be provided with a continuous solid parapet along its\n              outer edge of at least 1 m height. The parapet may be constructed with the same material\n            as the platform.\n              d) Catch platform shall be capable of sustaining a live load of not less than 610 kg/m2.\n              e) Catch platforms shall neither be used for storing of materials nor dumping of\n                  materials.\n\n             3.11   Demolition of different types of structures and elements\n\n             3.11.1 General.      Structures may be dealt with as masonry, concrete, steel and\n              timber. The structures or their elements shall be dealt with as below, in addition to other\n             requirements as applicable.\n\n            3.11.2 Masonry structures.  Jack Arches – Where tie rods are present between main\n            supporting beams, these should not be cut until after the arch or series of arches in the\n               floor have been removed. Particular care should be exercised and full examination of\n             structure be made before the demolition is commenced. The floor should be demolished\n               in strips parallel to the span of arch rings (at right angles to the main floor beam).\n\n\n\n            Brick Arches\n\n              1)   As much dead load as possible may be removed provided it does not interfere with\n                 stability of main arch rings; it should be noted that the load carrying capacity of many old\n             arches relies on the filling between the spandrels. On no account should the restraining\n              influence of the abutments be removed before the dead load of the spandrel fill and the\n             arch rings are removed. The normal sequence of demolition includes the following:\n                           -    remove the spandrel filling down to the springing line,\n                           -    remove the arch rings,\n                           -    Remove the abutments.\n\n              2)   A single span arch can be demolished, by hand, by cutting narrow segments\n              progressively from each springing parallel to the span of the arch, until the width of the\n             arch has been reduced to a minimum which can then collapse. Where it is impossible to\n              allow debris to fall to the ground below, centering designed to carry the load should be\n             erected and the arch demolished progressively. The design of the centering should make\n              appropriate allowance for impact.\n              3)    Where  deliberate collapse  is  feasible the crown may be broken working\n              progressively from the edges to the center.\n              4)     In multi-span arches, before individual spans are removed, lateral restraint should\n           be provided at the springing level. Demolition may be proceeded as for a single span care\n             being taken to demolish the spandrels down to the springing line as the work proceeds.\n\n             3.11.3 Reinforced concrete\n\n              a)  Before commencing demolition, the condition and position of reinforcement and\n                    possibility of lack of  its continuity should be ascertained. Demolition should be\n             commenced by removing partitions, non-load bearing cladding, etc. and similar non-\n                   structural elements.\n              b) Where hand demolition methods are used, the following procedures should be used:\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. ### Jdba3f2606eeb9cce

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4A#Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 4A: Specifications for Demolition/Dismantling Works|Vol 2 Part 4A]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 31 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4a_demolition/demolition_clauses.json#/source_page_context/8`)

>   "text": "178\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n              b)   Cantilevers – A  cantilever  type  of  construction depends on  the  balancing\n            superimposed structure for its stability. Canopies, cornices, staircases, balconies should\n           be demolished or supported before the balancing load is removed.\n               c)  Heavy floor beams – Heavy bulks of timber should be supported before cutting at\n             the extremities and should then be lowered to a safe working place.\n\n             3.12  Removal of materials\n\n            3.12.1  General.     Removal of dismantled materials should be done carefully; they\n         may be thrown / lowered to the ground. The materials shall preferably be dumped inside\n            the building. Normally such materials shall be lowered to the ground or to the top of the\n            sidewalk shed where provided by means of ropes or suitable tackles.\n            3.12.2  Through chutes\n\n               a.   Wooden or metal shall be provided for removal of materials.  The chutes shall\n              preferably be provided at the center of the building for efficient disposal of debris.\n\n                   b.  Chutes if provided at an angle of more than 45 degree from the horizontal shall\n                 be entirely enclosed on all sides, except for opening at or about the floor level for\n                     receiving materials.\n                    c.  Opening for chutes shall not exceed 1.20 m in height measured along the wall of\n                    the chute and in all storeys below the top floor such opening shall be kept closed\n                when not in use.\n                   d. To prevent the descending material attaining a dangerous speed, the chute shall\n                    not extend in an unbroken line for more than two storeys. A gate or step shall be\n                    provided with suitable means of closing at the bottom of each chute to stop the\n                     flow of materials.\n                   e.  Chutes at an angle less than 45 degree to the horizontal may be left open on the\n                   upper side provided that at the point where such chute discharges into the chute\n                    steeper than 45 degree to the horizontal, the top of the steeper chute shall be\n                  boarded over to prevent the escape of materials.\n                            f.  Any opening into which workmen dump debris at the top of the chute shall be\n                  guarded by a substantial guard rail extending at least 1 m above the level of the\n                        floor or other surface on which men stand to dump the materials into the chute.\n                   g. A toe board or bumper not less than 50 mm thick and 150 mm high shall be\n                    provided at each chute opening, if the required material is dumped from the wheel\n                    barrows. Any space between the chute and the edge of the opening in the floor\n                    through which it passes shall be solidly planked over.\n\n             3.12.3 Through openings\n\n                  a)  Debris may also be dropped through holes in the floor without the use of chutes.\n                       In such a case the total area of the hole cut in the intermediate floor, one which\n                         lies between floor that is being demolished and the storage floor shall not exceed\n                 25 per cent of such floor area.  It shall be ensured that the storage floor is of\n                  adequate strength to withstand the impact of the falling material.\n                  b) Openings in all floors below the floor from which materials are being removed,\n                       shall be protected by standard railings and toe boards (see IS 4912: 1978) or\n                     preferably planked over if the holes are not being used for dumping materials.\n                   c)  All intermediate floor openings for passage of materials shall be completely closed\n                     with barricades or guard rails not less than 1 m high and at a distance of not less\n                   than 1 m from the edge of the general opening. No barricades or guard rails shall\n                 be removed until the storey immediately above has been demolished down to the\n                        floor line and all debris cleared from the floor.\n\n\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 28 of 37",

>       "text": "3.12.1 General. \nRemoval of dismantled materials should be done carefully; they \nmay be thrown / lowered to the ground. The materials shall preferably be dumped inside \nthe building. >     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         108.00032043457031,
>         251.28289794921875,
>         539.2277221679688,
>         274.2383728027344
>       ],
>       "block_number": 6,
>       "text": "a. \nWooden or metal shall be provided for removal of materials.  The chutes shall \npreferably be provided at the center of the building for efficient disposal of debris. \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         126.00052642822266,
>         276.60284423828125,
>         539.2274780273438,

>         301.80279541015625,
>         539.2273559570312,
>         337.4782409667969
>       ],
>       "block_number": 8,
>       "text": "be entirely enclosed on all sides, except for opening at or about the floor level for \nreceiving materials. \nc. Opening for chutes shall not exceed 1.20 m in height measured along the wall of \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         125.9999008178711,
>         339.8427429199219,
>         539.2274780273438,
>         375.3982238769531
>       ],
>       "block_number": 9,
>       "text": "the chute and in all storeys below the top floor such opening shall be kept closed \nwhen not in use. \nd. To prevent the descending material attaining a dangerous speed, the chute shall \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         126.00016021728516,
>         377.7627258300781,
>         539.2273559570312,
>         426.0382385253906
>       ],
>       "block_number": 10,
>       "text": "not extend in an unbroken line for more than two storeys. A gate or step shall be \nprovided with suitable means of closing at the bottom of each chute to stop the \nflow of materials. \ne. Chutes at an angle less than 45 degree to the horizontal may be left open on the \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [

>         428.2827453613281,

Any opening into which workmen dump debris at the top of the chute shall be \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         125.99942779541016,
>         478.9227294921875,
>         539.2266235351562,

>       ],

>       "text": "guarded by a substantial guard rail extending at least 1 m above the level of the \nfloor or other surface on which men stand to dump the materials into the chute. \ng. A toe board or bumper not less than 50 mm thick and 150 mm high shall be \n"

>       "text": "provided at each chute opening, if the required material is dumped from the wheel \nbarrows. Any space between the chute and the edge of the opening in the floor \nthrough which it passes shall be solidly planked over. \n \n"

It shall be ensured that the storage floor is of \nadequate strength to withstand the impact of the falling material. \nb) Openings in all floors below the floor from which materials are being removed, \n"

>       "text": "shall be protected by standard railings and toe boards (see IS 4912: 1978) or \npreferably planked over if the holes are not being used for dumping materials. \nc) All intermediate floor openings for passage of materials shall be completely closed \n"
>     },
>     {

### J788981bc61b5b76d

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4A#Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 4A: Specifications for Demolition/Dismantling Works|Vol 2 Part 4A]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 30 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4a_demolition/demolition_clauses.json#/source_page_context/7`)

>   "text": "177\n BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                       Technical Specifications\n\n\n\n           1) Beams – For beams supporting rope should be attached to the beam. Then the\n              concrete should be removed from both ends by pneumatic drill or cutting tools\n            and the reinforcement exposed. The reinforcement should then be cut in which a\n           way as to allow the beam to be lowered under control to the floor.\n           2) Columns – For columns reinforcement should be exposed at the base after\n               restraining wire guy ropes have been placed around the member at the top. The\n              reinforcement should then be cut in such a way as to allow the column be pulled\n           down to the floor under control.\n           3) Walls – Reinforced concrete walls should be cut into strips and demolished as for\n             columns.\n           4) Suspended floors and roofs – where ribbed construction is used, the principle\n                of design and method of construction should be ascertained before demolition.\n            Care should be taken not to cut the ribs inadvertently.\n\n       3.11.4 Pre-cast reinforced concrete\n\n       a) Pre-cast reinforced concrete units in a structure are normally held in position by the\n           strength of the joints in-situ or on supporting walls, etc. As such before starting on\n           demolition the joint structures or the supporting mechanisms shall be studied and\n          understood.\n       b) In devising the following demolition sequences, due precaution shall be taken to avoid\n           toppling over of the prefabricated units or any other part of the structure and wherever\n          necessary temporary supports shall be provided.\n\n       3.11.5 Pre-stressed concrete.     Before  commencing  of  the  demolition  work\n        involving such structures advice of an expert engineer should be obtained.\n\n       3.11.6 Steel\n\n       a)    No beams shall be cut until precautions have been taking to prevent  it from\n       swinging freely and possibly striking any worker or equipment or any part of the structure\n       being demolished.\n       b)      All structural steel members shall be lowered from the building and shall not be\n       allowed to drop.\n        c)    Tag lines shall be used on  all materials being lowered or hoisted up and a\n       standard signal system shall be used and workmen instructed on the signals. No person\n        shall be permitted to ride the load line.\n       d)    When a derrick or hoisting equipment is used care shall be taken to see that the\n        floor on which it is supported shall be strong enough for the loading.  If necessary heavy\n       planking shall be used to distribute the load to floor beams and girders. Overloading /\n       overturning of the equipment shall be avoided.\n\n       3.11.7 Other elements\n\n       a)     Roof trusses – Roof trusses shall be removed to wall plate level by hand methods.\n        Sufficient purlins and bracing should be retained to ensure stability of the remaining roof\n       trusses while each individual truss is removed. Temporary bracing should be added,\n      where necessary, to minimize instability. The end frame opposite to the end where\n       dismantling is commenced, or a convenient intermediate frame should be independently\n      and securely guyed in both directions before work starts. On no account should the\n      bottom tie of a truss be cut until the principal rafters are prevented from making outward\n      movement.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 27 of 37",

### J02d1919d27928b39

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4A#Clause 3 — Serviceable and Unserviceable Materials|Vol 2 Part 4A Clause 3]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 23 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4a_demolition/demolition_clauses.json#/clauses/2/fragments/0`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 23,
>   "text": "3.  Serviceable and unserviceable materials\n          3.1 Inventory.    Before  dismantling/demolition  operations  are  undertaken  by  the\n              contractor, inventory of all materials, fittings and fixtures (except hidden materials) which\n             are considered useful shall be made and signed by the Employers representative and the\n              contractor, wherever the operations are entrusted to a contractor.\n\n          3.2 Serviceable materials.    Any material which is in the opinion of the Employer’s\n              representative could be reused or otherwise useful will be considered as serviceable. The\n             serviceable/salvageable items (for which ‘owner losing structure totally/partially’ has no\n               interest) will belong to the contractor, for which the contractor shall give credit to BMRCL\n           (Summary Sheet)\n\n          3.3 Unserviceable materials.  Any material declared by the Employer’s representative are\n          not serviceable shall be considered as unserviceable. A register shall be opened at the work\n            site to show day-to-day account of the turnout of salvaged materials. The register shall also\n           indicate whether dismantled materials are properly stacked or wasted. The contractor shall\n        be responsible for the safe custody of all serviceable materials.\n\n          3.4 Hazards in demolition.     Demolition of any structure is, inherently, more hazardous\n         than the construction or erection of the same. From the point of view of safety, the conditions\n          usually encountered while dismantling a structure, whatever  its magnitude, do not lend\n         themselves to the degree of control possible in the construction operations, where more\n          stable conditions are generally obtainable.  It is  all the more imperative; therefore, that\n         adequate attention is paid to planning and execution of demolition work, in its various stages,\n         so as to minimize the risk of accidents and injuries to the personnel engaged in demolition\n          operations. It has therefore become necessary to lay down certain safety procedures, which\n         along with a planned programme could ensure adequate safety, particularly with the\n         involvement  of management, supervisors and workers. The demolition work  shall be\n         preceded in such a way that:\n\n              a)       it causes least damage and nuisance to other parts of the same building, adjoining\n                     building and the residents of the building and the members of the public ; and\n\n              b)       it satisfies all safety requirements to avoid mishaps and accidents."
> }

>       "text": "2.0     ELIGIBLE TENDERERS\n\n\n       2.1.   Tenderer may be a Proprietorship Firm/ Partnership Firm/Private Limited Company/ Public\n              Limited Company. Tenderer shall apply as a Single Entity. Joint Venture/Consortium is\n            not permitted in this tender.\n\n       2.2.   Only those Tenderers who satisfy the condition of ‘Class-I Local Supplier’ as per Clause\n              2.3 of EQC shall be eligible to participate in this Tender.\n\n       2.3.    ‘Class-I Local Supplier’ means a supplier or service provider whose goods, services or works\n              offered for procurement, meets the minimum Local content of 90%.\n\n       2.4.    ‘Local content’ means the amount of value added in India which shall, be the total value of\n              the item procured (excluding net domestic indirect taxes) minus the value of imported content\n                 in the item (including all customs duties) as proportion of the total value, in percent.\n\n       2.5.   The minimum Local Content for this service shall be certified as below;\n\n                (a) The ‘Class-I Local Supplier’ at the time of Bid submission shall provide a Declaration\n                    that the item offered meets the minimum ‘Local Content’ and shall give details of the\n                    location(s) at which the local value addition is made. (Attachment-1 to Letter of Technical\n                    Bid).\n\n                (b) DELETED\n\n       2.6.   Bidder claiming as ‘Class-I Local Supplier is exempted from meeting the stipulated\n             ‘Local content’ in case, if the product is being manufactured in India under a license from a\n               foreign manufacturer, who holds intellectual property rights and where there is a technology\n               collaboration agreement/transfer of technology agreement for indigenous manufacture of a\n             product developed abroad with clear phasing of increase in local content, subject to\n             submission of necessary documents.\n\n       2.7.   Bidder  shall note  that  in case  of ‘Imported Products’, the related services such as\n               transportation, insurance,  installation, commissioning, training and after sales services"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "text": "support like AMC/CMC etc., shall not be claimed as Local value addition. Such services will\n              not be considered as ‘Local Content’.\n\n       2.8.   A committee  with  Internal and  external experts  for Independent  verification  of  self-\n              Declarations by the Bidder may be constituted by BMRCL on random basis and in case of\n              complaints.\n\n       2.9.    In case of false declarations by a Bidder claiming as Class-I Local Supplier, the following\n              actions will be taken;\n\n                (a) The proposal submitted by the Bidder will be rejected.\n\n                (b) The Bidder will be debarred for up to Two years.\n\n       2.10.  Any Bidder from a country which shares a land border with India will be eligible to bid in this\n             Bid only  if the Bidder  is registered with the Competent Authority. Further, any bidder\n               (including from India) having specified Transfer of Technology (ToT) arrangement with an\n                entity from a country which share a land border with India, shall also require to be registered\n              with the same competent authority constituted by Department for Promotion of Industry and\n               Internal Trade (DPIIT), Government of India or the Competent Authority constituted by\n            Government of Karnataka.\n\n                          i.  \"Bidder\" (including the term 'Bidder', 'consultant' or 'service provider' in certain contexts)\n             means any person or firm or company, including any member of a consortium or joint\n                venture (that is an association of several persons, or firms or companies), every artificial\n                    juridical person not falling in any of the descriptions of Bidders stated hereinbefore,\n                  including any agency branch or office controlled by such person, participating in a\n               procurement process.\n\n                          ii.  \"Bidder from a country which shares a land border with India” means:\n\n                    (a) An entity incorporated, established or registered in such a country; or\n\n                    (b) A subsidiary of an entity incorporated, established or registered in such a country; or\n\n                     (c) An  entity  substantially  controlled through  entities  incorporated,  established  or\n                      registered in such a country; or\n\n                    (d) An entity whose beneficial owner is situated in such a country; or\n\n                    (e) An Indian (or other) agent of such an entity; or\n\n                         (f) A natural person who is a citizen of such a country; or\n\n                    (g) A consortium or Joint venture where any member of the consortium or joint venture\n                           falls under any of the above.\n\n                          iii. The beneficial owner for the purpose of (ii) above will be as under:\n\n                    (a) In case of a company or Limited Liability Partnership, the beneficial owner is the\n                      natural person(s), who, whether acting alone or together, or through one or more\n                          juridical person, has a controlling ownership interest or who exercises control through\n                     other means.\n\n                         \"Controlling ownership interest\" means ownership of or entitlement to more than\n                           twenty-five per cent of shares or capital or profits of the company;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "text": "   \"Control” shall include the right to appoint majority of the directors or to control\n                         the management or policy decisions including by virtue of their shareholding or\n                    management rights or shareholders  agreements  or voting agreements;\n                    (b) In case of a partnership firm, the beneficial owner is the natural person(s) who,\n                   whether acting alone or together, or through one or more juridical person, has\n                   ownership of entitlement to more than fifteen percent of capital or profits of the\n                      partnership;\n\n                     (c) In case of an unincorporated association or body of individuals, the beneficial owner\n                           is the natural person(s), who, whether acting alone or together, or through one or\n                 more juridical person, has ownership of or entitlement to more than fifteen percent of\n                     the property or capital or profits of such association or body of individuals;\n\n                    (d) Where no natural person is identified under (a) or (b) or (c) above, the beneficial\n                  owner is the relevant natural person who holds the position of senior managing\n                            official;\n\n                    (e) In case of a trust, the identification  of beneficial  owner(s) shall include identification\n                       of the author of the trust, the trustee, the beneficiaries with fifteen percent or more\n                        interest in the trust and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control\n                    over the trust through a chain of control or ownership.\n\n                         (f) An Agent is a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in\n                     dealings with third person.\n\n                                      i. Successful Bidder shall not be allowed to sub-contract works to any contractor from\n                  a country which shares a land border with India unless such contractor is registered\n                       with the Competent Authority. The definition of “Contractor from a country which\n                     shares a land border with India” shall be as in para (ii) above.\n                                       ii. The registration shall be valid at the time of submission of bids and at the time of\n                    acceptance of bid.\n                                       iii. If the bidder was validly registered at the time of acceptance / placement of order,\n                         registration shall not be relevant consideration during contract execution.\n       2.11.  Bidder  is required  to submit undertaking  for compliance  of the above Clause 2.10\n             (Attachment-1 to Letter of Technical Bid).\n\n       2.12.  The above Clause 2.10 will not apply to Bidders from those countries (even if sharing a land\n             border with India) to which the Government of India has extended lines of credit or in which\n              the Government of India is engaged in development projects. Updated lists of countries to\n             which lines of credit have been extended or in which development projects are undertaken\n             are given in the website of the Ministry of External Affairs.\n\n       2.13.  Tenderers shall not have a conflict of interest that affects the Bidding Process. Any Tenderer\n             found to have a Conflict of Interest shall be disqualified. A Tenderer will be deemed to have\n               Conflict of interest with one or more parties in this Tendering process, if:\n\n                (a) A tenderer submits more than one bid either individually or as a member of a JV for a\n                work will result in disqualification of all its bids for that work.\n\n                (b) The Tenderer has been engaged by the Employer to provide consulting services for the\n                  preparation related to procurement for or implementation of this work.\n\n                 (c) Any association/affiliation (inclusive of parent firms) of the Bidder has been engaged by\n                  the Employer to provide consulting services for the preparation related to procurement"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "text": "for or implementation of this work.\n\n                (d) The Tenderer lends, or temporarily seconds its personnel to Firms or organizations\n                which are engaged in Consulting services for the preparation related to procurement for\n                   or implementation of this work.\n\n       2.14.  DELETED\n\n       2.15.  As on date of submission of Bid, the Bidder (each member, in case of JV) should not be\n             excluded as per the GROUNDS FOR EXCLUSION. The Bidder should submit an\n              undertaking to this effect.\n\n                      (i) GROUNDS FOR EXCLUSION will constitute the following, if the Bidders (in case of JV\n                 applicable to all member(s));\n\n                  (a) are bankrupt, being wound up or ceasing their activities, are having their activities\n                   administered by the courts, have entered into receivership, or are in any analogous\n                      situation arising from any similar procedure; or\n\n                         is under insolvency proceedings at the time of bid submission and until the contract is\n                awarded or adjudged insolvent by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), with\n                 any resolution proceedings pending before the NCLT;\n\n                  (b) have been convicted within the past five years by a court decision, which has the force\n                      of residential jurisdiction in the country where the project is implemented, of fraud or\n                    corruption or any other offence committed during the procurement or performance of a\n                     contract, unless they provide supporting information together with their Statement of\n                       Integrity which shows that this conviction is not relevant in the context of this project;\n\n                   (c) have committed serious professional misconduct within the past five years during the\n                 Procurement or performance of a contract, as evidenced by any means by the\n                  Employer;\n\n                  (d) have not fulfilled their obligations regarding the payment of social security contributions\n                    or taxes in accordance with the legal provisions of the country where they are\n                    established or the Employer ‘s country;\n\n                  (e) have indulged in ‘Corrupt Practice’; “corrupt practice” means the offering, giving,\n                    receiving or soliciting of anything of value to influence the action of a public official in\n                   the procurement process or in contract execution;\n\n                       (f) have indulged in ‘Fraudulent Practice’; “fraudulent practice” means a misrepresentation\n                      of facts in order to influence an evaluation process or the execution of a contract, and\n                    includes misleading or false representation in forms or statements or attachment\n                   submitted and collusive practices among Bidders (prior to or after bid submission)\n                  designed to establish bid prices at artificial, non-competitive levels and to deprive the\n                 Employer of the benefits of free and open competitions;\n\n                  (g) have been considered ineligible due to execution of Bid–Securing Declaration by any\n                    Central Govt./State Govt./PSUs;\n\n                  (h) have been Black  listed/debarred /banned business by any Central Govt./State\n                 Govt./PSUs or Local Authority or World Bank or ADB or JICA or any other International\n                   Financing Institution, or any entity controlled by them;\n\n                         (i) have left/abandoned the awarded works on his own in the last 05 years;"
>     },

> It sets out the responsibilities of the Employer, the Contractor and the Consultant/Engineer, and the general principles and precautions for safe demolition and dismantling work.

### J833a01a77569c205

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part1#Clause 4 — General Principles of Demolition/Dismantling of the Buildings/Structures|Vol 2 Part 1 Clause 4]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 6, 7, 8 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_1_general/general_clauses.json#/clauses/3`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "4",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 6,
>       "text": "4.    General Principles of Demolitions/Dismantling of the Buildings/Structures.\n    The  Contractor  shall  adopt  appropriate  methodology  and  equipment  for  safe\n      demolition/dismantling of the buildings/ Structures. Certain precautions not limited to the\n      following are required to be taken during demolition work:\n\n        (a)   Prior to start demolition operations, the contractor shall conduct an engineering\n            survey and survey report shall be discussed with consultant/Engineer appointed by\n            the employer for consensus and approval of the consultant /Engineer/BMRCL.  In\n            engineering survey a competent person preferably structural engineer should\n             inspect the site to determine the condition of the framing, floors and walls, and\n               possibility of unplanned collapse of any portion of the structure. Any adjacent\n             structure shall also be similarly checked before commencement of demolition.\n\n        (b)   Within a structure to be demolished which has been damaged by  fire, flood,\n             explosion, or other cause, the walls or floor shall be shored or braced.\n\n        (c)  The contractor should ensure that. all electric, gas, water, steam, sewer and other\n             service lines are shut off, capped, or otherwise controlled (at his own cost), outside\n            the building line before starting the demolition work. If any notification is to be issued\n           by BMRCL, BMRCL will issue the notification to the concerned.\n\n        (d)    If  it is necessary to maintain (temporarily) electric power, water or other utilities\n            during demolition, such lines shall be temporarily relocated, as necessary and\n            protected before commencement of demolition work. The contractor shall make his\n         own arrangements for power requirement for his equipment/machinery used for\n             demolition.\n\n        (e)    It shall also be determined if any type of hazardous chemicals, gases, explosives,\n           flammable materials, or similarly dangerous substances have been used in any\n             pipes, tanks, or other equipment on the property. When the presence of any such\n           substances is apparent or suspected, testing and removal shall be performed and\n            the hazard eliminated before demolition is started.\n\n          (f)   Where a hazard exists from fragmentation of glass or any such kind of materials\n           hazards shall be removed.\n\n        (g)  Where a hazard exists to contractor’s employees and the residents falling through\n             wall openings, the opening shall be protected to a height of approximately 105 cm.\n\n        (h)  When debris is dropped through holes in the floor without the use of chutes, the\n           area onto which the material  is dropped  shall be completely enclosed with\n            barricades not less than 100cm high and not less than 180cm back from the\n            projected edge of the opening above. Signs, warning of the hazard of falling\n             materials, shall be posted at each level. Removal shall not be permitted in this lower\n           area until debris handling ceases above."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 7,
>       "text": "(i)    All floor openings, not used as material drops, shall be covered over with material\n                    substantial enough to support the weight of any load which may be imposed. Such\n                   material shall be properly secured to prevent its accidental movement.\n\n                     (j)   Except for the cutting of holes in floors for chutes, holes through which to drop\n                    materials, preparation of storage space, and similar necessary preparatory work,\n                   the demolition of exterior walls and floor construction shall begin at the top of the\n                    structure and proceed downward. Each story of exterior wall and floor construction\n                     shall be removed and dropped into the storage space before commencing the\n                 removal of exterior walls and floors in the story next below.\n\n                (k)  Employee entrances to multistory structures being demolished shall be completely\n                   protected by sidewalk sheds or canopies, or both, providing protection from the face\n                     of the building for a minimum of 2.4m. All such canopies shall be at least 0.6m wider\n                  than the building entrances or openings (0.3m wider on each side thereof), and shall\n                be capable of sustaining a load of 750kg per square meter.\n\n                     (l)   The contractor shall take sufficient care to erect safety sign boards and sufficient\n                     to manage traffic flow during demolition should be ensured.  If required, local traffic\n                    police to be informed prior to commencement of demolition.\n\n            (m)  Safety procedure: The demolition contractor shall:\n\n                                (i)   Comply with all applicable safety regulations.\n                                  (ii)  Take care for the safety of all persons entitled to be on site. Provide Personal\n                           Protective Equipment to all workers involved. PPEs shall include Helmets,\n                         Safety Shoes, Safety belts, Goggles, Hand Gloves, Safety Jackets and\n                          other equipment required for safety of work force.\n                                    (iii)  Use reasonable efforts to keep the site and works clear of unnecessary\n                           obstructions so as to avoid dangers to persons.\n                           (iv)  Provide  fencing,  lighting,  guarding and  watching  of  the works  until\n                         completion of the demolition and safety certification (by the structural\n                         engineer) of remaining portion of the building where partial demolition is\n                           carried out.\n                       (v)    Provide any temporary works including road ways, foot ways, guards and\n                        fences which may be necessary because of the demolition of the building,\n                               for the use and protection of public and of owners and occupiers of adjacent\n                            buildings.\n                           (vi)  The structure to be demolished/dismantled must have barricades, which\n                             shall be of plain MS Sheet of 16 gauge fixed with steel frame, painting, with\n                           synthetic enamel paint of approved color, quality and brand, writing letter\n                     and logo of metro including maintenance of the same, duly cleaning the\n                   same frequently, arrangement for blinker light as per requirement. During\n                          demolition barricades has to be kept continuously. Removal of barricade will\n                          not be permitted till completion of demolition, dismantling of properties.\n\n               (n)  Protection of the Environment: The contractors shall take all reasonable steps to\n                    protect the environment (both on and off the site) and to limit the damage and\n                 nuisance to the people and property resulting from pollution, noise and other result\n                     of the operations. The contractors shall ensure that emissions, surface discharges\n                and effluent from the contractor’s activities shall not exceed the values prescribed\n                by the applicable laws. The dust and noise level during demolition to be maintained\n                    within acceptable norms under the provisions of BMRCL safety manual/applicable\n                  codal standards including regular watering for dust suppression."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 8,
>       "text": "(o)  Security of the site: The contractor shall be responsible for keeping unauthorized\n           person off the site and authorized person shall be limited to the contractor’s\n            personnel and BMRCL personnel and to any other personnel notified to the\n             contractor by the BMRCL.\n\n        (p)  Contractor’s operations on site: The contractor’s shall confine his operations to\n            the site and to any additional areas which may be obtained by the contractor, agreed\n           by the BMRCL as working area. The contractor shall take all necessary precautions\n              to keep contractor’s equipment and contractor’s personnel within the site.\n\n        (q)  Labour laws: The Contractor shall comply with all the relevant labor laws applicable\n              to the contractor’s personnel, including laws relating to their employment, health,\n              safety, welfare, immigration and emigration and shall allow them all their legal rights.\n          The Contractor shall require his employees to obey all applicable laws, including\n            those concerning safety at work.\n\n          (r)   Health and Safety:  The Contractor  shall  at  all times take  all reasonable\n            precautions to maintain the health and safety of the Contractor’s Personnel.  In\n             collaboration with local health authorities, the Contractor shall ensure that medical\n                staff, first aid facilities, sick bay and ambulance service are available at all times at\n            the site and any accommodation for Contractor’s and Employer’s Personnel and\n              that suitable arrangements are made for  all necessary Welfare and hygiene\n            requirements and for the prevention of epidemics.\n\n          The Contractor shall appoint an accident prevention officer at the site, responsible\n               for maintaining safety and protection against accidents.  This person shall be\n              qualified for this responsibility and shall have the authority to issue instructions and\n            take protective measures to prevent accidents. Throughout the execution of the\n            works, the Contractor shall provide whatever is required by this person to exercise\n               this responsibility and authority.\n\n          The Contractor shall send, to the BMRCL details of any accident as soon as\n             practicable after its occurrence. The Contractor shall maintain records and make\n             reports concerning health, safety and welfare of persons and damage to property\n           as the Engineer may reasonably require."
>     }
>   ],

>       "text": "1.    General Requirements\n\n           (a) Contract Package – P1: “Partial and Full Demolition/Dismantling of Buildings/Structures\n               identified from JP Nagar 4th Phase Station to Mysore Road Station (from Ch: (-) 0.330\n        Km to Ch: 10.550 Km) in Corridor-1of Bangalore Metro Rail Project Phase-3.”\n\n          To  commence  the   civil   construction  works  and   float  the    civil   tenders,\n              demolition/dismantling of the buildings and structures identified for the viaduct, double-\n            decker structure, stations, loops, and ramps shall be undertaken.\n\n             This package includes the demolition/dismantling of various types of commercial and\n               residential buildings ranging from Basements, Ground Floor (G+0) to Ground +4 (G+4),\n            as well as sheds. The scope of work includes demolition of the identified structures,\n             salvage of specified items and materials, and removal and disposal of the resulting debris,\n              walls with all leads and lifts, etc. The debris shall be disposed of at BBMP/GBA identified\n         C&D waste management facility.\n\n           The identified buildings and structures have been classified into the following categories:\n\n              1.  Partial demolition/dismantling of all types of structures of varying heights, consisting of\n              basements, ground floor and/or one or more upper floors (RCC framed structures,\n                load-bearing structures with RCC roofs, and other structures such as AC roof\n                  structures, etc.), by mechanical and manual methods, comprising cement concrete,\n               stone masonry,  brickwork, steelwork, woodwork,  etc.,  with a  total quantity as\n              mentioned in the BoQ.\n\n\n              2.  Full demolition/dismantling of all types of structures of varying heights, consisting of\n              basement level, ground floor and/or one or more upper floors (RCC framed structures,\n                load-bearing structures with RCC roofs, and other structures such as AC roof\n                  structures,  etc.), by mechanical and manual methods, with a  total quantity as\n              mentioned in the BoQ.\n\n\n              3.  Demolition/dismantling of compound walls of all shapes and heights by mechanical\n             and manual methods, comprising cement concrete, stone masonry, brickwork,\n                 steelwork, fencing, stone slab walls, chain-link fencing, etc., with a total quantity as\n              mentioned in the BoQ.\n\n\n              4.  Demolition/dismantling of steel structures such as bus stops, median grills, compound\n                 wall grills, signboards, hoardings, etc., with a total quantity as mentioned in the BoQ.\n                Dismantled/released material to be handed over to the concerned authority at the\n                 locations specified by owning authority and removal of resulting debris with all lead\n             and lifts and as directed by the Engineer.\n\n\n           (b) Demolition and dismantling works.\n           The work includes demolition, salvage of identified items and materials, and removal of\n               resulting debris.  Debris shall be removed from the premises daily, unless otherwise\n              directed, to avoid accumulation at the demolition premises.  The demolition shall be\n              carried out after taking necessary strengthening methods for the buildings proposed for\n              demolition and also for neighboring buildings. The contractor shall develop and take\n            necessary strengthening methods for the balance portion of the structure not being\n             dismantled. In the interest of occupational safety and health, the work shall be performed"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 16,
>       "text": "in accordance with relevant IS codes on demolition and other applicable Sections. In the\n        interest of conservation, salvage shall be pursued to the maximum extent possible. The\n      salvaged items and materials shall be disposed of as specified in which the ‘owner losing\n       structure totally/partially’ and the ‘contractor’ has no interest. The work also includes\n       disconnection of power supply with the permission of BESCOM, rewiring and shifting of\n      energy meter along with accessories to the suitable place as per BESCOM’s direction for\n        partially demolished building. For full demolition of buildings, disconnection of power\n       supply, releasing and handing over the electrical energy meter along with accessories as\n       per directions of concerned BESCOM office through govt. licensed electrician.\n\n    (c) Restoration works for safety reasons.\n      The BMRCL has appointed consultant/Engineer who has conducted Building Condition\n      Study (BCS) and suggest sequence and methodology of demolition including remedial\n      measures required to be undertaken prior to demolition and / or during demolition and /\n       or post demolition.\n\n            It is anticipated that, certain structures will be required to be constructed for safety and\n        functional reasons as a result of Building Condition Study. The structures anticipated\n       are front walls, doors, windows, beams and columns etc.\n      Works done as permanent remedial measures (for example –excavation, backfilling,\n     PCC, RCC, brick/RR/CC block masonry, fixing of doors, windows, plastering, painting of\n       face of wall remained after demolition, water supply, sanitation, electrical works including\n       restoration of power supply to the balance building portion through govt. licensed\n        electrician, etc.) shall be paid as per accepted price for the BoQ schedule for KPWD-\n     Common SR 2023-24. The contractor shall carry out these works  after obtaining\n        instructions from Consultant  / Engineer/BMRCL to that effect. The contractor has to\n      execute these items in accordance with KPWD-Common SR 2023-24 and rate in the\n      accepted priced bill of quantities. Measurements will be recorded for only those buildings\n      completed under the supervision of consultant/Engineer appointed for Building Condition\n       Study."

[[OKF_bundle/Financial/vol4_secJ#1.0 — Pricing Document Preamble and Instructions|Financial Section J]], `Vol4DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 6

> - **Read BOQ with the Complete Tender and Contract Documents** (Instruction 1)
> - **Provisional Quantities and Payment for Measured Work** (Instruction 2)
> - **Price Bid Preparation in the Prescribed XLS Sheet** (Instruction 3; ITT 10)
>   - Schedule-A: percentage rate to two decimals; At Par / Excess / Less
>   - Schedule-B: At Par only
>   - Schedule-C: lump-sum salvage credit to BMRCL
> - **Proportionate Recovery and Adjustment of Salvage Credit** (Instruction 4)
> - **Salvage Credit Based on Quoted Price** (Instruction 5)
> - **Taxes and Statutory Levies Included, Except GST** (Instruction 6)
> - **Measurement of Completed Work** (Instruction 7)
> - **Completed-Work Pricing and Included Execution Costs** (Instruction 8)
> - **Included Safety and Protection Costs** (Instruction 9)
> - **Overheads, Profit, Risks and Defect-Remedy Obligations** (Instruction 10)
> - **Accommodation, Insurance, Wages and Approval Costs** (Instruction 11)
> 
> 
> 
> - **Execution Standards and Engineer’s Directions** (Instruction 12)
> - **Incidental Removal Works Without Separate Payment** (Instruction 13)
> - **Temporary Relocation and Protection of Utilities** (Instruction 14)
> - **Temporary Works, Power and Supports at Contractor’s Cost** (Instruction 15)
> - **Permanent Supports and Restoration Payment Provisions** (Instruction 16)
> - **Balcony and Canopy Area at 50%; Chejjas Excluded from Payment** (Instruction 17)
> - **Demolition Depth and Refilling of Low-Level Areas** (Instruction 18)
> - **Removal Within the Line of Cut, Excluding Trees** (Instruction 19)
> - **Total Floor Area as the Sum of Built Areas of All Floors** (Instruction 20)
> - **Building Additions or Deletions and Accepted Percentage Rates** (Instruction 21)

>       "text": "1      DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION\n\n       Definitions    1.1       The following contract terms and expressions as used in the contract defined shall\n                             have the meanings assigned to them, except where the context otherwise requires.\n                           Words indicating persons or parties include corporations and other legal entities\n                                except where the context requires otherwise.\n\n                        1.1.1     Documents\n\n                        1.1.1.1    “Appendix/Attachment”  means  the  completed  pages  in   title  Appendix/\n                                 Attachment, which are appended to and form part of the Tender.\n                        1.1.1.2     “Construction  and/or  Manufacture  Documents”  means   all  drawings,\n                                     calculations, computer software (programs), samples, patterns, models, operation\n                             and maintenance manuals, and other manuals and information of a similar nature,\n                                      to be submitted by the Contractor.\n                        1.1.1.3     “Contract” means the written Contract Agreement, the Letter of Acceptance,\n                               General Conditions of Contract, Special Conditions of Contract, the Employer’s\n                              Requirements& Technical specifications, the Tender, the Notice of Invitation to\n                                Tender, Instructions to Tenderers, the Contractor’s Proposal, the Schedules of\n                         BOQ, Clarifications issued and such further documents which are listed in the Letter\n                                      of Acceptance or Contract Agreement (if completed).\n                        1.1.1.4     “Contract Agreement” means the contract agreement pursuant to acceptance\n                                           letter  referred  to  in Sub-Clause  1.4.   It  shall  also  include  all subsequent\n                                    modifications/  amendments  to  record  the  Contract  as  a  result  of  the\n                               communications or negotiation proceedings between the parties.\n                        1.1.1.5     “Contractor’s Proposal” means the proposal submitted by the Contractor with the\n                                Tender, as modified and accepted by the Employer and included in the Contract.\n                            Such documents may include the Contractor’s preliminary Design.\n                        1.1.1.6    “Design Data” means all specifications, plans, drawings, details, graphs, sketches,\n                                models, levels, setting-out dimensions, calculations duly checked by the Contractor\n                             and other documents relating to the Design of the works prepared or to be prepared\n                              by or on behalf of the Contractor.\n                        1.1.1.7    “Drawings” means the Employer’s Drawings and the Drawings submitted by the\n                                  Contractor and any modification of such drawings as any, from time to time, be\n                                   furnished or for which the Engineer has issued a Notice of No Objection.\n                        1.1.1.8    “Employer’s Requirements” means the description of the scope, standard,\n                                      specifications, drawings, programme of work, indigenisation programme (where\n                                    applicable) as included in the Contract, and any alterations and modifications\n                                    thereto in accordance with the Contract.\n                        1.1.1.9     “Letter of Acceptance” means the letter from the Employer or the Engineer, or a\n                               person nominated by them on their behalf for this purpose, to the Contractor,\n                                conveying acceptance of the Tender, subject to any modifications agreed to\n                             between the parties and includes advance acceptance of the tender.\n                       1.1.1.10    “Safety, Health and Environmental (SHE) Manual” means the Employer’s\n                             manual containing the requirements and conditions to be met during the execution\n                                      of the Works by the Contractor.\n                       1.1.1.11   “Schedules” means the information and data submitted with the Tender, as\n                                  included in the Contract.\n                       1.1.1.12   “Tender or Bid “means the completed offer made by individual, Firm, Company,\n                                   Corporation, Joint Venture or Consortium for the execution of the works.\n                       1.1.1.13    Deleted\n\n                       1.1.1.14    “Special Conditions of Contract” means any special conditions of contract issued\n                              by the Employer prior to submission of the Tender or negotiated and agreed in\n                                      writing by the Employer and the Contractor prior to acceptance of the Tender.\n                       1.1.1.15   “Works Programme” means the programme showing the sequence, method and\n                                    timing of investigations, Design, issue of No Objection Notices, execution (including\n                                     dismantling/demolition/restoration),  manufacture,  delivery  to   site,  erection,\n                                         installation, testing, commissioning of the Works, indigenisation (where applicable)\n                             and related  activities  in the form and content prescribed by the Employer’s\n                              Requirements& Technical specifications, or any
