>       "text": "1.1.2      Persons\n\n                 1.1.2.1     “Party” means the Employer or the Contractor as the context requires.\n                 1.1.2.2     “Contractor” shall mean the person, firm, association of firms, Company or\n                            Corporation, Joint Venture identified as the Contractor and whose tender for the\n                        work has been accepted by the Employer and responsible for carrying out the\n                            construction scope, in accordance with the Contract Documents and unless the\n                           context otherwise so requires shall include his/their executors, administrators,\n                         successors and permitted assignees.\n                 1.1.2.3     “Contractor’s Representative” means the person (if any) named as such in the\n                           Contract or other person appointed from time to time by the Contractor under Sub\n                        Clause 4.3.\n                 1.1.2.4    \"Designated Contractors\" means any of the following whose activities or the\n                        works they are engaged to carry out, affect or are affected by the Works, in any way\n                             or at any time:\n                                  (a) Contractors, design consultants and utility authorities engaged on the Project\n                               from time to time by the Employer;\n                                 (b) Sub-contractors of any  tier of the contractors above; provided that the\n                                      definition shall exclude the Contractor and his sub-contractors of any tier in\n                                     relation to the Works.\n                 1.1.2.5    “Designer” means the Contractor, or part of the group forming the contractor,\n                           person, firm or company or group of companies, or any replacement, carrying out\n                           the Design or part thereof.\n                 1.1.2.6    “Employer” means BANGALORE METRO RAIL CORPORATION LIMITED\n                       (BMRCL), its legal successors and assignees.\n                 1.1.2.7    “Engineer” means Chief Engineer or Addl. Chief Engineer or Deputy Chief\n                         Engineer or General Consultant or any person/party nominated or appointed from\n                           time to time by the Employer to act as the Engineer for the purposes of the Contract\n                       and notified as such in writing to the Contractor.\n                 1.1.2.8    “General Consultant” or “GC” means the firm/JV or consortium of firms appointed\n                        by the Employer as a general consultant to the Employer or any other person\n                          appointed from time to time and notified as such to the Contractor.\n                 1.1.2.9     “Sub-Contractor” means  the  Individual,  Firm, Company,  Corporation,  Joint\n                         Venture or Consortium, having direct contract with the Contractor and to whom any\n                             part of the Work has been sublet by the Contractor, with prior permission of the\n                         Engineer or Employer and shall include his heirs, his executors, administrators,\n                          successors, legal representatives, as the case may be.\n                1.1.2.10   “Partner/member” means partner or member of  joint venture, as the context\n                             requires.\n                1.1.2.11    “Tenderer” or “Bidder” means the person, firm or corporation, Joint Venture\n                            submitting a tender against the notice of invitation of tender and shall include his\n                               heirs, his executors, administrators, successors, legal representatives, as the case\n                    may be. Tenderer shall mean ‘Contractor’ wherever the context so requires and\n                             vice-versa.\n                1.1.3      Dates, Times and Periods\n\n                 1.1.3.1    “Commencement Date  “will be reckoned as the date of signing of Contract\n                        Agreement.\n                 1.1.3.2     “Contract Period” means the period from the Commencement Date to the end of\n                                  final Defects Liability Period.\n                 1.1.3.3    “Day” means a calendar day; “Week” means 7 calendar days; “Month” means\n                         Georgian calendar month and “Year” means 365 calendar days.\n                 1.1.3.4     “Gazetted Holiday” means every holiday which is observed by Bangalore Metro\n                             Rail Corporation Limited as a gazetted holiday.\n                 1.1.3.5    “General Holiday” means Sunday.\n                 1.1.3.6    “Key Date  / Mile Stones” means a date identified as such in the Contract\n                       documents as the same may be extended by the Engineer pursuant to GCC clause\n                              8.4.\n                 1.1.3.7    “Stage” means level of progress of the works identified as such and more\n                               particularly described in the Employer’s Requirements for which a Key Date for the\n                        achievement thereof is stipulated in the Contract.\n                 1.1.3.8    “Time for Completion” means the time for completing the Works physically or a\n                            section or a part thereof (as the case may be), and passing the Tests on Completion\n                             including  Integrated  Testing  and Commissioning, as stated in the Contract and\n                        as applicable for the nature of contract calculated from the Commencement Date."

### J7ef88675279ec260

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol1/secE#Clause 11 — Contract Price and Payment|GCC 11]], `Vol1DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 110 (`parsed_json/vol1/section_e_gcc/gcc_clauses.json#/clauses/10/fragments/0`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 110,
>   "text": "11         Contract Price and Payment\n\n    The              11.1       Contract Price\n     Contract Price\n                                   Contract Price is the sum stated in the Letter of Acceptance, subject to such\n                                     additions or deductions as may be made under the provisions of the Contract. The\n                                    Contractor shall be responsible for and shall pay all taxes, duties, royalties, and\n                                   fees arising from or required under this Contract, except as specifically provided\n                                      herein. The Employer shall reimburse Output GST to the Contractor in accordance\n                                     with the provisions of the Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the rules made\n                                    thereunder.\n                             The Contract Price shall remain firm and shall not be subject to any adjustment\n                              on account of tax-related changes, except for adjustments expressly permitted\n                                 under Sub-Clause 11.1.1\n\n                       11.1.1     Change in Law\n\n\n                             The Contract Price is based on the applicable taxes as on last day of the month\n                                   previous to the month of invitation of this tender. Any subsequent change in these\n                                 laws that becomes effective after this date shall be considered a ‘Change in Law’\n                                          for the purposes of this Clause\n\n\n                                                                     i. Any imposition, abolition, increase, decrease, or change in the rate or scope\n                                            of any tax, duty, levy, or cess (including but not limited to Goods and Services\n                                 Tax (GST)) applicable to the output of the Works/Services under this Contract,\n                                    whether by way  of primary  legislation,  notification,  circular,  or  judicial\n                                   pronouncement, shall result in a corresponding adjustment to the Contract\n                                           Price, limited to the actual variation in tax liability arising from such change,\n                                         calculated on the value of the portion of the Works executed after the effective\n                                      date of such change.\n                                                                       ii. The adjustment contemplated in the preceding paragraph shall not apply to\n                                  any taxes, duties, royalties, or fees arising from or required under this Contract\n                                               in relation to the inputs for the Works. Such input-related levies shall remain\n                                        the sole responsibility of the Contractor and shall not give rise to any change\n                                               in the Contract Price.\n                                                                        iii. Should there be a partial or complete waiver or exemption for any taxes and\n                                           duties, etc. in  full or part thereof during the execution of the project, the\n                                         contractor shall be obliged to follow and obtain exemption / refund of such\n                                         taxes, duties etc., from the concerned Authorities and pass on the benefit so\n                                      obtained to the employer. In case of failure by the contractor to obtain and\n                                         remit the exemption / concession within reasonable time to the employer (to\n                                 be decided by the employer& intimated to the contractor), the same will be\n                                     recovered by the employer from the amounts due to the contractor.\n                                                   iv. The Contractor shall maintain complete records in respect of payments made\n                                  by them for taxes and duties payable to various authorities (except Income\n                                 Tax or Corporate Tax) and advise the Employer the summary of such payment\n                                     every month in a format advised by the Employer during execution of the\n                                           contract.\n                                            v. The detailed records shall however remain open for inspection by the Engineer\n                                            at any time and copies of the records shall be furnished as required by the\n                                      Engineer. The amount payable/recoverable from the contractor will generally\n                                 be calculated based on these records. However, Engineer  at  his sole\n                                            discretion, if not satisfied with the veracity of records or records are incomplete\n                                         or otherwise, may separately determine the amount payable/recoverable from\n                                       the contractor in accordance with the conditions of the contract, which shall be\n                                                  final and binding."

The Advance payment will\n                          be paid against submission of either unconditional and irrevocable e- Bank\n                             Guarantee(s) or Insurance Surety bond in accordance with provision with set out\n                              below.\n                                       (a) e-Bank Guarantees (e-BG): The e- Bank Guarantees shall be from an\n                                       Indian Schedule bank (excluding Cooperative Banks) or from a schedule\n                                     Foreign Bank as defined in Section 2(e) of RBI Act 1934 read with Second\n                                    Schedule. e-Bank Guarantee format is provided in the contract forms. In case of Joint Venture, e-Bank Guarantees can be furnished by\n                                 any member or members of the consortium/JV.\n                                       (b) Insurance Surety Bond: The Insurance Surety Bond shall be issued by\n                                an Insurance Company authorized by the Insurance Regulatory and\n                                 Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and shall be payable in Bengaluru\n                                              in favor of Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL).  It shall\n                                   conform to the prescribed format provided in Contract forms. In case of\n                                          Joint Venture, Insurance Surety Bond can be furnished by any member or\n                              members of the consortium/JV.\n                                         (c) Wherever e-Bank Guarantee or Insurance Surety Bond is to be extended\n                                        or fresh e-Bank Guarantee/Insurance Surety Bond is to be obtained, the\n                                       cost towards getting extension of e-Bank Guarantee/Insurance Surety\n                               Bond or fresh e-Bank Surety Bond and other incidental charges will be in\n                                       the contractor’s account.\n                                       (d) BMRCL is not liable to pay GST on any advances paid to the contractor.\n                                       (e) The Contractor shall issue the receipt voucher for having received the\n                                 advance to the Employer as per the GST Laws.\n\nMobilisation      11.2.1       Interest free Mobilization Advance Payment shall be paid for an amount as stated\nAdvance                          in ‘Contact Data’. The number of instalments  (if more than one) and  their\n                               proportions shall be as stated in the contract Data. If an amount is not stated in\n                                  ‘contract data’ this sub- clause shall not apply."

>   "text": "Lo =The average consumer price index for industrial workers for Bangalore Centre\n\n                                as applicable for the month of submission of the tender as published by Labour\n\n                                 Bureau, Ministry of Labour, GOI.\n\n                                           Li = The average consumer price index for industrial workers for Bangalore Centre\n\n                                    during the ‘month under consideration’ as published by Labour Bureau, Ministry\n\n                                        of Labour, GOI.\n\n                                 PL =cost co-efficient of “Labour” to the total cost.\n\n                                         b. Adjustment for High-Speed Diesel component:\n\n                                    Price adjustment for increase or decrease in the cost of High-Speed Diesel (HSD)\n\n                              components shall be paid in accordance with following formula (Base: 2022-\n\n                                 23=100).\n\n                                VF = R X PF x [(Fi –Fo)/Fo] where\n\n                                VF = Increase  or decrease  in the cost  of work during the month under\n\n                                    consideration due to change in rates for High-Speed Diesel components.\n\n                            Fo = All India average wholesale price index for High-Speed Diesel component as\n\n                                     applicable for the month of submission of the tender as published by Office of the\n\n                              Economic Adviser.\n\n                                        Fi = All India average wholesale price index for High-Speed Diesel component for\n\n                                    the ‘month under consideration’ as published by Office of the Economic Adviser.\n\n                                PF = cost co-efficient of “Fuel and Lubricants” to the total cost.\n\n                                            c. Adjustment on account of Other Materials component:\n\n                                    Price adjustment  for increase  or decrease  in the  cost  of  other  materials\n\n                              components shall be paid in accordance with following formula (Base: 2022-\n\n                                 23=100).\n\n                             VM = R X PM x [(Mi –Mo)/Mo] where\n\n                             VM = Increase  or decrease  in the cost  of work during the month under\n\n                                    consideration due to change in rates for other material components.\n\n                        Mo = The wholesale price index for ‘All Commodities’ as applicable for the month\n\n                                        of submission of the tender as published by Office of the Economic Adviser.\n\n                                Mi = The whole sale price index for ‘All Commodities’ during the month preceding\n\n                                    the ‘month under consideration’ as published by Office of the Economic Adviser.\n\n                             PM =cost co-efficient of “Other Materials” to the total cost.\n\n                                         d. Adjustment on account of Plant, Machinery and spares:\n\n                                    Price adjustment for increase or decrease in the cost of Plant, Machinery and\n\n                                 spares component shall be paid in accordance with following formula (Base: 2022-\n\n                                 23=100).\n\n                               VP = R X PP x [(Pi – Po)/Po] where\n\n                               VP = Increase  or decrease  in the cost  of work during the month under\n\n                                    consideration due to change in rates for Plant, Machinery and spares components.\n\n                           Po = the wholesale price index for Construction Machine/Equipment including\n\n                               Batching Plants as applicable for the month of submission of the tender as\n\n                                   published by Office of the Economic Adviser."

Conciliation  shall\n                       commence when the other party accepts in writing this invitation.  If the invitation\n                                        is not accepted, then Conciliation shall not take place.    If the party initiating\n                                   conciliation does not receive a reply within 30 days from the date on which he\n                           sends the invitation, he may elect to treat this as a rejection of the invitation to\n                                  conciliate and inform the other party accordingly.\n                         The Conciliation shall be undertaken by one Conciliator selected from a panel of\n                                 Conciliators maintained by the Employer. Provided that if none of the\n                          above actions is taken within a 30-day period, the Engineer shall be deemed to\n                          have given consent to the programme submitted.\n\n                         The Contractor shall, within 21 days of receiving notification under sub-paragraphs\n                                    (c) or (d) above, provide further information requested or the programme shall be\n                        deemed to have been rejected. The Engineer shall, within 21 days of receipt of\n                           such further information, either reject the programme or give his consent.\n\n                                  In the event of a programme being rejected, or deemed to have been rejected, the\n                               Contractor shall, within 21 days thereafter, submit a revised programme taking\n                            account of the reasons given for the rejection or incorporating further information\n                             requested by the Engineer, as the case may be.\n\n                         The Contractor, following receipt of consent to the Works Programme, may at any\n                                 time, submit to the Engineer an amended version. In the event that the Engineer\n                               grants an extension  of  time,  instructs an Employer's  Variation, or on the\n                             occurrence of any event or happening or situation, which could materially affect\n                               the progress of the Works, the Contractor shall submit a revised programme to\n                               the Engineer for his consent.\n                                                   If the Engineer feels that there is a significant deviation between the actual or\n                                anticipated progress of the Works and the Works programme, the Engineer may\n                                require the Contractor to submit a revised/modified programme to ensure timely\n                             completion of Whole of Works or a Key Date. The Contractor shall submit such\n                               revised programme within 14 days of the Engineer's instruction or within such\n                               other time as the Engineer will allow in writing.\n                            Unless and until an amended version has the consent of the Engineer, the existing\n                         programme shall remain as the  Plant, and Materials.\n                         The Contractor shall also submit to the Engineer such other reports as may\n                             reasonably be required by him or any relevant At the end of each such co-ordination period,\n                                          the Contractor and the other contractor with whose works the interface\n                                          period refers shall jointly state in writing that their design co-ordination\n                                                   activities are complete and that their respective designs are integrated and\n                                    can be finalised without interference with each other's designs or the\n                                       designs with which their designs have already been integrated. A copy of\n                                                  this joint written statement shall be provided to the Engineer within 7 days\n                                               of the end of the said design co-ordination period. Unless and until copies\n                                               of all relevant and necessary design co-ordination statements have been\n                                        submitted to the Engineer, the Engineer shall be entitled to suspend any\n                                        review or further review of the Contractor's or the other contractor's design\n                                        submissions. Such suspension shall not be grounds for the Contractor to\n                                          claim nor shall be entitled to receive an extension of time or additional\n                                      payments.\n\n                                  c   The Contractor shall share within the Site, staging, storage and unloading\n                                       areas for the use of Designated Contractors,  if any, who are undertaking\n                                                          civil work, fare collection system, supply, testing and commissioning of\n                                            Rolling Stock, escalators,  lifts, signalling and telecommunications and\n                                               traction power installation works, etc. Separate locations shall be provided\n                                                  for each such contractor. The exact size and location of these staging,\n                                         storage and unloading areas, and the commencement date shall be co-\n                                          ordinated and agreed  during  the design  interface  period  with each\n                                      Designated Contractor.\n\n                               d   Any other contract which depends for its execution on the Contract or upon\n                                      which the Contract is dependent for its own execution shall be identified by\n                                          the Engineer as a \"Designated Contract\". The Contractor shall provide\n                                       attendance on Designated Contractors in accordance with the Employer's\n                                     Requirements and as instructed by the Engineer. The identity of the\n                                            contractor  for a Designated Contract may not be known before the\n                                         execution of the Contract but this shall not be a ground for the Contractor\n                                               to object to the subsequent appointment of a Designated Contractor.\n\n ### Jc0b69557db8e02f2

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol1/secE#Clause 4 — The Contractor|GCC 4]], `Vol1DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 79 (`parsed_json/vol1/section_e_gcc/gcc_clauses.json#/clauses/3/fragments/3`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 79,
>   "text": "Guarantees and  4.2.4        Within time period stated  in ‘Contract Data’, Contractor shall submit to the\nWarranties                  Employer:\n\n                                                  (i)  An Undertaking and written Guarantee in the approved formats from a parent\n                              company, the identity of which shall have been submitted in writing to the\n                               Employer prior to acceptance of the Tender and against which the Employer\n                                        shall have raised no objection.\n                                                     (ii) A contractor warranty  in the approved format. The formats  of Parent\n                           Company  Undertaking, Parent Company Guarantee, and  Contractor’s\n                                Warranty are provided in the contract forms.\n                                   In the event  that  the Contractor  shall comprise two  or more members,\n                                corporations acting in partnership, joint venture, consortium or otherwise each\n                            such member or corporation shall submit a parent company Undertaking and\n                             Guarantee.\n\n\n\nContractor’s       4.3      The contractor shall appoint the Contractor's Representative and shall give\nRepresentative               him/her  all authority necessary to act on the Contractor’s behalf under the\n                                Contract, except another replacement of the Contractor’s Representative.\n                         The Contractor’s Representative shall be qualified, experienced and competent in\n                               the main engineering discipline applicable to the works and fluent in English\n                             language.\n\n                             Unless the Contractor's Representative is named in the Contract, the Contractor\n                                     shall, within 14 days of signing the ‘Contract Agreement’, submit to the Engineer\n                                     for consent the name and particulars of the person the Contractor proposes to\n                                appoint. The Contractor shall not revoke the appointment of the Contractor's\n                              Representative  without  the  prior consent  of  the Engineer and  appoint a\n                             replacement (unless the Contractor's Representative is unable to act as a result\n                                  of death, illness, disability or resignation) The Contractor’s Representative so\n                            nominated shall have  full authority to act on behalf of the Contractor. The\n                                Contractor's Representative shall give his whole time to directing the preparation\n                                  of the Construction and/or Manufacture Documents and the execution of the\n                           Works. The Contractor's Representative shall receive (on behalf of the Contractor)\n                                           all notices, instructions, consents, approvals, certificates, determinations and\n                                other  communications  under  the  Contract.  Whenever  the  Contractor's\n                              Representative is to be temporarily absent from the Site during execution of works,\n                          a suitable replacement person shall be appointed, with prior consent of Engineer.\n\n                                 Failure on part of the Contractor to comply with these provisions shall constitute a\n                            breach of Contract leading to action under Sub Clause no. 13.2.\n\n                         The Contractor's Representative may delegate any of his powers, functions and\n                                  authorities to any competent person, and may at any time revoke any such\n                                delegation. Any such delegation or revocation shall be in writing and shall not take\n                                   effect  until the Engineer has given  prior consent thereto. The Employer may request the Tenderer to submit the\n            necessary information or documentation, within a reasonable period, to rectify nonmaterial\n             nonconformities  in  the  Tender  related  to  documentation  requirements. The Financial Bid of such Tenderer shall not be opened on the eProcurement Portal.\n\n  21.4     The decision of the Employer as to which of the Tenders are not substantially responsive\n               shall be final."

> This part contains the key engineering controls and work practices of Section H (Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications) in Volume 2 of BMRCL Tender No. `BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157`, concerning partial and full demolition or dismantling of buildings and structures identified for Bangalore Metro Rail Project Phase 3.

CONTACT WITH LIVE ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT AND OTHER UTILITIES\n\n          Key Engineering Controls and Work Practices\n\n                 Assume that electrical lines are energized until proven otherwise. Lines and other\n                conductors may become reenergized without warning as utilities are evaluated and\n                 restored after a disaster\n                  Inspect the work area for downed conductors and do not go near, drive over, or\n                 otherwise come in contact with them\n                 Downed electrical conductors can energize other objects, including fences, water\n                  pipes, bushes, trees, and telephone/CATV/fiber optic cables\n                 Unless de-energized and visibly grounded, maintain proper distance from overhead\n                    electrical power lines (at least 3.3m) and/or provide insulating barriers\n                 Do not approach any gas leaks;  if a gas leak is detected, secure spark-producing\n                devices  (e.g., engines,  tools,  electronic and communications equipment) and\n               evacuate the area until the leak is secured"

### J39a8772c5c03105d

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part2#Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 2: Key Engineering Controls and Work Practices|Vol 2 Part 2]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 12 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_2_engineering_controls/engineering_controls.json#/topics/9`)

>       "pdf_page": 12,
>       "text": "10.   GENERATOR USE\n\n     Key Engineering Controls and Work Practices\n\n          Never attach a generator directly to the electrical system of a structure unless a\n            qualified electrician has installed a transfer switch for the generator. If the structure’s\n            electrical system is not isolated, it may energize the utility’s wiring system for great\n          distances and create a risk of electrocution for utility workers and others in the area\n          Always plug electrical equipment directly into the generator using the manufacturer’s\n           supplied cords or grounded (3-pronged) extension cords that are rated for the total\n           anticipated load\n          Do not overload a generator; it can overheat and create a fire hazard\n          Ground and bond generators according to the manufacturer’s recommendations;\n          ensure that any manufacturer-required connections are secure before using the\n          generator\n          Keep the generator dry; protect with a canopy if needed; do not use it in wet or rainy\n           conditions\n          Carbon monoxide (CO) is a poisonous, colorless, and odorless gas that is produced\n         by the incomplete burning of the generator’s fuel. CO is harmful when breathed\n         because it displaces oxygen in the blood and deprives the heart, brain, and other vital\n          organs of oxygen\n          Never use a generator indoors or  in enclosed spaces such as garages and\n         basements; opening windows and doors may not prevent CO from building up in\n          those spaces. Do not use a generator outdoors near doors, windows, and vents that\n          could allow CO to enter\n          Ensure that a generator has 1 to 1.2 m of clear space on all sides and above it to\n          ensure adequate ventilation and cooling. Before refueling, shut down the generator\n         and allow it to cool\n\n       Additional Personal Protective Equipment\n\n       Hearing protection for Noise hazard."
>     }

>       "text": "11.    SILICA, MOLD, NUISANCE DUST, DRIED MUD, OR SILT\n\n     Key Engineering Controls and Work Practices\n\n          Stay upwind of or away from dust-generating activities, and in particular those\n           involving crystalline silica-containing materials like concrete, brick, tile, drywall,\n           mortar, sand, or stone. When inhaled, the fine crystalline silica particles contained in\n           the dust can become lodged deep in the lung, which can lead to silicosis and other\n           respiratory illnesses\n          Use water spray or mist to suppress dust generation, especially during operations\n            that may create a lot of dust, such as cutting or sawing silica-containing materials,\n           jack hammering, impact drilling, using heavy equipment, and demolishing structures\n          Avoid using compressed air for cleaning surfaces\n           Limit contact or disturbance of surfaces containing substantial visible mold growth\n\n       Additional Personal Protective Equipment\n\n           At a minimum, use respirators with filters for work with crystalline silica-containing\n           materials (e.g., concrete, brick, tile, mortar). The use of filters may provide additional\n            protection. Higher levels of respiratory protection may be needed for some operations\n             (e.g., cutting concrete, sandblasting, mixing concrete)\n           Respirators may be used for nuisance dusts (e.g., dried mud, dirt, or silt)"
>     }

WELDING, CUTTING, AND BURNING\n\n          Key Engineering Controls and Work Practices\n\n                 Remove flammable and combustible materials from the area\n                 Do not perform \"hot work\" such as welding, cutting, or burning in areas where\n                flammable, combustible, corrosive, or toxic substances are being used, stored, or\n            may otherwise be present\n                  Maintain a fire watch during all hot work until material has cooled\n                 Ensure fire extinguishers and extinguishing agents are available in the immediate\n                area\n                  Provide natural, exhaust, or forced ventilation to control exposure to the metal fumes\n              and other contaminants being generated (e.g., generator exhaust)\n                 Ensure that pipes and other vessels are purged of hazardous materials\n                  Identify building materials that will be welded, cut, or burned and that may contain\n                  lead, such as painted surfaces and pipes.\n\n             Additional Personal Protective Equipment\n\n                 Gloves and protective clothing for the activity being performed\n                  At a minimum, filtered lenses and face-protection as appropriate for the activity being\n               performed\n                  Respiratory protection based on anticipated exposure to metal fumes, including lead"
>     }

CONFINED SPACES\n\n          Key Engineering Controls and Work Practices\n\n                 Confined spaces have limited means of entry or exit, are large enough to bodily enter,\n              and may contain physical (e.g., mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic energy;\n                engulfment hazards; inwardly converging surfaces) or atmospheric hazards (e.g.,\n               atmospheres that are oxygen-deficient or oxygen-enriched, contain or may contain\n               flammable gas, vapor or mist, airborne combustible dust, toxic substances, or any\n                 other atmosphere that is immediately dangerous to life or health). Examples include\n                storage tanks, process vessels, bins, boilers, vaults, ventilation or exhaust ducts,\n                sewers, tunnels, pipelines, and pits more than 1.2m in depth\n                 Some events might introduce hazards or potential hazards into confined spaces. For\n                example, a space might have a potential to contain a hazardous atmosphere due to\n                 the presence of decomposing organic matter, to the use of hazardous chemicals in\n                 the space, or to the performance of operations in the space, such as welding, cutting,"
>     },

>       "pdf_page": 38,
>       "text": "LETTER OF TECHNICAL BID\n\n                               (To be submitted on Tenderer’s Letterhead)\n\n\n\n  Ref:                                                  Dated……….\n\n  The Managing Director,\n   Third floor, BMTC Complex\n  KH Road, Shanthinagar, Bangalore-560027.\n\n  Dear Sir,\n\n\n  Application for (Name of Work) ---------------------------------------\n\n  Tender Notification No: ------------------------------------------------\n\n\n  We, M/s ------------------ hereby apply as a Tenderer for the above said work. In support of the application, we\n  submit herewith untampered documents as required. We are aware that we will be considered only if we are\n  found to fulfil the eligibility criteria as given in Tender document.\n\n We do hereby solemnly affirm and state the following:\n\n  1.    We understand that in the event of any information furnished by us being found later to be incorrect\n          or any material information having been suppressed, the following action can be taken in addition to\n          the provisions of Clause 4.33 of GCC.\n\n                  I. Our name may be removed from the panel of qualified agencies.\n\n                 II. Any tender submitted by us based on qualification may not be considered.\n\n                III. If any tender from us is accepted and a contract awarded to us based on our qualification,      the\n            tender acceptance may be withdrawn and the contract awarded to us may be cancelled without\n          any financial claim request from our side.\n\n  2.    We declare  that the submission  of  this Tender confirms  that no agent, middleman  or any\n          intermediary has been, or will be engaged to provide any services, or any other item of work related\n           to the award and performance of this Contract. We further confirm and declare that no agency\n         commission or any payment which may be construed as an agency commission has been, or will be,\n          paid and that the tender price does not include any such amount. We acknowledge the right of the\n         Employer, if he finds to the contrary, to declare our Tender to be non-compliant and if the Contract\n         has been awarded to declare the Contract null and void.\n\n  3.     Our Tender shall be valid for a period as described in clause 12 of Instructions to Tenderers (ITT)\n        and it shall remain binding upon us and may be accepted at any time before the expiration of that\n           period.\n\n  4.    We understand that you are not bound to accept the lowest evaluated Tender or any other Tender\n           that you may receive.\n\n  5. >       "text": "1.    MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP:     The whole of the materials used on the work\n               shall be new and of the best quality of their respective kind. ### J97fd952a114e3577

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Clause 6 — Cement Concrete Plain and Reinforced|Vol 2 Part 4B Clause 6]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 35 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4b_restoration/restoration_clauses.json#/technical_specifications/5`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "6",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 35,
>       "text": "6.   CEMENT CONCRETE PLAIN AND REINFORCED:\n\n            A) Cement:  Cement shall comply in every respect with the requirements of the latest\n                 publication of IS: 8112 and unless otherwise specified, ordinary Portland cement shall\n             be used. No other make of cement but that approved by the Engineer will be allowed\n             on works and the source of supply not be changed without approval of the Engineer in\n                   writing. Test certificates to show that the cement used fully complies with the relevant\n                IS specifications shall be submitted to the Engineer and not withstanding this, the\n               Engineer may at their discretion order that the cement brought to site and which they\n            may consider damaged or of doubtful quality for any reasons whatsoever shall be re-\n                tested in an approved testing laboratory and fresh certificate of its soundness shall be\n               produced. Cement ordered for retesting shall not be used for any work pending results\n                  of retest.\n             Cement shall be stored and neatly packed in piles not exceeding 10 bags high in\n               weather proof sheds with raised wooden plank flooring to prevent deterioration by\n             dampness or intrusion of foreign matter. It shall be stored in such a way as to allow\n                the removal and use of cement in chronological order of receipt, i.e. the first received\n               being first used. Cement deteriorated and/or clotted shall not be used on work but shall\n             be removed at once from the site.\n\n           B) Fine Aggregates: Sand shall conform to IS: 383. It shall pass through 1.5 sieve 4.75\n         mm (3/16 B.S) test sieve leaving a residue not more than 5%. It shall be from a natural\n               source or crushed stone screedings.  It shall be washed  if directed to reduce the\n               percentage of deleterious substances to acceptable limits. Sand shall not contain any\n                 trace of salt and sand containing any trace of salt shall be rejected.\n             The fine aggregate for concrete shall be graded within limits as specified in IS: 383\n             and the fineness modules shall range between 2.60 to 3.20. The fine aggregate shall\n               stacked carefully on a clean hard dry surface so that  it will not get mixed up with\n                 deleterious foreign materials. If such a surface is not available a platform of planks or\n                corrugated sheets or brick floor or concrete floor shall be prepared. Sand shall be\n             added in the desired proportion as required for the strength specified, with suitable\n                 correction for bulking.\n\n           C) Coarse Aggregates:    Coarse aggregate shall conform to IS: 383. It shall consist\n                  of crushed or broken stone, 95% of which shall, be retained on 4.75 mm is test sieve.\n                          It shall be obtained from crushed granite, trap, basalt or similar approved stones from\n              approved quarry. Coarse aggregate shall be chemically inert when mixed with cement\n           & shall be angular in shape and free from soft friable thin porous laminated or flaky\n                pieces. It shall be free from dust and other foreign matter. Gravel/shingle of desired\n                grading may be permitted as a substitute in part or full in plain cement concrete if the\n               Engineer are otherwise satisfied about the quality of aggregate.\n\n           D) Water:    Water used for mixing concrete shall be fresh, clean, free from oil, salts,\n                 acids, alkali and shall be in accordance with the clause 4.3 of IS 456 - 1978. The\n                 contractor shall produce test results for approval by the Engineer for the mixing of\n               water proposed to be used on the job, before casting any concrete.\n\n            E) Mixing Of Concrete:    MACHINE  MIXED:  Aggregates  shall  be  accurately\n             measured out in boxes and mixed dry along with required cement, water shall then be\n             added in measured quantity and mixing shall be continued until there is uniform\n                  distribution of the materials and the mass is uniform in color and consistency but in no\n              case shall the mixing be done for less than 2 minutes. Only hopper loading mixer shall\n             be used."
>     }
>   ],

### J5e888e90e75effdc

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Clause 5 — Specifications for Concrete Works|Vol 2 Part 4B Clause 5]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 34 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4b_restoration/restoration_clauses.json#/technical_specifications/4`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "5",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 34,
>       "text": "5.    SPECIFICATIONS FOR CONCRETE WORKS\n\n      Concrete General\n      Wherever grade of concrete like M15, M20 etc. are mentioned, the concrete mix shall be\n       designed by the contractor and approval of Engineer for the same shall be obtained.\n      Weigh batching shall be adopted for producing the concrete. Obtaining of concrete from\n       concrete batch mix plant will be permitted. Contractor shall obtain approval of Engineer\n         for each such batching plant. Proportion of ordinary cement concrete will be expressed\n      as l:3:6, 1:2:4, 1:1.5:3 etc. in the specification. The first figure will be the quantity of\n      cement by volume, the second figure will be dry coarse sand (fine aggregate) by volume\n      and the third figure will be the quantity of course aggregate by volume. Cement shall be\n      measured by weight. The weight is to be derived on the basis that 1 cubic meter of\n      cement will weigh 1440 kgs., or one full bag of 50 kgs. will be assumed to be 35 ltrs.\n      when the sand is wet or moist suitable correction for bulking is to be given while\n        proportioning. Engineer may allow measuring cement by volume.\n       Unless otherwise specified the rates for all RCC will be exclusive or reinforcements.\n       Reinforcements will be paid for separate1y.\n       Unless, otherwise stated, for all RCC work the size of course aggregate will be 20 mm\n      and down size."
>     }

TRANSPORTING:    Concrete shall be conveyed from the place of mixing to the place\n       of final deposit as rapidly as practicable by methods which will prevent segregation or loss\n       of any of the ingredients. Normally not more than 30 minutes shall lapse between\n      mixing and consolidation in position."

> {

>   "fragments": [
>     {

>       "text": "7.  CONSISTENCY:"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 36,
>       "text": "Only sufficient water giving due allowance for the moisture content of aggregate shall be\n      added to the cement and aggregates during mixing to produce a mixture of sufficient\n        workability to enable  it to be well consolidated, to be worked into the corners of the\n       shuttering and around the reinforcements where there is reinforcement to give the\n       specified finish and to have specified strength.\n       Normally for every 50 kg of cement total water including moisture content of aggregate\n       should not be more than 34 liters for 1:3:6 mix 32 liters for 1:2:4 mix. 30 liters for 1:1½:3\n      and 27 liters for 1:1:2.\n            If  difficulty be experienced in placing the concrete of specified mix and approved\n       consistency between and below reinforcement bars, in the bottom of beams and similar\n        situations, the concrete shall have improved workability by increasing the proportion of\n       water and corresponding additional quantity of cement and using aggregates of smaller\n        size than specified as directed by Engineer for which no extra be paid.\n      The consistency shall be determined by making trial mixtures with dried aggregates, or\n      when so instructed by test of laboratory made test cubes under the direction of Engineer.\n       Consistency may be measured by slump test using a standard cone or the Engineer may\n        direct the use of any other means of testing the consistency.\n            If the apparatus used for the slump test is a standard cone when filled. It shall be raised\n         vertically clear of the concrete and the measurement of the slump shall be 300 mm minus\n       the height of the slumped cone of concrete. Care shall be taken to prevent vibration of\n       the samples being tested. The following slumps shall be adopted for different kind of\n       works:\n\n     WITH/WITHOUT VIBRATOR\n        1.   Mass concrete in RCC foundation, footings & retaining walls. 10 mm to 25 mm 80\n       mm\n        2.   Beams, slabs and columns 25 mm to 40 mm 100 mm to 125 mm simply reinforced\n        3.   Thin RCC section or 40 mm to 50 mm 125 mm to 150 mm section with congested\n              steel"
>     }

### J56df1cb7fd233760

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Clause 15 — Reinforcement|Vol 2 Part 4B Clause 15]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 40 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4b_restoration/restoration_clauses.json#/technical_specifications/14`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "15",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 40,
>       "text": "15.   REINFORCEMENT:  Steel reinforcement shall be either mild steel of tested quality high\n        yield strength deformed bars of grade Fe-415 conforming to IS; 1786--1966, Fe-500 or\n      as called for on the drawings Fabric reinforcement where called for shall be of hard drawn\n       mild steel wire mesh conforming to IS: 1566-1967. Bars shall be free from deleterious\n        materials, mill scale, loose rust, oil or paint. The contractor shall submit bar bending\n       schedules for approval of the Engineer prior to commencement of fabrication. These shall\n        indicate the accurate dimensions and bending of bars as called for on the structural\n       drawings. Fabrication shall be accurately done to the dimensions, spacing and ensuring\n      minimum cover as called for on structural drawings. All steel shall be rigidly held in place\n       with 18 gauge annealed steel wire. Cement mortar (1;2) blocks of required shape, M.S.\n       chairs and spacer bars shall be used  in order to ensure accurate positioning  of\n       reinforcement.\n         All reinforcing steel within the limit of a day's polish shall be in place and firmly wired at\n        least one day, prior to the date of pour to permit inspection. The contractor shall also\n       ensure that all conduits and inserts are in position before placing concrete.\n      Hooks where indicated shall be either a complete semi-circular turn with a radius of not\n        less than four and not more than six bar's diameters, plus an extension of at least four\n       bar diameters at the free end, or a 90-degree bend having a radius of not less than 4 bar\n       diameters plus an extension of 12 bar diameters. Unless otherwise shown or specified\n      on the drawings, all lapped by 50 times the diameter of bar. Not more than 33%. (Thirty-\n      Three Percent) of the bars shall have lapped joints at the same location. Only where\n        specifically shown on the drawings, reinforcement shall have welded joints. Rate quoted\n         for steel reinforcement work shall be deemed to include the cost of such welding\n       wherever specified."
>     }

### J75ac9732bdf074f2

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Clause 14 — Concrete Formwork and Centering|Vol 2 Part 4B Clause 14]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 37, 38, 39 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4b_restoration/restoration_clauses.json#/technical_specifications/13`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "14",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 37,
>       "text": "14   CONCRETE FORMWORK AND CENTERING:\n\n      14.1   General:\n           Form work shall be rigidly constructed of 12 mm thick new plastic coated plywood sheets\n                for column, pedestals, beams, walls and fascia and steel or plywood for roof slab,\n             canopies, floors, cover slabs, retaining walls, etc. Shuttering faces in contact with the\n             concrete shall be free from adhering grout, projecting nails, splits or other defects that\n             are likely to mar the concrete surface. The shuttering shall be erected on battens, beams\n           and steel props properly cross-braced so as to make the form work rigid.\n           Form work shall be erected true to line and levels and to the required shapes as called\n                for and shall be able to carry without deformation the full weight of wet concrete and live\n              loads. It shall also withstand the effect of vibration without deflection, bulging, distortion\n              or loosening of its component parts. Details of centering and form work shall be subject\n               to the approval of the Engineer. The completed form work shall also be subject to the\n             approval by the Engineer before placement of reinforcement. Contractor shall be\n              responsible for sufficiency and adequacy of all form work centering and moulds.\n                 All joints shall be sufficiently tight to prevent leakage of grout. Chamfer fillets shall be\n             provided at all corners wherever called for on the drawings or as directed by the Engineer.\n            Openings may .be given with the approval of Engineer at convenient places for washing\n           down all the rubbish. These are to be closed before concreting.\n\n      14.2  Surface Treatment of Shuttering:  The surfaces of shuttering coming into contact with\n             concrete shall be plastic coated of approved make. The shuttering shall be thoroughly\n            cleaned and coated before each use.\n      14.3  Removal of Form Work:     All formwork shall be removed without shock or vibration\n           and shall be eased off carefully in order to allow the structure to take up its load gradually.\n           Forms shall not be disturbed until, concrete had adequately hardened to take up its own\n             weight and superimposed load coming on it and in no circumstance shall forms be struck\n                 until the concrete reaches strength of at least twice the stress to which the concrete may\n             subjected at the time of striking. The side forms shall be so fixed that while removing\n           them the supporting forms & posts are not disturbed.\n      14.4  Surface Finish of Concrete:\n            Only cement mortar rendering of maximum 6 mm thickness may be permitted as finishing\n               to concrete surface. Imperfect surfaces shall not be patched but shall be repaired by\n            removal and replacement of the member as directed by the Engineer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 38,
>       "text": "If centering and shuttering is to be paid for separately, measurement will be taken\n       according to IS 1200. The unit area for payment will be one square meter.\n         All aggregate are to conform strictly to IS specification IS 383. The aggregates will be\n       tested as frequently as directed by the Engineer to see that their specification is the same\n      as adopted in the mix design. They must be stored on clean platform made for the\n       purpose.\n       Concrete shall be weighed batched. The dials of weigh batching unit to be used shall be\n      checked with standard weights periodically. The conversions of weights to volume will be\n       allowed by the Engineer under special circumstances. Despite the design for several\n       mixes the following quantities of cement are the minimum to be used for the different\n       grades of the concrete:-\n      Cement concrete (1:4:8)                 - 3.40 Bags per cum.\n      Cement concrete (1:3:6)                 - 4.40 Bags per cum.\n      Cement concrete (1:2:4)                 - 6.40 Bags per cum.\n      Cement concrete (1:1.5:3)              - 8.00 Bags per cum.\n     RCC             (1:1.5:3)               - 8.00 Bags per cum.\n     RCC              (1:1:2)            -10.80 Bags per cum\n\n14.5.  DEFECTS IN CONCRETE:\n       Immediately on removal of form work, the surface of the concrete shall be examined by\n       the contractor and any bone combs or other imperfections shall be brought to the notice\n        of the Engineer. The acceptability or otherwise of such defective concrete shall be at the\n       sole discretion of the Engineer who may direct the contractor to repair the defective work\n        or ask for demolition and replacement of such defective work at the risk and cost of the\n        contractor."
>     },

### Jac91342faf7280a7

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Clause 8 — Placing and Compacting|Vol 2 Part 4B Clause 8]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 36 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4b_restoration/restoration_clauses.json#/technical_specifications/7`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "8",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 36,
>       "text": "8.    PLACING AND COMPACTING:         Method  of  placing  shall be such as  to\n       preclude segregation and as far as practicable the placing shall be continuous.\n       Special care shall be taken in accordance with IS 456 while laying concrete under\n       extreme weather. Concrete, during the operation of placing shall be thoroughly worked\n       around the reinforcements, embedded fixtures, spaded against corners of the formwork\n      by punning, rodding, or by any other approved means and thoroughly compacted by\n       mechanical vibrators. The number and type of vibrator to be used shall be subject to the\n       approval of the Engineer, and in general immersion type vibrators shall be used."
>     }

>       "text": "11.  CONSTRUCTION JOINTS:   Construction joints in exposed concrete work shall be made\n      only where shown on the drawings or directed by the Engineer and shall be in accordance\n      with the details shown or approved by the Engineer. The procedure given in clause\n      20.1.4.2 of IS; 456-1978 shall be followed for general guidance. All laitance shall be\n     removed from the concrete before  it is allowed to fully harden. The removal shall be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 37,
>       "text": "effected by scrubbing the concrete surface with wire and with bristle brushes and washing\n          down to expose clearly the aggregate. However, care shall be taken to avoid dislodgement\n              of particles of aggregate.\n                       If concrete has been allowed to harden excessively the surface shall be chipped over its\n            whole surface to a depth of at least 10 mm and thereafter thoroughly washed. Before\n              fresh concrete is added on the construction joints, the surface of the old concrete shall\n           be thoroughly wetted and covered with a thin layer of cement mortar 1:2."
>     }

>   "text": "180\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n    PART – B: SPECIFICATIONS FOR REHABILITATION AND RESTORATION WORKS\n\n      Restoration works for safety reasons.\n       1.    The BMRCL may appoint consultant/Engineer to conduct Building Condition Study (BCS)\n          and suggest sequence and methodology of demolition including remedial measures\n             required to be undertaken prior to demolition and/or during demolition and/or post\n             demolition.\n                    It is anticipated that, certain structures will be required to be constructed for safety and\n              functional reasons as a result of Building Condition Study. The structures anticipated are\n               front walls, doors, windows, beams and columns etc.\n          The BMRCL has identified few items which are to be executed in this contract. These\n            items  shall be as per KPWD Common Schedule  of Rates  for the year 2023-24.\n           Measurements will be recorded for only those buildings completed under the supervision\n              of consultant/Engineer appointed for Building Condition Study.\n       2.      All Standards, Technical Specifications and Codes of Practice referred to shall be latest\n             editions including all applicable official amendments and revisions. The contractor shall\n         make available at site all relevant KPWD Specifications and Indian Standard Codes of\n             practice as applicable.\n              In case of discrepancy among Standard codes of practice, Technical Specifications and\n             provisions in Sub clauses in this ‘Employer Requirement, Scope of Work & Technical\n              Specifications’, the order of precedence will be as below:\n\n                               i)  Provision in this ‘Employer Requirement, Scope of Work & Technical\n                    Specifications’\n                                 ii)  Technical Specifications\n                                  iii) KPWD Specifications\n                    v) MORTH Specifications\n                           vii) Standard Codes of Practice\n\n       3.    The utilities which are not to be diverted but require supporting, proper supporting be done\n           so that they are not damaged along their branches. All Precautions shall be taken while\n            handling the utilities. The Contractor shall be liable for any damages in this behalf.\n       4.    Before carrying out the work at site, necessary permissions as required from various local\n            agencies / authorities shall be required to be obtained by the contractor. The Employer\n              shall assist only by way of issue of necessary support letters.\n       5.    The work has to be executed carefully without damaging the existing surface/over\n            ground/underground utilities. The contractor shall execute electrical and plumbing works\n            through Licensed Electrical/Plumbing contractors.\n       6.    The Contractor shall strictly adhere to the working drawings or detail drawings and written\n              instructions of the Engineer.\n\n     TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS\n\n       1.    MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP:     The whole of the materials used on the work\n               shall be new and of the best quality of their respective kind. Other articles, tools, plants\n               shall be the best of the several kinds available in the market and shall be used in the best,\n           most workman like, and most substantial manner to the complete satisfaction of the\n             Engineer.\n           The workmanship is to be the best available and of a high standard. The Contractor shall\n             take all steps immediately to make up deficiency if any noticed by the Engineer. Use must\n           be made of a special tradesman in all aspects of the work and allowances must be made\n                in the rates for the same.\n\n              Contractor shall maintain uniform quality and consistency in workmanship throughout the\n             execution of the work.\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 30 of 37",

>   "text": "181\n BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                       Technical Specifications\n\n\n        Materials shall be of the best approved quality obtainable and they shall comply with the\n       respective Indian Standard Specification.\n        In case of non-availability of materials in metric sizes, the nearest size in FPS units shall\n      be provided with the prior approval of the Engineer for which neither extra will be paid\n       nor shall any rebate be recovered.\n            It shall be obligatory for the Contractor to furnish Certificate, if demanded by the Engineer,\n       from manufacturer or the material supplier that the work has been carried out by using\n         their material and as per their recommendation.\n       Unless otherwise shown on the drawings or mentioned in the schedule of quantities or\n        special specifications the quality of materials, workmanship, dimensions, etc., shall be as\n        specified here in under.\n         All equipment and facilities for carrying out field tests on materials shall be provided\n        without any extra cost.\n\n2.    TESTING OF WORKS AND MATERIALS:              If required by the Engineer/Employer\n       the Contractor shall arrange to test materials, concrete cubes etc. and portions of the\n      work in order to prove their soundness and sufficiency at his own cost. If, after any such\n        test and in the opinion of the Engineer the materials or workmanship is found defective\n       or unsound, the Contractor shall pull down and re-execute the same at his own cost. All\n       materials deemed defective in the opinion of the Engineer shall be removed from the site\n       immediately.\n\n3.    SAMPLES OF MATERIAL: The Contractor shall deposit at the office of the Engineer\n        for their approval samples of the materials proposed to be used in the works, at least 15\n      days before placing the order supply, and the bulk shall be equal in every respect to the\n      approved samples deposited.\n\n4.    STORAGE:   Safe, dry and proper storage shall be provided for all materials, particularly\n        for materials like cement. Adequate storage should be made at least sufficient for 1 month\n       during active construction.\n      The Contractor shall procure necessary guarantees from the manufactures and furnish\n       the same to the Engineer.\n\n5.    SPECIFICATIONS FOR CONCRETE WORKS\n\n      Concrete General\n      Wherever grade of concrete like M15, M20 etc. are mentioned, the concrete mix shall be\n       designed by the contractor and approval of Engineer for the same shall be obtained.\n      Weigh batching shall be adopted for producing the concrete. Obtaining of concrete from\n       concrete batch mix plant will be permitted. Contractor shall obtain approval of Engineer\n         for each such batching plant. Proportion of ordinary cement concrete will be expressed\n      as l:3:6, 1:2:4, 1:1.5:3 etc. in the specification. The first figure will be the quantity of\n      cement by volume, the second figure will be dry coarse sand (fine aggregate) by volume\n      and the third figure will be the quantity of course aggregate by volume. Cement shall be\n      measured by weight. The weight is to be derived on the basis that 1 cubic meter of\n      cement will weigh 1440 kgs., or one full bag of 50 kgs. will be assumed to be 35 ltrs.\n      when the sand is wet or moist suitable correction for bulking is to be given while\n        proportioning. Engineer may allow measuring cement by volume.\n       Unless otherwise specified the rates for all RCC will be exclusive or reinforcements.\n       Reinforcements will be paid for separate1y.\n       Unless, otherwise stated, for all RCC work the size of course aggregate will be 20 mm\n      and down size.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 31 of 37",

>   "text": "184\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n             effected by scrubbing the concrete surface with wire and with bristle brushes and washing\n          down to expose clearly the aggregate. However, care shall be taken to avoid dislodgement\n              of particles of aggregate.\n                       If concrete has been allowed to harden excessively the surface shall be chipped over its\n            whole surface to a depth of at least 10 mm and thereafter thoroughly washed. Before\n              fresh concrete is added on the construction joints, the surface of the old concrete shall\n           be thoroughly wetted and covered with a thin layer of cement mortar 1:2.\n\n      12.   VERTICAL JOINTS: At the end of any day's work or run of concrete, the concrete shall\n           be finished of against temporary shutter stop which shall be vertical and securely fixed.\n             This stop shall be removed as soon as the weather permits.\n\n      13.   STRENGTH OF ORDINARY CONCRETE:       The contractors have to see that\n             proper materials are used and the proportion and the correct water cement ratio just\n                sufficient for the workability are maintained to see that the following minimum strength of\n             concrete are obtained.\n           To verify this, test cubes from the concrete used should be made and tested. The\n             frequency of testing and the acceptability criteria will be according to IS 456 and IS 516.\n\n     14   CONCRETE FORMWORK AND CENTERING:\n\n      14.1   General:\n           Form work shall be rigidly constructed of 12 mm thick new plastic coated plywood sheets\n                for column, pedestals, beams, walls and fascia and steel or plywood for roof slab,\n             canopies, floors, cover slabs, retaining walls, etc. Shuttering faces in contact with the\n             concrete shall be free from adhering grout, projecting nails, splits or other defects that\n             are likely to mar the concrete surface. The shuttering shall be erected on battens, beams\n           and steel props properly cross-braced so as to make the form work rigid.\n           Form work shall be erected true to line and levels and to the required shapes as called\n                for and shall be able to carry without deformation the full weight of wet concrete and live\n              loads. It shall also withstand the effect of vibration without deflection, bulging, distortion\n              or loosening of its component parts. Details of centering and form work shall be subject\n               to the approval of the Engineer. The completed form work shall also be subject to the\n             approval by the Engineer before placement of reinforcement. Contractor shall be\n              responsible for sufficiency and adequacy of all form work centering and moulds.\n                 All joints shall be sufficiently tight to prevent leakage of grout. Chamfer fillets shall be\n             provided at all corners wherever called for on the drawings or as directed by the Engineer.\n            Openings may .be given with the approval of Engineer at convenient places for washing\n           down all the rubbish. These are to be closed before concreting.\n\n      14.2  Surface Treatment of Shuttering:  The surfaces of shuttering coming into contact with\n             concrete shall be plastic coated of approved make. The shuttering shall be thoroughly\n            cleaned and coated before each use.\n      14.3  Removal of Form Work:     All formwork shall be removed without shock or vibration\n           and shall be eased off carefully in order to allow the structure to take up its load gradually.\n           Forms shall not be disturbed until, concrete had adequately hardened to take up its own\n             weight and superimposed load coming on it and in no circumstance shall forms be struck\n                 until the concrete reaches strength of at least twice the stress to which the concrete may\n             subjected at the time of striking. The side forms shall be so fixed that while removing\n           them the supporting forms & posts are not disturbed.\n      14.4  Surface Finish of Concrete:\n            Only cement mortar rendering of maximum 6 mm thickness may be permitted as finishing\n               to concrete surface. Imperfect surfaces shall not be patched but shall be repaired by\n            removal and replacement of the member as directed by the Engineer.\n\n\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 34 of 37",

>   "text": "185\n BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                       Technical Specifications\n\n\n            If centering and shuttering is to be paid for separately, measurement will be taken\n       according to IS 1200. The unit area for payment will be one square meter.\n         All aggregate are to conform strictly to IS specification IS 383. The aggregates will be\n       tested as frequently as directed by the Engineer to see that their specification is the same\n      as adopted in the mix design. They must be stored on clean platform made for the\n       purpose.\n       Concrete shall be weighed batched. The dials of weigh batching unit to be used shall be\n      checked with standard weights periodically. The conversions of weights to volume will be\n       allowed by the Engineer under special circumstances. Despite the design for several\n       mixes the following quantities of cement are the minimum to be used for the different\n       grades of the concrete:-\n      Cement concrete (1:4:8)                 - 3.40 Bags per cum.\n      Cement concrete (1:3:6)                 - 4.40 Bags per cum.\n      Cement concrete (1:2:4)                 - 6.40 Bags per cum.\n      Cement concrete (1:1.5:3)              - 8.00 Bags per cum.\n     RCC             (1:1.5:3)               - 8.00 Bags per cum.\n     RCC              (1:1:2)            -10.80 Bags per cum\n\n14.5.  DEFECTS IN CONCRETE:\n       Immediately on removal of form work, the surface of the concrete shall be examined by\n       the contractor and any bone combs or other imperfections shall be brought to the notice\n        of the Engineer. The acceptability or otherwise of such defective concrete shall be at the\n       sole discretion of the Engineer who may direct the contractor to repair the defective work\n        or ask for demolition and replacement of such defective work at the risk and cost of the\n        contractor.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 35 of 37",

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 4B: Specifications for Rehabilitation and Restoration Works|Vol 2 Part 4B]], `Vol2DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 35 (`parsed_json/vol2/part_4b_restoration/restoration_clauses.json#/source_page_context/2`)
