>       "text": "11.0    SHE Audit\n\n\n11.1     General\n\n\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\n\n\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\n          audit program during the construction work.\n\n\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\n\n\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative based on the pre-\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 23,
>       "text": "11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable the Employer to\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions of Contract, the\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE Plan.\n\n\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines.  The\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\n                      invited to attend.\n\n\n          11.2.4   Timing\n\n\n                The Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\n                       prior to the scheduled date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\n\n\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\n\n\n          11.2.5.1  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\n                        their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\n                    the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\n                    applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\n                  achieved by:\n\n\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\n\n                                  Maximum Possible Score\n\n\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\n                      classified as:\n\n\n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\n                   No.\n\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within 24\n                                                          hours\n\n                 2    < 75%   Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\n                                Necessary               confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable    Contractor rectification within one month\n                                                    and confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n\n          11.2.6   Report\n\n              A copy of each Audit Report will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective actions are agreed upon.\n\n\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\n\n\n          11.3.1   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\n                    representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\n                  submit the report to Employer.\n\n\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents investigation findings and remedy\n\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation and power requirements\n\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission system in place\n\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the current condition of power\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\n\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\n\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 24,
>       "text": "vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\n\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\n\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance system and register.\n\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\n\n             xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\n\n11.4   External SHE Audi\n\n\n11.4.1    External SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors with the prior approval of the Employer.\n\n\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\n\n\n11.4.2.1  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\n         health/medical and welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\n        and control, traffic management, electrical safety, rigging, safety of construction\n        equipment and environment management.\n\n\n11.4.2.2  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\n         standards. Audit report shall also be presented as per the above formats.\n\n\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted on a quarterly basis throughout the\n         currency of the contract.\n\n\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE Audit:\n\n\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\n\n\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\n\n\n                i)     Organization\n\n                  ii)    Communication and Motivation\n\n                  iii)   Time office\n\n             iv)    Inspection\n\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\n\n             vi)   Budget allocation\n\n              vii)   Education and Training\n\n               viii)  Work permit system\n\n\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\n\n\n                i)     Building and Structure\n\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\n\n                  iii)    Material safety\n\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\n\n           v)     Electrical system\n\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\n\n              vii)   Fire prevention and control\n\n               viii)  Housekeeping\n\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery safety\n\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\n\n             xi)   Welfare measures\n\n              xii)   Environmental Management"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 25,
>       "text": "11.4.5   Audit Documents:\n\n\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by\n                  the Audit team.\n\n\n                                 i)   SHE policy\n\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\n\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\n\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\n\n                          vi)   Accident / near miss statistics and analysis\n\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records for all personnel\n\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments\n\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears\n\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\n\n                          xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\n\n                             xii)   Environmental management reports\n\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records including mock drill\n\n\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\n\n\n                                 i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\n                           interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\n\n                                    ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\n                           rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\n\n                                     iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\n                      gaps and weakness.\n\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion.\n\n\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\n\n\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\n                   conducting the audit with a copy to the contractor.\n\n\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\n\n\n                                 i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\n                        concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\n\n                                    ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\n                     and post-audit activities).\n\n                                     iii)    Principal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\n                       observed by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\n                   may warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\n                        achievement.\n\n\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\n\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally be\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\n\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\n                                    injury or business loss."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 26,
>       "text": "11.4.9    Conformity Report & Action by Employer\n\n\n11.4.9.1  The auditor shall inspect the site after 14 days of conducting initial audit for checking\n          the adequacy of implementation of items maintained under priority 1 by the contractor\n        and shall submit a conformity / non-conformity report to the Employer with a copy to the\n          contractor.\n\n\n11.4.9.2  The auditor shall again inspect after 28 days of conducting initial audit for checking the\n        adequacy of implementation of items mentioned under priority 2 by the contractor and\n           shall submit a conformity / non-conformity report to the Employer with a copy to the\n          contractor.\n\n\n11.4.9.3  In case of non-conformity of items mentioned by auditor, the Employer shall take\n         necessary steps including stoppage of work and or imposing any penalty for getting the\n          item implemented.\n\n\n11.4.10   Failure of contractor to conduct External SHE Audit\n\n\n11.4.10.1 If the contractor fails to conduct the external SHE audit in time, the Employer at\n         the cost of contractor shall get it done."
>     }

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 12.0 — SHE Communication|SHE 12.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 26 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/11`)

>       "pdf_page": 26,
>       "text": "12.0    SHE Communication\n\n\n12.1    The contractor shall take every effort to communicate the Safety, Occupational health\n        and Environment management measures through posters campaigns  / billboards  /\n         banners / glow signs being displayed around the work site as part of the effort to rise\n          safety awareness amongst to the work force. Posters should be in Hindi, English and\n          other suitable language deemed appropriate. Posters  / billboards  / banners/ glow\n          signs should be changed at least once in a month to maintain the impact.\n\n\n12.2    The contractor shall also observe important days as listed in General Instruction\n        BMRC/SHE/CEO/008and printing and displaying safety signage and posters as listed\n            in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/009\n\n\n12.3    The list indicated are the minimum requirements of the Employer and the contractor is\n         encouraged  to  further the SHE communication  activities by formulating suitable\n         reward schemes for safety performers and any other activities, which deem fit for the\n         purpose."
>     }

>       "text": "13.0    SHE Submittals to the Employer\n\n\n13.1    The contractor’s SHE management should send the following reports to the Employer\n           periodically:\n\n                i)     Daily Reporting of total no of workmen (as given in Clause 13.2 )\n\n                  ii)    Monthly SHE Report (as given in Clause 13.3 )\n\n                  iii)   SHE Committee Meeting Minutes (as given in Clause 7.9.1)\n\n             iv)  SHE Inspection Reports\n\n           v)   SHE Audit Reports\n\n                a)    Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) report\n\n                b)    External SHE Audit\n\n                 c)     Electrical Safety Audit\n\n             vi)    Air and Noise Quality monitoring report\n\n\n13.2     Daily Reporting of total number of workmen"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 27,
>       "text": "13.2.1   The contractor shall report to the Employer the total number of workmen\n                engaged by all including any subcontractor within 2 hours of starting of any\n                      shift in any day. This reporting shall be the primary duty of the Chief SHE\n               Manager of the contractor and reporting shall be through tele-fax / email. The\n               onus of checking the receipt of the same by the Employer  lies with the\n                   contractor. If the information is not received or received more than 2 hrs after\n                    starting of the shift, penalty shall be levied as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          13.3     Monthly SHE Report\n\n\n          13.3.1   The contractor shall prepare a monthly SHE report consisting of the following and\n                  submit 3 copies within 7th of next month to the Employer as specified in the Project\n             SHE manual.\n\n\n                                 i)    Monthly man-hour details as specified in the Project SHE manual\n\n                                    ii)    Monthly accident / incident details as specified in the Project SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE committee details\n\n                          iv)    Details of SHE training conducted in the month\n\n                      v)   SHE Inspection\n\n                          vi)  SHE internal audit details like electrical audit etc.\n\n                             vii)  SHE Communication activities under taken in the month indicating the number\n                            of posters displayed and balance availability in stock.\n\n                               viii)   Air quality / Noise monitoring details\n\n                          ix)   Toolbox talks details\n\n                      x)   PPE details: Quantity purchased, issued to the workmen and stock available.\n\n                          xi)    Details on IP 44 panel boards, lighting poles, welding and cutting equipments,\n                        Ladders, Hoists, tools & tackles.\n\n                             xii)   Monthly Lux meter study results\n\n                               xiii)  Housekeeping\n\n                        xiv)  Barricade maintenance details\n\n                     xv)  No of critical excavations\n\n                        xvi)  Health & Welfare activities\n\n                          xvii)  Safety walk conducted by Contractors’ Project Manager in the month\n\n                           xviii) SHE Activities Planned for next month"

>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 27,
>       "text": "14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\n\n\n          14.1     Reporting to Employer\n\n\n          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\n                   verbally to the Employer. This will enable the Employer to reach to the scene of\n                  accident  / dangerous occurrences to monitor/assist any rescue work and/or\n                     start conducting the investigation process so that the evidences are not lost.\n\n\n          14.1.2   Reports of all accidents (fatal / injury) and dangerous occurrences shall also be\n                  sent within 24 hours as per format provided in the Employer’s Project SHE\n                 manual.\n\n          14.1.3   No accident   / dangerous occurrences  is exempted from reporting to the\n                 Employer.\n\n\n          14.1.4   Any wilful delay in verbal and written reporting to the Employer shall be\n                  penalised as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          14.2     Reporting to Govt. organisations"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "text": "14.2.1    In addition to the above verbal and written reporting to the Employer, as per Rule 210\n           of BOCWR, notice of any accident to a worker at the building or construction site that:\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\n                 following the accident;\n\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\n\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\n                     the firm/work\n\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\n\n                             iii)    Director General and\n\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\n\n\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\n\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\n\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\n\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\n\n\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\n          treatment.\n\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\n\n\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\n\n\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\n         namely:\n\n\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\n               work;\n\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\n\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\n            means of access including formwork;\n\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\n                 building material;\n\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\n                 building workers are employed;\n\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\n\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\n\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\n\n\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "text": "such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\n\n\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\n\n\n          14.3     Accident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.1   General\n\n\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\n\n\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\n\n\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\n                management system.\n\n\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\n\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\n\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\n                          conditions\n\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\n\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\n\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\n\n\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\n\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\n\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\n\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\n\n\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\n\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\n\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\n\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\n\n\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\n\n\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\n                  about the accident.\n\n\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\n                  completes the investigation."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "text": "14.4.3     All persons summoned by the Employer in connection to witness recording shall obey\n          the instructions without delay. Any wilful suppression of information by any person shall\n        be removed from the site immediately and  / or punishable as per relevant penalty\n          clause."
>     }

>       "text": "          14.3.1   General"

>     {

>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": "          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": "                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": "                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": "          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": "               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": "                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": "          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": "                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": "                management system."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": "          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 36,
>       "text": "          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 37,
>       "text": "                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 38,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 39,
>       "text": "                     a)    take photographs and make sketches"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": "                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "                          conditions"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": "                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": "                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": "          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": "                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": "                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": "                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": "                      caused the accident must be identified."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": "          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": "                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": "                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": ""

>     {

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          192\n                     PART – I: SHE MANAGEMENT\n\n      1.0      General\n\n\n      1.1    Scope\n\n\n      1.1.1   This document defines the principal requirements of the Employer on Safety,\n             Health and Environment (SHE) associated with the contractor / sub-contractor and\n            any other agency to be practiced at construction worksites at all time.\n\n\n      1.2     Definition / languages\n\n\n      1.2.1  The Environmental Quality Management Manual (EQM) forms an essential part of\n              the  overall  Environmental  protection system employed by BMRCL  for  the\n              construction of Bangalore Metro project.\n\n\n      1.3     DEFINITIONS & ABBREVIATIONS\n\n                a)     Environment- The total surroundings of an organism including water, air\n                    and land and other living creatures.\n\n                b)      Environmental Pollutant means any solid, liquid or gaseous substance\n                       present in such concentration as may be or tend to be injurious to\n                      environment.\n\n                 c)      Environmental Pollution means the presence in the environment of any\n                      environmental pollutant.\n\n                d)     Nuisance is annoyance, which results from any construction activity that\n                          affects the material comfort and quality of life of the inhabitants of the\n                      area surrounding the construction site.\n\n                e)      Monitoring is the use of direct or indirect reading field instrumentation to\n                       provide information regarding the levels of pollutants released during\n                         construction.\n\n                       f)      Construction Site is the contract limits for construction. It shall be all the\n                      area within the limits of the work as shown on the Plans. Construction\n                            site  shall  also  include  staging, and  debris  disposal  areas  and\n                         transportation routes to and from these areas.\n                g)     Noise is any unwanted sound disturbance of the environment around\n                       the area of construction operations.\n\n                h)      Decibel is a measure on a logarithmic scale of the magnitude of a\n                          particular quantity (such as sound pressure, sound power) with respect\n                          to a standardized reference quantity.\n\n                           i)    A - weighted Noise levels in Decibels (referenced to 20 micro-\n                      Pascal) as measured with A-weighting network of standard\n                    sound level meter,\n                      abbreviated dB (A).\n\n                         j)      Energy Equivalent Level (Leq) is the level of a steady noise\n                     which has the same energy as the  fluctuating noise level\n                        integrated  over  the  period  of  measurement.  Lmax  is  the\n                 maximum Noise Level during the period of measurement. L10\n                   and L90 is the percentile exceeding levels of sound which is\n                    exceeded 10% and 90% of the time of measurement.\n\n                 k)     Waste  is  unwanted  surplus  substances  arising  from  the\n                         application of all construction operations and any substance or\n                            article which is required to be disposed.\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 4 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n195\n                                    ii)   The use of ‘should’ indicates a guideline that is strongly recommended.\n\n                                     iii)   The use of ’may’ indicates a guideline that is to be considered.\n\n                          iv)   ‘SHE’ means Safety, Health and Environment.\n\n                      v)    Employer means Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRC)\n\n                          vi)    Chief Safety Officer means an officer nominated by BMRC who is overall\n                         responsible for monitoring all SHE functions prescribed in this document.\n\n                             vii)  BOCWA means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996\n\n                               viii)  BOCWR means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of\n                     Employment and Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998\n\n                          ix)  DG means Director General of Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India.\n\n                      x)  BOCWWCA means Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare\n                     Cess Act, 1996\n\n                          xi)  BOCWWCR means Building and Other Construction workers welfare\n\n                    Cess rules 1998\n\n                             xii)   Building and other construction workers’ (Regulation of Employment and\n                         Condition of service) Karnataka rules, 2006.\n\n                               xiii)  Notifications (Central and state) – collection of cess.\n\n\n          1.4      Application of this document\n\n\n          1.4.1     This document applies to all aspects of the contractor’s scope of work, including\n                            all aspects conducted by sub-contractors and all other agencies. There shall be\n                no activity associated to the contract, which is exempted from the purview of this\n                  document.\n\n\n          1.5     Purpose of this document\n\n\n          1.5.1    The objective of these guidelines is to ensure that adequate precautions are\n                   taken  to avoid  accidents, occupational  illness and harmful  effects on  the\n                  environment during construction.\n\n\n          1.5.2     This document:\n\n\n                                 i)    Describes the SHE interfaces between Employer and the Contractor.\n\n                                    ii)    Details the processes by which the contractor shall manage SHE issues\n                          while carrying out the work under the contract.\n\n                                     iii)   Describes by reference, the practices and procedures as given in the\n                BMRC  Project  Safety,  Health & Environment manual  for  best SHE\n                        performance.\n\n\n          1.5.3    These requirements shall be read together with BMRC Project SHE Manual,\n             OHSAS 18001-1999 Occupational Health and Safety Management System\n               and ISO 14001: 2004 Environmental Management Systems.  Definition of\n                key terms used in these requirements related to OHSAS 18001 and ISO\n                14001 standards are found in BMRC’s Project SHE Manual.\n\n\n          2.0      ‘SHE’ Targets and Goals\n\n\n          2.1     The SHE targets, goals and aim for the Works are to achieve:\n\n                                 i)    Zero total recordable injuries.\n\n                                    ii)    Zero reportable environmental incidents\n\n                                     iii)     All personnel inducted in accordance with the approved contractor SHE\n                         plan\n\n                          iv)    Total compliance of conducting inspections and audits as per approved\n                 SHE plan\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 7 of 114",

>       "text": "ii) \nThe use of ‘should’ indicates a guideline that is strongly recommended. \niii) \nThe use of ’may’ indicates a guideline that is to be considered. \niv) \n‘SHE’ means Safety, Health and Environment. \nv) \nEmployer means Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRC) \nvi) \nChief Safety Officer means an officer nominated by BMRC who is overall \nresponsible for monitoring all SHE functions prescribed in this document. \nvii) \nBOCWA means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of \nEmployment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 \nviii) \nBOCWR means Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of \nEmployment and Conditions of Service) Central Rules, 1998  \nix) \nDG means Director General of Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India. \nx) \nBOCWWCA means Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare \nCess Act, 1996   \n"
>     },
>     {

>         132.11868286132812,
>         215.31622314453125,

>         242.1002197265625
>       ],
>       "block_number": 4,
>       "text": "xi)    BOCWWCR means Building and Other Construction workers welfare \n         Cess rules 1998 \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.5595932006836,
>         250.37942504882812,
>         493.328125,
>         488.331787109375

>       "text": "xii) \nBuilding and other construction workers’ (Regulation of Employment and \nCondition of service) Karnataka rules, 2006. \nxiii) Notifications (Central and state) – collection of cess.  \n   \n1.4 \nApplication of this document  \n \n1.4.1 \nThis document applies to all aspects of the contractor’s scope of work, including \nall aspects conducted by sub-contractors and all other agencies. There shall be \nno activity associated to the contract, which is exempted from the purview of this \ndocument. \n \n1.5  \nPurpose of this document \n \n1.5.1  \nThe objective of these guidelines is to ensure that adequate precautions are \ntaken to avoid accidents, occupational illness and harmful effects on the \nenvironment during construction. \n \n1.5.2 \nThis document: \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         121.55994415283203,
>         492.97900390625,
>         123.79376220703125,
>         500.5285339355469
>       ],
>       "block_number": 6,
>       "text": " \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [

>         505.6192932128906,
>         493.32769775390625,
>         682.3716430664062

>       "block_number": 7,
>       "text": "i) \nDescribes the SHE interfaces between Employer and the Contractor. \nii) \nDetails the processes by which the contractor shall manage SHE issues \nwhile carrying out the work under the contract. \niii) \nDescribes by reference, the practices and procedures as given in the \nBMRC Project Safety, Health & Environment manual for best SHE \nperformance. \n \n1.5.3  \nThese requirements shall be read together with BMRC Project SHE Manual, \nOHSAS 18001-1999 Occupational Health and Safety Management System \nand ISO 14001: 2004 Environmental Management Systems.  Definition of \nkey terms used in these requirements related to OHSAS 18001 and ISO \n14001 standards are found in BMRC’s Project SHE Manual. \n \n2.0 \n‘SHE’ Targets and Goals \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         40.55998611450195,
>         687.138916015625,
>         42.79380416870117,
>         694.6884765625

>       "text": "2.1 \nThe SHE targets, goals and aim for the Works are to achieve: \ni) \nZero total recordable injuries. \nii) \nZero reportable environmental incidents  \niii) \nAll personnel inducted in accordance with the approved contractor SHE \nplan \niv) \nTotal compliance of conducting inspections and audits as per approved \nSHE plan \n"
>     },

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 15.0 — Emergency preparedness plan|SHE 15.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 30 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/14`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "15.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "text": "15.0    Emergency preparedness plan\n\n\n15.1    The Contractor shall prepare as required under Rule 36 of BOCWR, an Emergency\n        Response Plan for all work sites as a part of the Contractor SHE Plan. The plan shall\n          integrate the emergency response plans of the Contractor and all other subcontractors.\n        The Emergency Response Plan shall detail the Contractor’s procedures, including\n          detailed communications arrangements, for dealing with  all emergencies that could\n           affect the  Site.   This include where applicable,  injury, sickness, evacuation,  fire,\n         chemical spillage, severe weather and rescue.\n\n\n15.2    The contractor shall ensure that an Emergency Response Plan is prepared to deal with\n         emergencies arising out of:\n\n\n                i)     Fire and explosion\n\n                  ii)    Collapse of lifting appliances and transport equipment\n\n                  iii)    Collapse of building, sheds or structure etc.\n\n             iv)   Gas leakage or spillage of dangerous goods or chemicals\n\n           v)   Bomb threatening, Criminal or Terrorist attack\n\n             vi)   Drowning of workers\n\n              vii)   Landslides getting workers buried floods, Earthquake, storms and other natural\n                 calamities.\n\n15.3     Arrangements shall be made for emergency medical treatment and evacuation of the\n           victim  in the event of an accident or dangerous incident occurring, the chain of\n       command and the responsible persons of the contractor with their telephone numbers\n        and  addresses  for  quick  communication  shall  be  adequately  publicized  and\n         conspicuously displayed in the workplace.\n\n\n15.4     Contractors shall require to tie-up with the hospitals and fire stations located in the\n         neighbourhood for attending to the casualties promptly and emergency vehicle kept on\n         standby duty during the working hours for the purpose.\n\n\n15.5      Contractor shall conduct an onsite emergency mock drill once in every month for all his\n         workers and his subcontractor’s workers.\n\n\n15.6         It shall be the responsibility of the contractor to keep the Local Law & Order Authorities\n         informed and seek  urgent  help, as  the case may  be, so as  to  mitigate  the\n        consequences  of an emergency. Prompt communication  to BMRC, telephonically\n             initially and followed by a written report, shall be made by the contractor."
>     }

>       "text": "16.0     Experts / Agencies for SHE services\n\n\n16.1     Contractors may utilise the services of experts/agencies empanelled under Rule 250 of\n      BOCWR for the purpose of training, internal audit and any other SHE services with\n           prior approval of the Employer.\n\n\n16.2    As an aide to contractors, a list of experts/agencies and the offered service are given in\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/010 for ready reference. In addition to  it  if the\n          contractor would like to use any expert/agencies’ services for any SHE activities the\n       same can also be allowed provided that they are competent and meet to the general\n         requirements of Employer. In every case prior approval of the Employer is mandatory."

>       "block_number": 5,
>       "text": " \n3.3.3.1  \nThe contractor shall ensure that all his employees / workmen are covered under \n‘Workmen Compensation Act’ and shall pay compensation to his workmen as \nand when the eventuality for the same arises. \n \n3.3.4 \nNotwithstanding the above Act/Rules, there is nothing in those to exempt the \ncontractor from the purview of any other Act or Rule in Republic of India for the safety \nof men and materials. \n \n3.3.5 \nIf the requirements stated in this document are less stringent than or in conflict with \nthe country’s applicable legislation, the latter shall apply. \n \n3.4 \nInternational Standards, Guidelines & ISO Certifications \n \n3.4.1 \nThe works should be undertaken in accordance with the applicable international \nguidelines, standards and specifications on SHE and every contract shall aim to \nachieve ISO certifications listed below during the currency of the contract: \n \n"
>     },

>       "bbox": [
>         85.56082153320312,
>         548.339111328125,
>         515.8890380859375,
>         791.571533203125
>       ],
>       "block_number": 6,
>       "text": "OHSAS 18001-1999  : Occupational Health and Safety Management System. \nISO 14001-2004 \n: Environmental Management Systems. \n3.4.2  \nThe process of certification shall start immediately after the award of the work and \ncomplete within reasonable time. Towards this, the contractor shall undertake the \nrequired steps including appointment of ISO consultant for obtaining the certification \non Occupational Health and Safety Management System and Environment \nManagement System.  \n \n3.4.3  \nIn case of failure on the part of the contractor, the Employer at the cost of the \ncontractor shall do the same. \n \n4.0 \nContractor SHE Policy and Plan \n4.1  \nThe contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW Act shall formulate a SHE policy and \nget it approved by DG respectively and display it at conspicuous places at work sites \nin Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood by the majority of construction \nworkers. \n \n4.2  \nWithin 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall \nsubmit a detailed and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall \n"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n199\n\n          5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\n                    affected by the work.\n\n\n          5.2      General philosophy\n\n\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\n                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\n                   excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\n                a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\n                 However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\n                   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\n                   purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\n                      principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\n                     or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\n                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\n\n\n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\n\n\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\n                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\n                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:\n\n\n                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\n                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid the risk);\n\n                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\n                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\n\n                                     iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\n                           protect all people;\n\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by means of personal\n                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\n\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself\n\n\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\n               who have to use the design information.\n\n\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\n                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\n                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\n                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\n                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\n\n\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\n\n\n          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\n                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\n                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 11 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n201\n          6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\n                  which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\n                      payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\n                   outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\n                          traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\n\n\n          6.6      Reporting of SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty shall be levied as indicated in the\n                    penalty clause.\n\n\n          6.7      Inadequate SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\n                   contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\n                      like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\n                  the cost of contractor.\n\n\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\n\n\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\n                  performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\n                    Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\n\n\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\n                    dispatch his duties effectively.\n\n\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements of such facilities / equipments to be provided\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\n\n\n          7.0      Contractor SHE Committee\n\n\n          7.1         All employees should be  able  to  participate  in the making and monitoring  of\n                  arrangements for safety, industrial health and environment at their place of work. The\n                   establishment of site SHE committees in which employees and Contractor and sub-\n                     contractor  management  are  represented  can  increase  the  involvement  and\n                 commitment of employees. The contractor shall ensure the formation and monitor the\n                     functioning of contractor SHE committees.\n\n\n          7.2      Terms of Reference\n\n\n          7.2.1    The Terms of Reference for the committee shall be as follows;\n\n\n                                 i)    To establish company safety policies and practices\n\n                                    ii)   To monitor the adequacy of the contractor’s site SHE plan and ensure  its\n                        implementation\n\n                                     iii)   To review SHE training\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 13 of 114",

### Jde580c9545e2869c

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|SHE vol3_part1]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 16 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/source_page_context/8`)

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          200\n          consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve  all these\n          designs.\n\n\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at\n           sites even for short duration.\n\n\n5.7           If any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\n         depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition\n\n\n6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\n\n\n6.1      Education and Experience\n\n\n6.1.1    The contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value.\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience are given  in\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\n\n\n6.1.2     In order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\n\n\n\n\n\n6.2     Conduct and Competency\n\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\n         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\n\n\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\n          procedural formalities.\n\n\n6.3      Approval from Employer\n\n\n6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\n           of each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\n          format prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work.\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.\n\n\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\n\n\n6.4.1    For  all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\n        main contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract\n        documents executed by the main contractor.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 12 of 114",

>       "text": "consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve all these \ndesigns. \n \n5.6 \nAny non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are \nvery old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can \nbe made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at \nsites even for short duration. \n \n5.7 \nIf any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed \ndepending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition \n \n6.0 \nContractor SHE Organisation \n \n6.1 \nEducation and Experience \n \n6.1.1 \nThe contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General \nInstruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory \nrequirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value. \nThe minimum educational qualification and the work experience are given in \nGeneral Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002 \n \n6.1.2 \nIn order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and \nthe statutory authorities enforcing the labour welfare legislations every \ncontractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and \nexperienced as per clause 6.1.1. \n \n \n \n6.2 \nConduct and Competency \n6. 2.1 \nThe conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by \nthe Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given \nunder penalty clause 56.0 of this document. \n \n6.2.2 \nThe Contractor shall ensure that all personnel are competent to perform the job \nassigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the \ncompetency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE \nperformance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any \nprocedural formalities. \n \n6.3 \nApproval from Employer \n \n6.3.1 \nThe name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition \nof each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the \nformat prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of \nthe work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work. \nIn case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated \nto the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.  \n \n6.4 \nResponsibility of SHE personnel \n \n6.4.1 \nFor all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the \nresponsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main \ncontractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer \nincludes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the \nmain contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed \nby all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract \ndocuments executed by the main contractor. \n \n"
>     },

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          198\n          include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\n         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\n          following but not be restricted to:\n\n\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation and arrangements for SHE\n\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the Contractor’s proposed\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring the\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\n\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line  of  communication  with  the  proposed\n                Contractor's agent;\n\n             iv)   A statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\n                estimating hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\n\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated for this Contract and sufficient information to\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for achieving effective and  efficient\n                health and safety procedures;\n\n             vi)   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\n\n             be provided by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\n\n              vii)   Details of the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\n                including personal protective equipment;\n\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\n                condition and are operated in a safe manner;\n\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's safety plan;\n\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to SHE\n                 related matters, and\n\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure for reporting and investigating\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\n\n\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\n         Employer to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\n           detailed, comprehensive and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\n            site safety, industrial health and environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any and all submissions of supplements\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance with the agreed\n         procedures.\n\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s opinion, insufficient or requires\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works and the safety of all\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\n          plan to the Employer for review.\n\n\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or the Employer’s\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\n           industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\n          contractor  to adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\n          execution of the Work.\n\n\n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\n           practically possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\n           parties each have a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\n\n\n4.7     The details of contents to be covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\n         No.: 3.\n\n\n5.0      Designer’s role\n\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "block_number": 3,
>       "text": "iv) \nTo review the contractor’s monthly SHE report. \nv) \nTo identify probable causes of accident and unsafe practices in building or other \nconstruction work and to suggest remedial measures.  \nvi) \nTo stimulate interest of Employer and building workers in safety by organizing \nsafety week, safety competition, talks and film-shows on safety, preparing \nposters or taking similar other measures as and when required or as necessary.   \nvii) \nTo go round the construction site with a view to check unsafe practices and \ndetect unsafe conditions and to recommend remedial measures for their \nrectifications including first-aid medical and welfare facilities. \nviii) \nCommittee team members should perform a site inspection before every \ncommittee meetings and to monitor SHE inspection reports. \nix) \nTo bring to the notice of the Employer the hazards associated with use, handling \nand maintenance of the equipment used during the course of building and other \nconstruction work  \nx) \nTo suggest measures for improving welfare amenities in the construction site \nand other miscellaneous aspect of safety, health and welfare in building or other \nconstruction work. \nxi) \nTo look into the health hazards associated with handling different types of \nexplosives, chemicals and other construction materials and to suggest remedial \nmeasures including personal protective equipment. \nxii) \nTo review the last safety committee meeting minutes and to take action against \npersons/sub-contractors for non-compliance if any. \n"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          204\n          the  operation. The  training  shall cover the contents as given  in the General\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/004.\n\n\n8.2        All personnel shall be issued a photo identity card of size 85mm x 55mm duly\n        signed by the authorized representative of the contractor before they are\n        engaged for any work as per the format given in the General Instruction\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/005\n\n\n8.3       Contractor shall also issue a personnel SHE handbook in a language known to the\n          workers, which provides information on SHE and emergency procedures that  all\n         personnel working on  contract are required  to know and the need  to  follow.\n          Contractor shall ensure that this  is distributed and  its content introduced to  all\n         personnel working at the site.\n\n\n9.0     SHE Training\n\n\n9.1     The behaviour of people at all levels of the contractor is critical for SHE performance.\n\n\n9.2     The contractor shall organise quality SHE training to engage Managers, supervisors\n        and other personnel in behavioural change and improve safety performance.\n\n\n9.3     The Contractor shall analyse the training requirements for  all the employees and\n             initiate a  training program  to demonstrate  that  all persons employed,  including\n          subcontractors, are suitably qualified, competent and fit. This will include:\n\n\n                i)     Detailed Job  descriptions  for  all personnel,  to include  their  specific SHE\n                  responsibilities\n\n                  ii)    Specification of qualifications, competency and training requirements for  all\n               personnel\n\n                  iii)   Assessment and  recording  of  training needs  for  all  personnel,  including\n                subcontractors’ employees in the workforce, vendor representatives and site\n                   visitors\n\n             iv)   A system for assessing new hirers e.g. previous training\n\n           v)   A means of confirming that the system is effective\n\n             vi)   A matrix and schedule of training requirements, covering general, task–specific\n             and SHE-related training, showing the training frequency and interval between\n                refresher courses\n\n              vii)   Timely, competent delivery of training courses\n\n\n9.4     The contractor  shall arrange behavioural-based  training programmes  for  all the\n          executives to identify, recognise and eliminate unsafe act and unsafe conditions.\n\n\n9.5     The minimum Employer’s requirement of training needs for various categories of\n        employees are given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/006\n\n\n9.6     The contents of SHE training to Managers/Supervisors as given in general instruction\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/007 shall be conducted.\n\n\n9.7     The refresher-training programme to all employees shall be conducted once in\n          six months.\n\n\n9.8      Toolbox talk as given in the Employer’s Project SHE manual shall be conducted\n          to all high-risk workmen everyday.\n\n\n9.9      On-the spot practical  skill development training on height safety including\n         scaffold safety, crane safety, welding safety, electrical safety, traffic safety for\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          206\n           v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\n\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\n\n\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\n\n\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\n         developed procedures.\n\n\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\n          construction site:\n\n\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\n\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\n\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\n\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\n\n\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\n\n\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\n\n         Other inspections include the following:\n\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\n\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\n\n\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\n\n\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection and Routine Inspection will be used\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\n\n\n11.0    SHE Audit\n\n\n11.1     General\n\n\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\n\n\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\n          audit program during the construction work.\n\n\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\n\n\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative based on the pre-\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 18 of 114",
