>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          226\n\n21.6    The contractor shall also maintain a register containing a system of identification\n           of all tools and tackles, its date of purchase, safe working load, competent person\n         date of examination etc.\n\n\n21.7     Test and periodical examination of lifting appliances and gears\n\n\n21.7.1     All  lifting appliances including  all parts and gears  thereof, whether  fixed or\n        movable shall be thoroughly tested and examined by a competent person once at\n           least in every six months or after it has undergone any alterations or repairs liable\n           to affect its strength or stability. Within the validity,  if the lifting appliances are\n           shifted to a new site, re-examination by the same competent person for ensuring\n              its safety shall also be done.\n\n21.7.2    Contractors can  utilise the services of any competent person as defined  in\n          Factories Act, 1948 and approved by Chief Inspector  of Factories with the\n         permission of the Employer.\n\n\n21.7.3     All alarms and signals  like automatic safe load indicators (SLI), boom angle\n           indicators, boom extension indicators, over lift boom alarm, swing alarm, hydraulic\n          safety valves, mechanical radius indicators, load moment indicators etc. shall be\n           periodically examined and maintained always in working condition\n\n\n21.8     Automatic safe load indicators\n\n\n21.8.1   As stipulated in Rule 78 of BOCWKR 2006, no lifting appliances gear or any\n         other material handling appliance is used, if:\n\n                i)     the  Inspector  having  jurisdiction  is  not  satisfied  with  reference  to a\n                   certification of test or examination or to an authenticated record maintain as\n               provided under these rules; and\n\n                  ii)     in the view of such Inspector, the lifting appliance, lifting gear or any other\n                material  handling  appliance  is  not  safe  for use  in  building  or  other\n                construction work; and\n\n                  iii)   no pulley block is used in building or other construction work unless the safe\n               working load and its identification are clearly marked on such block.\n\n\n21.9      Qualification of operator of lifting appliances and of signaller etc\n\n\n21.9.1   The contractor shall not employ any person to drive or operate a lifting machine\n            like crane, hydra etc whether driven by mechanical power or otherwise or to give\n          signals to work as a operator of a rigger or derricks unless he\n\n                i)      is above twenty-one years of age and possesses a valid heavy transport\n                vehicle driving licence as per Motor Vehicle Act and Rules.\n\n                  ii)     is absolutely competent and reliable\n\n                  iii)   possesses the knowledge of the inherent risks involved in the operation of\n                      lifting appliances by undergoing a formal  training  at any  institution  of\n                national importance acceptable to Employer\n\n             iv)     is medically examined periodically as specified in schedule VII of BOCW\n               Rules.\n\n\n21.10    General requirements of appliances\n\n\n21.10.1   Out-of level\n\n\n21.10.1.1 One of the most severe effects of being out-of fit level is that side loads develop in\n          the boom. Because of side loads all mobile cranes lose capacity rapidly as the\n         degree of out-of-level increases and therefore\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n229\n                           xviii) Access to drinking water & toilet shall be ensured to all workmen engaged\n                              for launching process.\n\n                       xix)  Proper access ladders/stairways shall be maintained for safe ascending  /\n                       descending of workmen / engineers.\n\n\n          22.3     Non-adherence to any of the clauses mentioned above shall be viewed\n                   seriously by the Employer and penalty levied as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          23.0     Construction machinery\n\n\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump trucks,  lift trucks and\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding equipments, mobile\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons, 360°\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\n                       etc.\n\n\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\n\n\n          23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\n                       certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\n                   warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\n                 by Employer before induction to any site.\n\n\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination details,\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\n\n\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\n\n\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\n\n\n          23.4     General operating procedures\n\n\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\n                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\n                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\n\n                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\n\n                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\n\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\n                             etc.\n\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\n\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\n                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\n                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\n                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\n                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\n                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\n                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\n                          excavating.\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n227\n          21.10.2  Boom\n\n\n                                 i)    The boom is one of the more critical elements of the crane and must be in\n                           perfect condition at all time. No boom section with a bent lattice member\n                             shall be allowed\n\n                                    ii)     All welds shall be crack and corrosion free\n\n                                     iii)   No member of the boom shall be bent\n\n                          iv)    All telescopic boom shall be free from cracks, rust, flaking or cracked paint,\n                          bulges, greases or varnishes\n\n          21.10.3  The sweep area (work area) of the construction machinery shall be always free\n                  from obstructions.\n\n\n          21.10.4   All hydraulic piping and fittings shall be maintained leak proof.\n\n\n          21.10.5  The operator cab shall posses good and safe:\n\n\n                                 i)     structure, windows and windshield wipers\n\n                                    ii)    Drivers chair and foot rest\n\n                                     iii)    Control handles\n\n                          iv)   Cab instrumentation\n\n                      v)    Telecommunication\n\n                          vi)   Cab out fitting\n\n                             vii)   wind  indicator  with an  adjustable  set  point  shall be  in a  position\n                          representative for the wind on the crane. The indicator shall give continuous\n                          information regarding constant speeds and gusts.\n\n\n         21.11    Mandatory rigging requirements\n\n\n          21.11.1  Rigging shall be done under experienced and qualified rigger only.\n\n\n          21.11.2  The primary requirement in rigging shall be to assess the weight of load\n                  before attempting any lift.\n\n\n          21.11.3   All hooks shall be fitted with Master Rings having certificate of fitness from\n                  the competent person, so that the hooks are subjected to balanced vertical\n                  loading only.\n\n\n          21.11.4  Only four legged slings shall be allowed which includes master link (ring),\n                  intermediate master link (ring)  if necessary, chain  / wire rope sling, sling\n               hook or other terminal fitting.\n\n\n          21.11.5  Hand spliced slings up to 32mm diameter shall not be used at site for any\n                       lifting purpose.\n\n\n          21.11.6  No load shall be slewed over public areas without stopping the pedestrians\n               and road traffic first.\n\n\n          21.11.7  Requirements of outriggers\n\n                              i)     All outriggers shall be fully extended and at all tyres are clear of the ground\n\n                                    ii)   Heavy duty blocking having large bearing area shall be necessary to prevent\n                        sinking of floats\n\n\n          21.11.8   All loads shall have tag-lines attached in order to ensure that the load can be\n                   controlled at all times.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n231\n          26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of the electrical loads and the\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of the contract.\n\n\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to be obtained  /\n                   generated. approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the job.\n\n\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub /\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\n                 source of power supply from diesel generators.\n\n\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty contractors’ under this contract.\n\n\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators are found used\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be  No electrical equipment shall be put into use where its strength and capability may\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to danger.\n\n\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous                 ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\n\n                                     iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\n\n                          iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\n\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools – 115V single phase\n\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          230\n              vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\n               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\n\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\n                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\n           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\n                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\n\n             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\n                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\n\n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\n                with adequate driver protection.\n\n             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\n                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\n\n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\n                condition\n\n\n23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\n\n\n23.6     Penalty\n\n\n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per\n         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition.\n\n\n24.0    Machine and general area guarding\n\n\n24.1    The contractor shall ensure at the construction site all motors, cogwheels, chains and\n            friction gearing,  flywheels,  shafting, dangerous and moving parts  of machinery are\n          securely fenced or legged. The fencing of dangerous part of machinery is not removed\n          while such machinery is in motion or in use.\n\n\n25.0    Manual lifting and carrying of excessive weight\n\n\n25.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  at  his  construction  site  of a  building  or other\n          construction work that no building worker lifts by hand or carries overhead or over\n           his back or shoulders any material, article, tool or appliances exceeding in weight\n         as said below as per Rule 38 of BOCWR, Unless aided by another building worker\n          or device.\n\n                      Person      Maximum weight in\n                                                 kg.\n\n                          Adult man             55\n\n                          Adult                 30\n                  woman\n\n\n25.2    No building worker aided by other building worker shall lift or carry weight higher\n         than or exceeding the sum of total of maximum limits set out for each building\n         worker separately as mentioned in the table above.\n\n\n26.0      Site Electricity\n\n26.1     Competency of Electrical personnel:\n\n26.1.1   The contractor shall employ qualified and competent electrical personnel as\n         specified in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001.\n\n\n26.2     Assessment of power\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 42 of 114",

>       "text": "vii) \nWhen the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe \nattachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place. \nviii) \nWhen operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink \ninto the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be \nmade for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered \nto the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed. \nix) \nThe netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the \nskip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform  \nx) \nIf a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided \nwith adequate driver protection. \nxi) \nWhen two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at \nleast 25m shall be kept between them. \nxii) \nIncase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working \ncondition \n \n23.5 \nAll wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top \nguard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop \nswitch easily accessible by the operator. \n \n23.6 \nPenalty \n \n23.6.1 \nIf any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per \nrelevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition. \n \n24.0 \nMachine and general area guarding \n \n24.1  \nThe contractor shall ensure at the construction site all motors, cogwheels, chains and \nfriction gearing, flywheels, shafting, dangerous and moving parts of machinery are \nsecurely fenced or legged. The fencing of dangerous part of machinery is not removed \nwhile such machinery is in motion or in use. \n \n25.0 \nManual lifting and carrying of excessive weight \n \n25.1 \nThe contractor shall ensure at his construction site of a building or other \nconstruction work that no building worker lifts by hand or carries overhead or over \nhis back or shoulders any material, article, tool or appliances exceeding in weight \nas said below as per Rule 38 of BOCWR, Unless aided by another building worker \nor device. \n"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          228\n21.11.9  No close working to any  live overhead power  line  is permitted without the\n         operation of a strict Permit to Work.\n\n\n21.11.10 Minimum lighting is to be ensured at all lifting operations.\n\n\n21.12    Failure to do any of the above shall attract penalty from the Employer as per\n         relevant clause\n\n\n22.0     Launching Operation\n\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor shall take utmost\n          precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting segments,\n          transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching  of\n         segments, pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\n\n\n22.2    The contractor shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\n          operation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\n          project SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\n           height. As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\n          safety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines\n           shall be adhered throughout the launching operation.\n\n\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall be\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\n\n                  ii)    Provisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\n                  girder.\n\n                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0\n\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment\n                  shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection\n                gloves.\n\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\n\n             vi)   Trucks  with  valid  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\n               approval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\n                transport of segments\n\n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at\n                specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.\n\n               viii)   Drivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant\n               clause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’.\n\n             ix)   The segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges\n             and necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly\n             seen by other road users both in day / night time.\n\n           x)    Every launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time.\n\n             xi)    All the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\n              wherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded.\n\n              xii)   Unloading  of  segments  from  trucks,  lifting  of  segments,  shifting  of\n              segments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved\n               engineer of the contractor.\n\n               xiii)  Auto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. After\n               every auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured.\n\n            xiv)  The vertical deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical\n               stages like with/without loads and after every auto launching.\n\n          xv)  A  register containing  all important operational  details from erection  to\n                dismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to\n              Employer whenever called for.\n\n            xvi)  Test  certificate  for  all  lifting  gears  including  Macalloy  bars  shall be\n               maintained at a location closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be\n                referred during all inspections.\n\n             xvii)  Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 40 of 114",

Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at \nheight.  As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the \nsafety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines \nshall be adhered throughout the launching operation.  \n \ni) \nNecessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall be \nprovided in the launching girder itself. \nii) \nProvisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching \ngirder. \niii) \nThe casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0   \niv) \nThe workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment \nshall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection \ngloves. \nv) \nCasting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of \nthe responsible engineer of the contractor. \nvi) \nTrucks with valid registration, licence, safe worthiness certificate, Employer’s \napproval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for \ntransport of segments \nvii) \nDrivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at \nspecified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.   \nviii) \nDrivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant \nclause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’. \nix) \nThe segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges \nand necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly \nseen by other road users both in day / night time.  \nx) \nEvery launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time. \nxi) \nAll the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers \nwherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded. \nxii) \nUnloading of segments from trucks, lifting of segments, shifting of \nsegments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved \nengineer of the contractor. \nxiii) \nAuto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          232\n26.7      Electrical protection circuits\n\n26.7.1    Precautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\n         danger arising when any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\n         reasonably foreseeable become charged as a result of either the use of a system, or a\n            fault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor shall be regarded as earthed\n        when conductors of sufficient strength and current-carrying capability to discharge\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.\n\n                If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference point, nothing\n         which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\n           continuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\n          suitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.\n\n\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection shall be provided for all circuits, against over load,\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\n\n\n26.7.3   The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\n              all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\n         panels etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\n\n\n26.7.4     All protection devices shall be capable of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\n         equipments and circuits in case of any fault may occur.\n\n\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should be\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\n\n\n26.7.6    Protection against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\n\n\n26.8     Cables:\n\n\n26.8.1   Cables shall be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\n        exposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\n            in accordance with BS 6346.\n\n\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where operating of the equipment\n          subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of these codes BS 6007 /\n       BS 6500 / BS 7375.\n\n\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\n\n\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS 7375. The\n          following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS\n        6346 and BS 6708\n\n\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour or metal\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking\n         tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged by any\n          disturbance of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\n           electrical register.\n\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport and mobile\n         equipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\n\n26.8.7   Cables that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\n         catenary wire on poles or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of\n         suspension. Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.\n\n\n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply for welding\n         process shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\n         monitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 44 of 114",

Tools and Power Tools\n\n\n          28.1     General\n\n\n          28.1.1   The contractor is wholly responsible for the safe condition of tools and equipment\n                 used by his employees and that of his sub-contractors.\n\n\n          28.1.2   Use of short / damaged hand tools shall be avoided and the contractor shall ensure all\n                      his hand tools used at his worksite are safe to work with or stored and shall also train\n                      his employees (including his sub-contractors) for proper use thereby.\n\n\n          28.1.3     All hand tools and >       "text": "Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                              September 2026         Section Page 47 of 114 \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.5589828491211,
>         38.09945297241211,
>         515.8881225585938,
>         542.4517211914062
>       ],
>       "block_number": 3,
>       "text": "a source of glare for the others. Strongly made clamps should be available for \nattaching luminaries to poles and other convenient supports. \n \n27.4 \nLuminaries should be robust, resistant to corrosion and rain proof especially at the \npoint of the cable entry. \n \n27.5 \nThe correct type of lamp for each luminaries should always be used and when lamps \nneed to be replaced if shall be in accordance with the supply voltage.  \n \n27.6 \nLamp holders not fitted with a lamp should be capped off. \n \n27.7 \nThe contractor shall take every effort to illuminate the work site as per the Employer’s \nrequirement illustrated in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/0011. \n \n28.0 \nHand Tools and Power Tools \n \n28.1 \nGeneral \n \n28.1.1 \nThe contractor is wholly responsible for the safe condition of tools and equipment \nused by his employees and that of his sub-contractors. \n \n28.1.2 \nUse of short / damaged hand tools shall be avoided and the contractor shall ensure all \nhis hand tools used at his worksite are safe to work with or stored and shall also train \nhis employees (including his sub-contractors) for proper use thereby. \n \n28.1.3 \nAll hand tools and power tools shall be duly inspected before use for safe operation. \n \n28.1.4 \nAll hand tools and power tools shall have sufficient grip and the design specification \non par with national/international standards on anthropometrics. \n \n28.2 \nHand tools \n \n28.2.1 \nHand tools shall include saws, chisels, axes and hatches, hammers, hand planes, \nscrew drivers, crow bars, nail pullers. \n \n28.2.2 \nThe contractor shall ensure that, \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.5603256225586,
>         547.6192626953125,
>         515.8878173828125,
>         779.931640625
>       ],
>       "block_number": 4,
>       "text": "i) \nFor crosscutting of hardwood, saws with larger teeth points (no. of points per \ninch) shall be preferred to avoid the saw jumping out of the job. \nii) \nMushroom headed chisels shall not be used in the worksite where the \nfragments of the head may cause injury. \niii) \nUnless hatchet has a striking face, it shall be used as a hammer. \niv) \nOnly knives of retractable blades shall be used in the worksite. \nv) \nNo screwdrivers shall be used for scraping, chiselling or punching holes. \nvi) \nA pilot hole shall always be driven before driving a screw. \nvii) \nWherever necessary, usage of proper PPEs shall be used by his employees. \n \n28.3 \nPower tools \n \n28.3.1 \nPower tools include drills, planes, routers, saws, jackhammers, grinders, sprayers, \nchipping hammers, air nozzles and drills. \n \n28.3.2 \nThe contractor shall ensure that \ni) \nElectric tools are properly grounded or / and double insulated. \n"
>     },

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n233\n                  sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in the cable and shall not\n                be used as the protective conductor.\n\n\n          26.8.9   Armoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an  oil\n                      resisting and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of\n                  mechanical damage occurring\n\n\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\n\n\n          26.9.1   The contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\n                  the construction  site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of\n                  Ingress Protection should be of IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.\n\n\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof type shall be used and they should be colour\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally recognised standards for example as detailed\n                 as follows:\n\n                      (a)   110 volts : Yellow.\n\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\n\n                       (c)   415 volts : Red.\n\n         26.10    Connections\n\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection in a system shall be mechanically and electrically\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors  as  per\n                    national/international standards shall only be used to connect cables.\n\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed any where in the work\n                       site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per relevant clause shall be\n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\n\n\n         26.11    Portable and hand-held equipments:\n\n\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable\n                       electrical hand equipment may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but\n                   they shall still be used only on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads.\n\n\n         26.12    Other equipments:\n\n\n          26.12.1   All equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\n                           itself.\n\n\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment shall be earthed through\n                    insulated cable\n\n\n          26.12.3   Isolate exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\n                open switches, and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\n                   unauthorised access.\n\n\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\n                      entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either red\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\" or a barrier of yellow\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor or work\n                    surface.\n\n\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 45 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n237\n\n          29.3       All gas cylinders shall be fixed with pressure regulator and dial gauges\n\n\n          29.4     Non-return valve and Flashback arrester shall be fixed at both end of cylinder and\n                      torch.\n\n\n          29.5     Domestic LPG cylinders shall not be used for Gas welding and Cutting purpose.\n\n\n          29.6    DCP or CO2 type Fire Extinguisher not less than 5 kg shall be fixed at or near to\n                   welding process zone  in an easily accessible  location. Fire Extinguisher should\n                    confirm to IS 2190: 1992.\n\n\n          29.7    Use firewatchers if there is a possibility of ignition unobserved by the operator (e.g. on\n                    the other side of bulkheads).\n\n\n          29.8    Oxygen cylinders and flammable gas cylinders shall be stored separately, at least 6.6\n                  meters (20 feet) apart or separated by a fire proof, 1.5 meters (5 feet) high partition.\n                 Flammable substances shall not be stored within 15 meters of cylinder storage areas.\n\n\n          29.9     Transformer used for electrical arc welding shall be fixed with Ammeter and Voltmeter\n                and also fixed with separate main power switch.\n\n\n         29.10    Welding grounds and returns should be securely attached to the work by cable lugs,\n                 by clamps in the case of stranded conductors, or by bolts for strip conductors. The\n                  ground cable will not be attached to equipment or existing installations or apparatus.\n\n\n         29.11   Use a low voltage open circuit relay device  if welding with alternating current in\n                     constricted or damp places.\n\n         29.12    Take precautions against the risk of increased fume hazards when welding with\n                chrome containing fluxed consumables or high current metal  inert gas (MIG) or\n                   tungsten inert gas (TIG) processes.\n\n         29.13    Avoid being in contact with water or wet floors when welding. Use duckboards or\n                   rubber protection.\n\n\n         29.14     All electrical installations shall meet the IS: 5571: 1997 and NFPA 70 for gas cylinder\n                   storage area and other hazardous areas.\n\n\n         29.15   The current for Electric arc welding shall not exceed 300 A on a hand welding\n                    operation.\n\n\n          30.0    Dangerous and harmful environment\n\n\n                As per BOCWR Rule 40,\n\n                                 i)   When internal combustion engines are to be used into a confined space or\n                         excavation or tunnel or any other workplace where neither natural or artificial\n                             ventilation system  is inadequate  to keep carbon monoxide below 50ppm,\n                       exposure of building workers shall be avoided unless suitable measures are\n                        taken and provided by the contractor.\n\n\n                                    ii)   No worker shall be allowed into any confined space or tank or trench or\n                         excavation wherein there  is given  off any dust, fumes  / vapours or other\n                            impurities which is likely to be injurious or offensive, explosive or poisonous or\n                        noxious or gaseous material or other harmful articles unless steps are carried\n                          out by the contractor and certified by the responsible person to be safe.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          236\n                  ii)    GFCIs/ RCCBs shall be used with all portable electric tool operated especially\n               outdoors or in wet condition.\n\n                  iii)   Before making any adjustments or changing attachments, his workers shall\n               disconnect the tool from the power source.\n\n             iv)   When operating in confined spaces or for prolonged periods, hearing protection\n                  shall be required. The same shall also apply to working with equipments, which\n                gives out more noise as mentioned in clause 43.0 of this contract document.\n\n           v)    Tool is held firmly and the material is properly secured before turning on the\n                   tool.\n\n             vi)    All  drills shall have suitable attachments respective of the operations and\n               powerful for ease of operation.\n\n              vii)  When any work  / operation need to be performed repeatedly or continuously,\n                 tools specifically designed for that work shall be used. The same is applicable to\n               detachable tool bit also.\n\n               viii)   Size of the drill shall be determined by the maximum opening of the chuck n\n              case of drill bit.\n\n             ix)   Attachments such as speed reducing screwdrivers and buffers shall be provided\n                 to prevent fatigue and undue muscle strain to his workers.\n\n           x)    Stock should be clamped or otherwise secured firmly to prevent it from moving.\n\n             xi)   Workers shall never stand on the top of the ladder to  drill holes in walls  /\n                  ceilings, which can be hazardous, instead standing on the fourth or fifth rung\n                  shall be recommended.\n\n              xii)    Electric plane shall not be operated with loose clothing or long scarf or open\n                 jacket.\n\n               xiii)   Safety guards used on right angle head or vertical portable grinders must cover\n             a minimum of 1800 of the wheel and the spindle / wheel specifications shall be\n              checked.\n\n            xiv)   All power tools / hand tools shall have guards at their nip points.\n\n          xv)  Low profile safety chain shall be used in case of wood working machines and\n                the saw shall run at high rpm when cutting and also correct chain tension shall\n             be ensured to avoid “kickback”.\n\n            xvi)  Leather aprons and gloves shall be used as an additional personal protection\n                  auxiliary to withstand kickback.\n\n             xvii)  Push sticks shall be provided and properly used to hold the job down on the\n                 table while the heels moves the stock forward and thus preventing kickbacks.\n\n              xviii)  Air pressure is set at a suitable level for air actuated tool or equipment being\n               used. Before changing or adjusting pneumatic tools, air pressure shall be turned\n                     off.\n\n            xix)  Only trained employees shall use explosive actuated tools and the tool shall\n                also be unloaded when not in use.\n\n          xx)  Usage of such explosive actuated tools shall be avoided in case of places\n             where explosive/flammable vapours or gases may be present.\n\n            xxi)  Explosive actuated tools and their explosives shall be stored separately and be\n               taken out and loaded only before the time of immediate use.\n\n             xxii)  Misfired cartridges of explosive actuated tools must be placed in a container of\n               water and be removed safely from the project.\n\n              xxiii) No worker shall point any power operated  / hand tool to any other person\n                especially during loading / unloading.\n\n\n29.0     Welding, Gouging and Cutting\n\n\n29.1    Gas cylinders in use shall be kept upright on a custom-built stand or trolley fitted\n          with a bracket to accommodate the hoses and equipment or otherwise secured.\n        The metal cap shall be kept in place to protect the valve when the cylinder is not\n         connected for use.\n\n\n29.2    Hose clamp or clip shall be used to connect hoses firmly in both sides of cylinders\n        and torches.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 48 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          238\n31.0      Fire prevention, protection and fighting system\n\n\n31.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  that  construction  site  is provided  with  fire\n         extinguishing  equipment  sufficient  to  extinguish  any  probable   fire  at\n         construction site. An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure as\n         per national standard.\n\n\n31.2     Recharging of fire extinguishers and their proper maintenance should be ensured and\n         as a minimum should meet Indian National Standards\n\n\n31.3       All drivers  of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers  shall be trained on\n          operating the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.\n\n31.4    The contractor shall also give consideration to the provision of adequate fire fighting\n         arrangements within the underground and tunnelling operations including the provision\n           of Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency lighting\n\n\n31.5    As per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin\n         should be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher.\n\n\n31.6     Combustible scrap and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a\n          regular basis. If scrap is to be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and\n          located at a distance no less than 12 metres from any construction work or any other\n         combustible material.\n\n\n31.7     Every fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to\n          the Employer representatives.\n\n\n31.8     Emergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued. Mock drills\n         should be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements and\n         as a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be\n          prominently displayed near each telephone on site.\n\n\n32.0     Corrosive substances\n\n\n32.1    As per BOCWR Rule 44, corrosive substances including alkalis and acids shall be\n          stored and used by a person dealing with such substances at a building / construction\n            site in a manner that it does not endanger the building worker and suitable PPE shall\n        be provided by the contractor to the worker during such handling and work. In case of\n           spillage of such substances on building worker, the contractor shall take immediate\n         remedial measures.\n\n\n33.0     Demolition\n\n33.1    The Contractor shall ensure that\n\n                i)       all  demolition  works be  carried  out  in a  controlled manner  under  the\n            management of experienced and competent supervision.\n\n                  ii)    the concerned department of the Government or local authority be informed and\n               permission obtained wherever required. Media shall also be informed regarding\n                   this concern.\n\n\n                  iii)     all glass or similar materials or articles in exterior openings are removed\n              before commencing any demolition work and all water, steam, electric,\n             gas and other similar supply lines are put-off and such lines so located or\n            capped with substantial coverings so as to protect it from damage and to\n               afford safety to the building workers and public..\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 50 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          242\n\n36.7     Regulatory signs\n\n\n36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\n         they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities.\n\n\n36.8     Warning signs\n\n\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\n         hazards that may be encountered.\n\n\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\n          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\n         entrances exist.\n\n\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\n         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\n           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\n\n\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\n          during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\n          the caution to the road users.\n\n\n36.9      Delineators\n\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have two\n            distinct purposes:\n\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path\n\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\n\n\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\n         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\n          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\n          Delineators.\n\n\n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\n\n\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\n\n36.9.3   Drums\n\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\n         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\n\n\n36.9.4    Barricades\n\n\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\n        movement. Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to\n          construction equipment and other temporary structures.\n\n\n36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,\n      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in\n          tender document.\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 54 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          240\n                i)    every compressed air system in a tunnel is provided with emergency power\n               supply for maintained continued supply of compressed air as per Rule 155 of\n         BOCWR\n\n                  ii)    watertight bulkhead doors are installed at the entrance of a tunnel to prevent\n                 flooding.\n\n                  iii)    reliable and effective means of communication such as telephone or walkie-\n                   talkie are provided and maintained for arranging better effective communication\n                 at an excavation or tunnelling work as per Rule 136 of BOCWR.\n\n             iv)     all portable electrical hand tools and inspection lamp used in under ground and\n               confined space at an excavation or tunnelling work is operated at a voltage not\n              exceeding 24V.\n\n           v)    only flame proof equipment of appropriate type as per IS:5571:2000 and or\n                other relevant national standard is used inside the tunnel\n\n             vi)    petrol or LPG of any other flammable substances are not used, stored inside the\n                tunnel except with prior approval from Employer, and also no oxy-acetylene gas\n                    is used in a compressed air environment in excavation or tunnelling\n\n              vii)   adequate number of water outlets provided for fire fighting purpose, an audible\n                     fire alarm and adequate number and types of fire extinguishers are provided\n             and maintained.\n\n               viii)  temperature in any working chamber in an excavation or tunnelling work where\n              workers employed does not exceed 29C as per Rule 165 of BOCWR.\n\n             ix)     all working areas in a free air tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\n              approved by the Director General and the fresh air supplied in such tunnel is not\n                less than 6 m3/ min for each worker employed in tunnel as per Rule 153 of\n          BOCWR.\n\n\n34.3     Warning signs and notices:\n\n\n34.3.1   The contractor shall ensure that\n\n                i)     suitable warning signs or notices, required for the safety of building workers\n                carrying out the work of an excavation or tunnelling, shall be displayed or\n               erected at conspicuous  places in Hindi and in a language understood by\n                majority of such building workers at such building such excavation or tunnelling\n              work\n\n                  ii)    such warning signs and notices with regard to compressed air working shall\n                include\n\n                a)    the danger involved in such compressed air work\n\n                b)     fire and explosion hazard\n\n                 c)    the emergency procedures for rescue from such danger or hazards.\n\n\n35.0    Work Permit system\n\n\n35.1    The Contractor shall develop a Work Permit system, which is a formal written system\n        used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. A work permit is a\n         document, which specifies the work to be done, and the precautions to be taken. Work\n         Permits form an essential part of safe systems of work for many construction activities.\n        They allow work to start only after safe procedures have been defined and they\n          provide a clear record that all foreseeable hazards have been considered. Permits to\n        Work are usually required in high-risk areas as identified by the Risk Assessments.\n\n\n35.2    A permit  is needed when construction work can only be carried out   if normal\n         safeguards are dropped or when new hazards are introduced by the work. Examples\n           of high-risk activities include but are not limited to:\n\n\n                 i)     Entry into confined spaces\n                  ii)   Work in close proximity to overhead power lines and telecommunication cables.\n                  iii)   Hot work.\n             iv)   To dig—where underground services may be located.\n           v)   Work with heavy moving machinery.\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 52 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n243\n          36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\n                 numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\n                   maintains a barricade register in site.\n\n\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously seen in the dark/night time by the road\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade. Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top\n                   of each barricade.\n\n\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\n                         (like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\n                    State Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\n                      of Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\n\n\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\n\n\n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\n\n\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at\n                   his cost.\n\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\n\n\n          36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\n                 proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\n                 brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\n                  the entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\n\n          37.0    Work to adjacent railways\n\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live railways then the\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\n\n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\n\n                      (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\n                         given specific authority.\n\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance with the railway owner’s requirements shall\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts)\n\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times.\n\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall be strictly observed\n\n\n          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\n\n\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\n                         avoided.\n\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\n                  PPE zone\n\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\n                            barrications.\n\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 55 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n239\n                          iv)   examine the walls of all structures adjacent to the structure to be demolished to\n                        determine thickness, method of support to such adjacent structures\n\n                      v)   no demolishing work be performed if the adjacent structure seems to be unsafe\n                         unless and until remedial measures life sheet piling, shoring, bracing or similar\n                    means be ensured for safety and stability for adjacent structure from collapsing.\n\n                          vi)    debris / bricks and other materials or articles shall be removed by means of\n                           a)      chutes\n                           b)     buckets or hoists\n                            c)      through openings through floors or\n                           d)     any other safe means\n\n                             vii)   no person other than  building workers  or other persons  essential  to the\n                         operation of demolition work shall be permitted to enter a zone of demolition and\n                          the area be provided with substantial barricades.\n\n\n          34.0     Excavation and Tunnelling:\n\n\n          34.1     Excavation\n\n\n          34.1.1   The contractor shall ensure\n\n\n                                 i)    where any construction building worker engaged in excavation is exposed to\n                       hazard of falling or sliding material or article from any bank or side of such\n                         excavation which is more than one 1.5 m above his footing, such worker is\n                          protected by adequate piling and bracing against such bank or side.\n\n\n                                    ii)    where banks of an excavation are undercut, adequate shoring is provided to\n                         support the material or article overhanging such bank.\n\n\n                                     iii)   excavated material is not stored at least 0.65 m from the edge of an open\n                         excavation or trench and banks of such excavation or trench are >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n247\n                    monitoring and inspection programs.\n\n          40.12.2   In  Site  Environmental  Plan,  the  Contractor  shall  prepare and submit monthly\n                   Environmental Quality Management Reports in accordance with Requirements as per\n                    Contract.\n\n          40.12.3  The monthly report shall include (but not limited to) the following:\n                       Executive Summary\n\n                       Brief mention of construction activities\n\n                       Monitoring results under AMCP, and NMCP\n\n                       Interpretation of monitoring results, significance and influencing factors\n\n                       Graphical representation of monitored results over past four reporting periods.\n\n                      Measures to control spill under SPCP.\n\n                       Action taken on recommendations under site inspection programme or specific\n                          directions.\n\n                      Summary of complaints, results of investigations and follow-up action\n\n                       Future key issues.\n\n         40.13   COMPLAINT RESPONSE PROCESS\n          40.13.1   Inquiries, complaints and requests for information can be expected from a wide range\n                      of  individuals and organizations both private and government.  The majority of\n                   complaints is likely to be received by BMRCL, although the site offices are also likely\n                      to be contacted.\n\n          40.13.2  The objective of complaint process is to ensure that public and agency complaints are\n                  addressed and resolved consistently and expeditiously.\n\n          40.13.3  The Contractor’s Site Manager will be notified immediately on receipt of complaint that\n              may relate to environmental impacts. The Site Manager will immediately inform the\n                  Engineer and through him the BMRCL.\n\n          40.13.4   Field investigation should determine whether the complaint has merit, and if so action\n                   should be taken to address the impact.\n          40.13.5  The outcome of the investigation and the action taken shall be documented on a\n                   complaint Performa prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Engineer in\n                 advance of the works.\n\n          40.13.6  Where possible, a formal response to each complaint received shall be prepared by\n                    the Contractor within seven days in order to notify the concerned person(s) that action\n                 has been taken.\n\n         40.14   COMPLETION OF THE EQM PROGRAMME\n          40.14.1  The construction of Bangalore Metro  will be undertaken as a series of individual\n                    construction contracts with necessarily different construction program and completion\n                    dates.\n\n          40.14.2  The Engineer shall maintain an overview of the ‘impact causing potential’ of each site\n                     or contract and monitoring parameter with a view to maintaining the most cost\n                      effective use of the environmental resources dedicated to the Project.\n\n          40.14.3 Termination of EQM should focus on the percentage contract completion status and on\n                  the basis of a history of environmental impact arising from the site over a representative\n                 period of monitoring.\n\n         40.13.5    Justifiable application for termination of EQM shall be put forward by the\n                    Contractor  to the Engineer, as necessary throughout the  construction\n                       period.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 59 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          246\n         Logo of the corresponding main contracting company for their employees and sub-\n           contracting company for their employees shall only be used.\n\n\n 39.5      In addition to the above any other PPE required for any specific jobs like, welding and\n            cutting, working at height, tunnelling etc shall also be provided to all workmen and also\n          ensure that all workmen use the PPEs properly while on the job.\n\n\n 39.6    The contractor shall not pay any cash amount in lieu of PPE to the workers/sub-\n          contractors and expect them to buy and use during work.\n\n\n 39.7    The contractor shall at all time maintain a minimum of 10% spare PPEs and\n          safety appliances and properly record and show to the Employer during the\n          inspections.  Failing  to do so  shall  invite appropriate penalty as per the\n          provisions of the contract.\n\n\n 39.8         It is always the duty of the contractor to provide required PPEs for all visitors. Towards\n             this required quantity of PPEs shall be kept always at the security post.\n\n\n 40.0      Visitors to site\n\n\n 40.1    No visitor is allowed to enter the site without the permission of the Employer. All\n          authorised visitors should report at the site office. Contractor shall provide visitor’s\n          helmet (White helmet with visitor sticker) and other PPEs like Safety Shoe, reflective\n            jacket, respiratory protection etc. as per requirement of the site.\n\n\n 40.2       All Visitors shall be accompanied at all times by a responsible member of the site\n          personnel.\n\n\n 40.3    The contractor shall be fully responsible for all visitors’ safety and health within the\n             site.\n\n\n 40.4    As indicated earlier in this Manual, the Engineer shall undertake regular audits at\n           quarterly intervals, of the Contractor’s onsite practices and procedures as a means of\n          assessing the ongoing performance of the Contractor.\n\n 40.5    The criteria against which the audits will be undertaken shall be derived from the\n          clauses within the Environment Protection Requirements (Appendix III herein above),\n           contract-specific Site Environmental Plan and previous site inspection results.\n\n 40.6      In addition to the quarterly audits by the Engineer, site inspection shall be undertaken\n         by the Contractor’s staff to inspect the construction activities in order to ensure that\n           appropriate environmental protection and pollution control measures are properly\n           followed and implemented.\n\n 40.7    The frequency of site inspection shall be at least once a week.\n\n 40.8    The Contractor shall prepare an ‘Environmental Inspection and Action Reporting\n          System’ and submit to the Engineer for approval and make amendments as\n          suggested.  It shall contain a contract specific comprehensive Environment Inspection\n           checklist as requirement of Site Environmental Plan.\n 40.9    The area of inspection shall not be limited to environmental compliance within the site\n           but areas outside the site which are likely to be affected, directly or indirectly by\n             activities at site.\n\n 40.10     Results of inspection shall be discussed with Engineer and his recommendations on\n           better environmental protection shall be notified to the Contractor for taking immediate\n           action and rapid resolution of identified non-compliance.\n40.11       If significant environmental problems are identified or if there is an environmental\n          complaint or as a part of investigation work, then the Engineer shall also carry out Ad\n         hoc site inspection which shall be attended by Contractor’s Representative.\n\n 40.12   REPORTING SYSTEM\n\n 40.12.1   reporting under  the Environmental Management System  will  contain  results  of\n\n\n Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. ### Jd279c4e4cfdf35c3

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 18.0 — Working at Height|SHE 18.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 40 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/1/fragments/8`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 40,
>   "text": "18.20    Requirements for Ladders\n\n\n          1)    Every contractor shall ensure that a ladder is used for work at height only if\n             a risk assessment has demonstrated that the use of more suitable work\n              equipment is not justified because of the low risk and\n\n                          i)    The short duration of use; or\n\n                            ii)    Existing features on site, which he cannot alter.\n\n          2)    Only metal ladders shall be allowed. Bamboo ladders are prohibited.\n\n          3)   Any surface upon which a ladder rests shall be stable, firm, of sufficient\n                strength and of suitable composition safely to support the ladder so that its\n              rungs or steps remain horizontal, and any loading intended to be placed on\n                            it.\n\n          4)   A ladder shall be so positioned as to ensure its stability during use\n\n          5)   A suspended ladder shall be attached in a secure manner and so that, with\n                the exception of a flexible ladder,  it cannot be displaced and swinging is\n               prevented.\n\n          6)   A portable ladder shall be prevented from slipping during use by -\n\n                          i)     securing the stiles at or near their upper or lower ends;\n\n                            ii)    an effective anti-slip or other effective stability device; or\n\n                             iii)   any other arrangement of equivalent effectiveness.\n\n          7)   A ladder used for access shall be long enough to protrude sufficiently above\n                the place of landing to which  it provides access, unless other measures\n             have been taken to ensure a firm handhold.\n\n          8)   No interlocking or extension ladder shall be used unless its sections are\n               prevented from moving relative to each other while in use.\n\n          9)   A mobile ladder shall be prevented from moving before it is stepped on.\n\n         10)  Where a ladder or run of ladders raises a vertical distance of 9 metres or\n             more above its base, there shall, where reasonably practicable, be provided\n                 at suitable intervals sufficient safe landing areas or rest platforms.\n\n         11)  Every ladder shall be used in such a way that\n\n                a)   a secure handhold and secure support are always available to the\n                      user; and\n\n                b)    the user can maintain a safe handhold when carrying a load unless, in\n                     the case of a step ladder, the maintenance of a handhold  is not\n                       practicable when a load  is  carried, and a  risk assessment has\n                   demonstrated that the use of a stepladder is justified because of\n\n                                    i)     the low risk; and\n\n                                       ii)    the short duration of use."
> }

### J7de3b9ae72bffb1e

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 21.0 — Lifting Appliances and Gear|SHE 21.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 43 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/4/fragments/2`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 43,
>   "text": "21.10.2  Boom\n\n\n                                 i)    The boom is one of the more critical elements of the crane and must be in\n                           perfect condition at all time. No boom section with a bent lattice member\n                             shall be allowed\n\n                                    ii)     All welds shall be crack and corrosion free\n\n                                     iii)   No member of the boom shall be bent\n\n                          iv)    All telescopic boom shall be free from cracks, rust, flaking or cracked paint,\n                          bulges, greases or varnishes\n\n          21.10.3  The sweep area (work area) of the construction machinery shall be always free\n                  from obstructions.\n\n\n          21.10.4   All hydraulic piping and fittings shall be maintained leak proof.\n\n\n          21.10.5  The operator cab shall posses good and safe:\n\n\n                                 i)     structure, windows and windshield wipers\n\n                                    ii)    Drivers chair and foot rest\n\n                                     iii)    Control handles\n\n                          iv)   Cab instrumentation\n\n                      v)    Telecommunication\n\n                          vi)   Cab out fitting\n\n                             vii)   wind  indicator  with an  adjustable  set  point  shall be  in a  position\n                          representative for the wind on the crane. The indicator shall give continuous\n                          information regarding constant speeds and gusts.\n\n\n         21.11    Mandatory rigging requirements\n\n\n          21.11.1  Rigging shall be done under experienced and qualified rigger only.\n\n\n          21.11.2  The primary requirement in rigging shall be to assess the weight of load\n                  before attempting any lift.\n\n\n          21.11.3   All hooks shall be fitted with Master Rings having certificate of fitness from\n                  the competent person, so that the hooks are subjected to balanced vertical\n                  loading only.\n\n\n          21.11.4  Only four legged slings shall be allowed which includes master link (ring),\n                  intermediate master link (ring)  if necessary, chain  / wire rope sling, sling\n               hook or other terminal fitting.\n\n\n          21.11.5  Hand spliced slings up to 32mm diameter shall not be used at site for any\n                       lifting purpose.\n\n\n          21.11.6  No load shall be slewed over public areas without stopping the pedestrians\n               and road traffic first.\n\n\n          21.11.7  Requirements of outriggers\n\n                              i)     All outriggers shall be fully extended and at all tyres are clear of the ground\n\n                                    ii)   Heavy duty blocking having large bearing area shall be necessary to prevent\n                        sinking of floats\n\n\n          21.11.8   All loads shall have tag-lines attached in order to ensure that the load can be\n                   controlled at all times."
> }
