### Jcf31dc552bb53faa

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 43.0 — Noise|SHE 43.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 67 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/2/fragments/1`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 67,
>   "text": "43.1.3   The noise monitoring requirements including monitoring locations are given in the\n                     project SHE Manual.\n\n\n          43.2    NOISE MONITORING\n\n          43.2.1   The activities which are expected to cause noise during the construction of Bangalore\n                   metro, include noise from construction equipment, construction activities such as portal\n                     construction, boring for piling, earthwork excavation, concreting, viaduct, station, depot\n                    construction (including shifting of launching truss  / girder) and removal of spoil and\n                movement of construction vehicles and delivery vehicles, traveling to and from the\n                    construction and disposal sites.\n          43.2.2   The level of impact of these noise sources depends upon the noise characteristics of\n                    the equipment and activities involved the construction schedule, and the distance from\n                   noise sensitive receptors.\n\n          43.2.3   The Noise Monitoring and Control Plan (NMCP) in contract specific site Environmental\n                    Quality Management Plan prepared by the Contractor shall establish procedures to\n                   monitor construction noise and determine when to apply measures to control noise\n                      pollution due to construction activities at work sites.\n\n          43.2.4   The NMCP will provide site description, define acceptable noise monitoring equipment,\n                    provide siting and operating procedures for noise equipment, indicate reports and record\n                   keeping on noise monitoring data.\n\n\n\n          43.2.5   The NMCP will provide guidance for construction activity.   It shall also address noise\n                  performance criteria used in the selection of construction equipment.\n\n          43.2.6   The Noise Monitoring and Control Plan shall provide for:\n                       a) Definition of noise-sensitive uses in the zones affected by construction.\n                       b)   Calculation of future noise levels at the closest noise-sensitive receptors to the\n                            construction activity based on construction activity and ambient noise levels.\n                        c)   Evaluation and specification of the noise abatement measures that can be\n                           applied to meet the noise objectives.\n                       d)   Monitoring construction activity and providing adjustments to noise abatement\n                             controls that may be required to increase their effectiveness.\n                       e)  regular reporting\n                                 f)   Requirements of NMCP:\n                                            (i)     It shall specify the nighttime and daytime construction activities, monitoring\n                                    locations, equipment, procedures, and schedule of measurements and\n                                   reporting methods to be used.\n                                                (ii)    It shall contain a scaled plan indicating monitoring locations, including\n                            measurements to be taken at construction site boundaries and at nearby\n                                     residential zones.\n                                                  (iii)  a record of the noise characteristics of powered mechanical equipment\n                             proposed to be used during day time and night time and of proposed\n                               working methods and of potential noise level reduction measures.\n                                      (iv)  Provisions for immediate notification when measured noise levels exceed\n                                 allowable limits,\n                                  (v)  Provide a reporting procedure whereby noise-monitoring data is furnished\n                                     to the Engineer on a weekly basis.\n\n          43.2.7    In defining the requirements of the NMCP, available measures for noise control, such\n                    as, the use of equipment with special exhaust silencers or enclosures, and the\n                    construction of temporary enclosures or noise barriers around specific construction\n                       site activity areas shall be considered.  It should also specify the measures to be\n                  adopted to counter the impact of noise pollution for public and workers working at site\n                    during construction.\n\n          43.2.8      If the measured noise levels exceed the noise limits, the noise levels shall be reduced\n                 by appropriate abatement measures.\n\n         43.2.9    The NMCP will be reviewed on a regular basis and updated as necessary to assure\n                    current construction activities are addressed."
> }

### J1dd8d9c8b2265f58

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 43.0 — Noise|SHE 43.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 68 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/2/fragments/2`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 68,
>   "text": "43.2.10  The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance of tasks specified, and  will\n          inspect necessary records, reports and procedures related to the control of noise.\n\n43.2.11  Impact monitoring shall be carried out at noise sensitive receptor locations within 200\n           feet of the construction site once each week and after a change in construction\n            activity. Construction noise measurements shall coincide with daytime and nighttime\n          periods of maximum noise generating construction activities.\n\n43.2.12  Noise Monitoring data will be submitted in a Noise Measurement Report Form. It will\n          contain the type of measurement, duration of measurement, distance of monitoring\n         from construction site, and construction equipment working during monitoring period.\n\n43.2.13   appropriate  parameter  for measuring  construction  noise  impacts  shall be  the\n          equivalent A-weighted sound pressure level (Leq) measured in decibels (dB). The two\n            statistical sound levels L10 and L90; the level exceeded for 10 and 90 percent of the time\n           respectively, shall also be recorded during monitoring. The L90 may be considered as\n          the ambient level into which the L10 as average peak level intrudes. The Lmax, Leq, L10\n        and L90 values will be reported in the noise measurement form along with allowable\n         noise limit. The duration of monitoring shall be for a minimum of 30 minutes.\n\n43.2..14  In no case  shall the Contractor expose the public  to construction noise levels\n         exceeding 90dBA (slow) or to impulsive noise levels with a peak sound pressure level\n         exceeding 140dB as measured on an impulse sound level meter.\n\n43.2.15   Limit for construction noise is based on the existing ambient noise levels in areas\n          adjoining the construction sites.\n\n43.2.16 The noise levels emanating from any source during construction, shall not exceed 5\n         dB(A) or more above existing ambient pre-construction noise levels when measured at\n        a point outside the premises of the location of source. The same may be varied from\n         time to time by and at the sole discretion of the Engineer.\n43.2.17  Where there are no ambient noise measurements, the construction activities shall be\n           limited to levels measured at a distance of 200 feet from the construction limits or at\n          the nearest affected building, whichever is closer, as given in Table-2.\n                                 TABLE-2\n                  ALLOWABLE CONSTRUCTION NOISE\n     LAND USE               MAXIMUM NOISE LEVELS- Lmax dB (A)\n                                            Day Time Night Time\n          Residential                      75             65\n          At all Times\n          Commercial                                   85\n             Industrial                                     90\n\n\n43.2.18   At the surface of the construction site during night time hours, the Contractor shall use\n          only equipment that operating under full load meets the noise limits specified in Table-\n           3, if a sensitive receptor would be affected.\n                             TABLE-3\n NOISE EMISSION LIMITS FOR CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT USED DURING NIGHTTIME\n              HOURS; MEASURED AT 50 FEET FROM CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT*\n Equipment Category                                     Lmax Level dB(A)\n\n Backhoe                                                80\n Bar Bender                                              75\n Chain Saw                                              81\n Compactor                                              80\n Compressor                                             80\n Concrete Mixer                                           85\n Concrete Pump                                           82\n Crane                                                  85\n Dozer                                                  85\n Front End Loader                                         80\n Generator                                               82\n Gradall                                                 85\n Grader                                                  85\n Paver                                                  85"
> }

      AGGREGATE DURATION            LIMIT\n           Sustained (1 hr/day)                               0.01 in/sec (80 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\n           Transient (<1 hr/day)                               0.03 in/sec (90 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\n           Transient (<10 min/day)                            0.10 in/sec (100 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\n\n\n          43.2.20  When  Diesel Generator (DG) Sets  are used  for  operation  of equipment and\n                   machinery, then ‘Standards and Guidelines  for  control  of Noise  Pollution from\n                    Stationery DG Sets’, under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 shall apply.\n         43.2.21  Should the impact monitoring record noise levels which are:\n                         indicative of a deteriorating situation such that closer monitoring is reasonably\n                            indicated, or\n                        when in the opinion of the Engineer additional measurements are required in\n                        view of deteriorating noise environment, then, the Engineer may require the\n                         Contractor to increase the frequency of impact monitoring at any one or more of\n                          the monitoring stations until the results indicate an improving and acceptable\n                             level of noise.\n\n        43.2..22    The Contractor  shall submit a copy  of monitoring  results. The  results should\n                    represent  a statistical evaluation of data for evaluation of trends and comparison\n                      with noise emission standards.\n\n        43.2.23   Where the Engineer determines that the recorded Noise level is significantly\n                    greater than the acceptable levels, the Engineer may direct the Contractor to\n                   take effective remedial measures including, but not limited to, reviewing noise\n                  sources and modifying working procedures.\n\n         43.2.23    The Contractor shall inform the Engineer of all steps taken to investigate cause of\n                  exceedance and immediate action taken to avoid further exceedance through\n                       written reports and proposals for action under an Event Contingency Plan.\n\n          43.3       Control Requirements\n\n\n          43.3.1     Construction material should be operated and transported in such a manner as not to\n                     create unnecessary noise as outlined below:\n\n\n                                 i)    Perform Work within the procedures outlined herein and comply with applicable\n                        codes,  regulations, and  standards  established by  the  Central and  State\n                     Government and their agencies."

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          248\n\n               PART – III: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND WELFARE\n\n\n41.0     Physical fitness of workmen\n\n\n41.1    The contractor shall ensure that his employees/workmen subject themselves to such\n         medical examination as required under the law or under the contract provision and\n        keep a record of the same.\n\n\n41.2    The contractor shall not permit any employee/workmen to enter the work area under\n          the influence of alcohol or any drugs.\n\n\n42.0     Medical Facilities\n\n\n42.1     Medical Examination\n\n\n42.1.1   The contractor shall arrange a medical examination of all his employees including his\n          sub-contractor employees employed as drivers, operators of  lifting appliances and\n          transport equipment before employing, after illness or injury,  if  it appears that the\n           illness or injury might have affected his fitness and, thereafter, once in every two years\n        up to the age of 40 and once in a year, thereafter.\n\n\n                i)    The Contractor shall maintain the confidential records of medical examination or\n                the physician authorized by the Employer.\n\n                  ii)   No building or other construction worker is charged for the medical examination\n             and the cost of such examination is borne by contractor employing such building\n               worker.\n\n                  iii)   The medical examination shall include: -\n\n\n                a)     Full medical and occupational history.\n\n                b)     Clinical examination with particular reference to\n\n                                    i)    General Physique;\n\n                                       ii)     Vision:- Total visual performance using standard orthorator  like\n                         Titmus  Vision  Tester  should be  estimated and  suitability  for\n                         placement  ascertained  in accordance  with  the  prescribed  job\n                           standards.\n\n                                        iii)    Hearing:  - Persons with normal must be able to hear a forced\n                          whisper at twenty-four feet. Persons using hearing aids must be\n                           able to hear a warning shout under noisy working conditions.\n\n                             iv)    Breathing:- Peak flow rate using standard peak flow meter and the\n                        average peak flow rate determined out of these readings of the test\n                          performed.  The  results  recorded  at  pre-placement  medical\n                          examination could be used as a standard for the same individual at\n                           the same altitude for reference during subsequent examination.\n\n                        v)   Upper Limbs: - Adequate arm function and grip\n\n                             vi)    Spine: - Adequately flexible for the job concerned.\n\n                               vii)   Lower Limbs: - Adequate leg and foot concerned.\n\n                                 viii)   General: - Mental alertness and stability with good eye, hand and\n                              foot coordination.\n\n                 c)   Any other tests which the examining doctor considers necessary\n\n\n42.1.2.     If the contractor fails to get the medical examination conducted as mentioned above,\n          the employer will have the right to get the same conducted by through an agency with\n           intimation to the contractor and deduct the cost and overhead charges.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n249\n          42.2     Occupational Health Centre\n\n          42.2.1   The contractor shall ensure at a construction site an occupational health centre,\n                 mobile or static is provided and maintained in good order. Services and facilities\n                as per the scale lay down in Schedule X of BOCWR. A construction medical\n                     officer appointed in an occupational health centre, possess the qualification as\n                     laid down in Schedule XI of BOCWR.\n\n\n          42.3    Ambulance van and room\n\n\n          42.3.1   The contractor  shall ensure  at a construction  site of a building or other\n                  construction work that an ambulance van and room are provided at such\n                  construction site or an arrangement is made with a nearby hospital for providing\n                such ambulance van for transportation of serious cases of accident or sickness\n                   of workers  to  hospital promptly and such ambulance van and room are\n                 maintained in good repair and is equipped with standard facilities specified in\n                Schedule IV and Schedule V of BOCWR.\n\n\n          42.4      First-aid boxes\n\n\n          42.4.1   The contractor shall ensure at a construction site one First-aid box for 100 workers\n                   provided and maintained for providing First-aid to the building workers. Every First-aid\n                 box  is  distinctly marked  “First-aid” and  is equipped with the  articles specified  in\n                 Schedule III of BOCWR.\n\n\n          42.5     HIV/ AIDS prevention and control\n\n\n          42.5.1   The contractor shall adopt the Employer’s Policy on “HIV  / AIDS Prevention and\n                    Control for Workmen Engaged by Contractors” and the copy of the policy is given in\n                Appendix No.: 4.\n\n          42.5.2   The Employer will engage a professional agency for implementing the guidelines laid\n               down in the policy and communicate to the contractor.\n\n          42.5.3   The Contractor shall extend necessary support to the appointed agency by deputing\n                    the workmen to attend the awareness creation programmes.\n\n          42.5.4   The contractor shall also extend necessary organizational support to the appointed\n                 agency  for the  effective implementation  of the Employers’ workplace  policy on\n                 HIV/AIDS for workmen of the Contractors.\n\n          42.5.5   As laid down in the policy the contractor shall identify peer educators (1 for every 100\n                   workers) and refer them for professional training to the Employers’ appointed agency\n                       for the purpose.\n\n          42.5.6   The peer educators on completion of the training shall serve as the focal point\n                    for any information, education and awareness campaign among the workmen\n                 throughout the contract period.\n\n          42.5.7   The peer educators will be paid a monthly honorarium as fixed by the Employer for\n                   rendering his services in addition to his regular duty.\n\n          42.5.8   The total number of peer educators (1 for 100 workers) shall always be maintained by\n                    the contractor.\n\n          42.5.9    In case if these peer educators leave the contractor by creating vacancy, then\n                  the contractor at his own expense train the new replacement peer educator from\n                  the Employers’ appointed agency for the purpose.\n          42.5.10    It is suggested to the contractor that due care should be taken to select the peer\n                   educators from among the group of workmen so that they remain with the contractor\n                   throughout the contract period.\n\n          42.6     Prevention of mosquito breeding\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. ### Jd8ad6700267a399b

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 43.0 — Noise|SHE 43.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 70 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/2/fragments/4`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 70,
>   "text": "ii)   Keep noise to the lowest reasonably practicable level.  Appropriate measures\n                     will be taken to ensure that construction works will not cause any unnecessary\n                or excessive noise, which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings,\n                schools, hospitals, or premises with similar sensitivity to noise. Use equipment\n                with  effective  noise-suppression  devices and employ  other  noise  control\n             measures as to protect the public.\n\n                  iii)   Schedule and conduct operations in a manner that will minimize, to the greatest\n                extent  feasible,  the  disturbance  to  the  public  in  areas  adjacent  to  the\n                construction  activities and  to occupants  of  buildings  in the  vicinity  of the\n                construction activities.\n\n             iv)   The Contractor shall submit to the Employer a Noise Monitoring and Control\n              Plan (NMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan.   It shall include\n                       full and comprehensive details of all powered mechanical equipment, which he\n              proposes to use during daytime and night - time, and of his proposed working\n             methods and noise level reduction measures. The NMCP shall include detailed\n               noise calculations and vibration levels to demonstrate the anticipated noise\n               generation and vibrations by the Contractor.\n\n           v)   The NMCP prepared by the Contractor  shall guide the implementation  of\n                construction  activity. The NMCP  will be reviewed on a regular basis and\n              updated  as  necessary  to  assure  that  current  construction  activities  are\n               addressed.  It may appear as a regular agenda item in project coordination\n               meetings, if noise is an issue at any location in the contract.\n\n\n43.4     Occupational Noise\n\n\n                i)     Protection  against  the  effects  of  occupational  noise exposure should be\n               provided when the sound level exceeds the threshold values as provided in\n                Project SHE Manual.\n\n                  ii)   When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in the\n                Table, feasible administrative or engineering controls should be utilized as given\n                   in this document and BMRC’s Project SHE Manual.\n\n                  iii)      If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal\n                 protective equipment shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within\n                the levels of the table.\n\n             iv)   When the daily noise exposure is composed of two or more periods of noise\n              exposure of different levels, their combined effect should be considered, rather\n               than the individual effect of each. Exposure to different levels for various periods\n                 of time shall be computed according to the formula and sample computations,\n              as given in project SHE Manual.\n\n\n43.4      Vibration Level\n\n\n43.4.1    In locations where the alignment  is close to  historical  / heritage structures, the\n          contractor shall prepare a monitoring scheme prior to construction at such locations.\n          This scheme for monitoring vibration level at such historical / heritage sites shall be\n         submitted to Employer for his approval. This scheme shall include:\n\n                i)     Monitoring requirements  for  vibrations  at  regular  intervals  throughout  the\n                construction period.\n\n                  ii)    Pre-construction  structural  integrity  inspections  of  historic  and  sensitive\n                structures in project activity.\n\n                  iii)    Information dissemination about the construction method, probable  effects,\n                 quality control measures and precautions to be used.\n\n             iv)   The vibration level limits at work sites adjacent to the alignment shall conform to\n                the permitted values of peak p velocity as given in article project SHE Manual."
> }

### Ja2ee2729a4e94860

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          250\n42.6.1   Measures shall be taken to prevent mosquito breeding at site. The measures to be\n         taken shall include:\n\n\n                i)    Empty cans, oil drums, packing and other receptacles, which may retain water\n                  shall be deposited at a central collection point and shall be removed from the\n                   site regularly.\n\n                  ii)      Still waters shall be treated at least once every week with oil in order to prevent\n              mosquito breeding.\n\n                  iii)    Contractor’s equipment and other items on the site, which may retain water,\n                  shall be stored, covered or treated in such a manner that water could not be\n                 retained.\n\n             iv)   Water storage tanks shall be provided.\n\n\n42.6.2    Posters in both Hindi, English and local language which draw attention to the dangers\n           of permitting mosquito breeding, shall be displayed prominently on the site.\n\n\n42.6.3   The contractor at periodic interval shall arrange to prevent mosquito breeding\n        by fumigation  / spraying of insecticides. Most  effective insecticides  shall\n         include SOLFAC WP 10 or Baytex, The Ideal Larvicide etc.\n\n\n42.7     Alcohol and drugs\n\n\n42.7.1   The contractor shall ensure at  all times that no employee  is working under the\n          influence of alcohol / drugs which are punishable under Govt. regulations.\n\n\n42.7.2   Smoking  at  public worksites by any employee  is also prohibited as per Govt.\n          regulations.\n\n\n43.0     Noise\n\n\n43.1    The Contractor shall consider noise as an environmental constraint in his design,\n          planning and execution of the Works and provide demonstrable evidence of the same\n        on Employer’s request. The Contractor shall, at his own expense, take all appropriate\n        measures  to ensure  that work  carried out by the Contractor and by  his sub-\n          Contractors, whether on or off the Site, will not cause any unnecessary or excessive\n         noise which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings, schools, hospitals, or\n         premises with similar sensitivity to noise.\n\n\n43.1.1    Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, noise level reduction measures\n           shall include the following:\n\n\n                i)    The Contractor shall ensure that all powered mechanical equipment used in the\n             Works shall be effectively sound reduced using the most modern techniques\n                available including but not limited to silencers and mufflers.\n\n                  ii)   The Contractor shall construct acoustic screens or enclosures around any parts\n                 of the Works from which excessive noise may be generated.\n\n\n43.1.2   The Contractor shall ensure that noise generated by work carried out by the Contractor\n        and his sub-Contractors during daytime and night time shall not exceed the maximum\n          permissible noise limits, whether continuously or intermittently, as given in the project\n       SHE Manual. The same may be varied from time to time by and at the sole discretion\n           of the Employer, In the event of a breach of this requirement, the Contractor shall\n         immediately re-deploy or adjust the relevant equipment or take other appropriate\n        measures to reduce the noise levels and thereafter maintain them at levels which do\n          not exceed the said limits. Such measures may include without limitation the temporary\n          or permanent cessation of use of certain items of equipment.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 62 of 114",

>       ],
>       "block_number": 3,
>       "text": "42.6.1 \nMeasures shall be taken to prevent mosquito breeding at site. The measures to be \ntaken shall include: \n \ni) \nEmpty cans, oil drums, packing and other receptacles, which may retain water \nshall be deposited at a central collection point and shall be removed from the \nsite regularly. \nii) \nStill waters shall be treated at least once every week with oil in order to prevent \nmosquito breeding. \niii) \nContractor’s equipment and other items on the site, which may retain water, \nshall be stored, covered or treated in such a manner that water could not be \nretained. \niv) \nWater storage tanks shall be provided. \n \n42.6.2 \nPosters in both Hindi, English and local language which draw attention to the dangers \nof permitting mosquito breeding, shall be displayed prominently on the site. \n \n42.6.3 \nThe contractor at periodic interval shall arrange to prevent mosquito breeding \nby fumigation / spraying of insecticides. Most effective insecticides shall \ninclude SOLFAC WP 10 or Baytex, The Ideal Larvicide etc. \n \n42.7 \nAlcohol and drugs \n \n42.7.1 \nThe contractor shall ensure at all times that no employee is working under the \ninfluence of alcohol / drugs which are punishable under Govt. regulations. \n \n42.7.2 \nSmoking at public worksites by any employee is also prohibited as per Govt. \nregulations. \n \n43.0 \nNoise  \n \n43.1  \nThe Contractor shall consider noise as an environmental constraint in his design, \nplanning and execution of the Works and provide demonstrable evidence of the same \non Employer’s request. The Contractor shall, at his own expense, take all appropriate \nmeasures to ensure that work carried out by the Contractor and by his sub-\nContractors, whether on or off the Site, will not cause any unnecessary or excessive \nnoise which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings, schools, hospitals, or \npremises with similar sensitivity to noise. \n \n43.1.1  \nWithout prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, noise level reduction measures \nshall include the following: \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         82.43981170654297,
>         578.5794677734375,
>         517.2078247070312,
>         772.4918823242188
>       ],
>       "block_number": 4,
>       "text": "i) \nThe Contractor shall ensure that all powered mechanical equipment used in the \nWorks shall be effectively sound reduced using the most modern techniques \navailable including but not limited to silencers and mufflers.  \nii) \nThe Contractor shall construct acoustic screens or enclosures around any parts \nof the Works from which excessive noise may be generated. \n \n43.1.2  \nThe Contractor shall ensure that noise generated by work carried out by the Contractor \nand his sub-Contractors during daytime and night time shall not exceed the maximum \npermissible noise limits, whether continuously or intermittently, as given in the project \nSHE Manual.  The same may be varied from time to time by and at the sole discretion \nof the Employer, In the event of a breach of this requirement, the Contractor shall \nimmediately re-deploy or adjust the relevant equipment or take other appropriate \nmeasures to reduce the noise levels and thereafter maintain them at levels which do \nnot exceed the said limits. Such measures may include without limitation the temporary \nor permanent cessation of use of certain items of equipment. \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         546.0439453125,
>         24.479991912841797,

>         41.38799285888672
>       ],
>       "block_number": 5,
>       "text": "250\n"
>     }

### J79c6bd3eb032dd81

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 44.0 — Ventilation and illumination|SHE 44.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 70, 71 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/3`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "44.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 70,
>       "text": "44.0      Ventilation and illumination\n\n\n44.1      Ventilation"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 71,
>       "text": "44.1.1   The contractor shall ensure at a construction site of a building or other construction\n                 work that all working areas in a free tunnel are provided with ventilation system as\n                 approved by the DG and the fresh air supply in such tunnel is not less than 6m3/min\n                       for each building worker employed underground in such tunnel and the free air flow\n                movement inside such tunnel is not less than 9m/min.\n\n\n          44.1.2   The oxygen level shall not be less than 19.5% in the working environment.\n\n\n          44.2      Illumination\n\n          44.2.1   The contractor shall take every effort to illuminate the work site as per the Employer’s\n                   requirement illustrated in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/011.\n\n          44.2.2   The contractor shall conduct a monthly illumination monitoring by lux meter for\n                         all the locations and the report shall be sent to the Employer within 7th of the\n                  next month and the same shall be reviewed during the monthly SHE committee\n                  meeting."
>     }

### Jeeb17043f0400cc9

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 46.0 — Welfare measures for workers|SHE 46.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 71, 72 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/5`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "46.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 71,
>       "text": "46.0     Welfare measures for workers\n\n\n          46.1      Latrine and Urinal Accommodation\n\n\n          46.1.1   The contractor shall provide one latrine seat for every 20 workers up to 100\n                 workers and thereafter one for every additional 50 workers. In addition one\n                    urinal accommodation shall be provided for every 100 workers.\n\n\n          46.1.2   When women are employed, separate latrine and urinals accommodation shall be\n                   provided on the same scale as mentioned above.\n\n\n          46.1.3    Latrine and urinals shall be provided as per Section 33 of BOCWA and maintained as\n                   per Rule 243 of BOCWR and shall also comply with the requirements of public health\n                      authorities\n\n\n          46.1.4   Moving sites\n\n\n          46.1.4.1  In case of works like track laying, the zone of work is constantly moving at elevated\n                      level or at underground level. In such cases mobile toilets with proper facility to drain\n                    the sullage shall be provided at reasonably accessible distance.\n\n\n          46.1.5    In case if the contractor fail to provide required number of urinals and latrines\n                  or fail to maintain it as per the requirements of Public Health laws, the Employer"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 72,
>       "text": "shall have the right to provide/maintain through renowned external agencies\n           like “Sulabh” at the cost of the contractor.\n\n\n46.2     Canteen\n\n\n46.2.1    In every workplace wherein not less than 250 workers are ordinarily employed\n         the contractor shall provide an adequate canteen conforming to Section 37 of\n       BOCWA, Rule 244 of BOCWR and as stipulated in Rule 247 of BOCWR the\n        changes for food stuff shall be based on ‘no profit no loss’ basis. The price list\n          of all items shall be conspicuously displayed in such canteen.\n\n\n46.3     Serving of tea and snacks at the workplace\n\n\n46.3.1   As per Rule 246 of BOCWR, at a building or other construction work where a\n        workplace is situated at a distance of more than 200 m from the canteen\n         provided under Rule 244(1) of BOCWR, the contractor employing building works\n          shall make suitable arrangement for serving tea and light refreshment to such\n         building works at such place.\n\n46.4     Drinking water\n\n\n46.4.1   As per Section 32 of BOCWA the contractor shall make in every worksite,\n          effective arrangements to provide sufficient supply of wholesome drinking\n         water with minimum quantity of 5 litres per workman per day. Quality of the\n         drinking water shall conform to the requirements of national standards on\n         Public Health.\n\n\n46.4.2   While locating these drinking water facility due care shall be taken so that these are\n           easily accessible within a distance of 200m from the place of work for all workers\n           at all location of work sites.\n\n\n46.4.3     All such points shall be legible marked “Drinking Water” in a language understood by a\n          majority of the workmen employed in such place and such point shall be situated\n           within six metres of any washing places, urinals or latrines.\n\n\n46.5     Labour Accommodation\n\n\n46.5.1   The contractor shall provide free of charges as near as possible, temporary\n          living accommodation to all workers conforming to provisions of Section 34 of\n       BOCWA. These accommodations shall have cooking place, bathing, washing\n        and lavatory facilities\n\n46.6     Creche\n\n46.6.1    In every workplace where in more than 50 female workers are ordinarily employed,\n          there shall be provided and maintained a suitable room for use of children under age\n           of 6 yrs, conforming to the provisions of Section 35 of BOCWA."
>     }

>       "text": "45.0     Radiation\n\n\n          45.1    The use of radioactive substances and radiating apparatus shall comply with the Govt.\n                    regulatory requirements and all subsidiary legislation\n\n\n          45.2     Operations involving ionising radiation shall only be carried out after having been\n                  reviewed without objection by the Employers representative and shall be carried out in\n                  accordance with a method statement.\n\n\n          45.3     each area containing irradiated apparatus shall have warning notices and barriers, as\n                    required by the Regulations, conspicuously posted at or near the area.\n\n\n          45.4     Radioactive substances will be stored, used or disposed shall be strictly in accordance\n                     with the Govt. Enactments.\n\n\n          45.5    The contractor shall ensure that all site personnel and members of the public are not\n                 exposed to radiation."
>     }

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          252\n43.2.10  The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance of tasks specified, and  will\n          inspect necessary records, reports and procedures related to the control of noise.\n\n43.2.11  Impact monitoring shall be carried out at noise sensitive receptor locations within 200\n           feet of the construction site once each week and after a change in construction\n            activity. Construction noise measurements shall coincide with daytime and nighttime\n          periods of maximum noise generating construction activities.\n\n43.2.12  Noise Monitoring data will be submitted in a Noise Measurement Report Form. It will\n          contain the type of measurement, duration of measurement, distance of monitoring\n         from construction site, and construction equipment working during monitoring period.\n\n43.2.13   appropriate  parameter  for measuring  construction  noise  impacts  shall be  the\n          equivalent A-weighted sound pressure level (Leq) measured in decibels (dB). The two\n            statistical sound levels L10 and L90; the level exceeded for 10 and 90 percent of the time\n           respectively, shall also be recorded during monitoring. The L90 may be considered as\n          the ambient level into which the L10 as average peak level intrudes. The Lmax, Leq, L10\n        and L90 values will be reported in the noise measurement form along with allowable\n         noise limit. The duration of monitoring shall be for a minimum of 30 minutes.\n\n43.2..14  In no case  shall the Contractor expose the public  to construction noise levels\n         exceeding 90dBA (slow) or to impulsive noise levels with a peak sound pressure level\n         exceeding 140dB as measured on an impulse sound level meter.\n\n43.2.15   Limit for construction noise is based on the existing ambient noise levels in areas\n          adjoining the construction sites.\n\n43.2.16 The noise levels emanating from any source during construction, shall not exceed 5\n         dB(A) or more above existing ambient pre-construction noise levels when measured at\n        a point outside the premises of the location of source. The same may be varied from\n         time to time by and at the sole discretion of the Engineer.\n43.2.17  Where there are no ambient noise measurements, the construction activities shall be\n           limited to levels measured at a distance of 200 feet from the construction limits or at\n          the nearest affected building, whichever is closer, as given in Table-2.\n                                 TABLE-2\n                  ALLOWABLE CONSTRUCTION NOISE\n     LAND USE               MAXIMUM NOISE LEVELS- Lmax dB (A)\n                                            Day Time Night Time\n          Residential                      75             65\n          At all Times\n          Commercial                                   85\n             Industrial                                     90\n\n\n43.2.18   At the surface of the construction site during night time hours, the Contractor shall use\n          only equipment that operating under full load meets the noise limits specified in Table-\n           3, if a sensitive receptor would be affected.\n                             TABLE-3\n NOISE EMISSION LIMITS FOR CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT USED DURING NIGHTTIME\n              HOURS; MEASURED AT 50 FEET FROM CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT*\n Equipment Category                                     Lmax Level dB(A)\n\n Backhoe                                                80\n Bar Bender                                              75\n Chain Saw                                              81\n Compactor                                              80\n Compressor                                             80\n Concrete Mixer                                           85\n Concrete Pump                                           82\n Crane                                                  85\n Dozer                                                  85\n Front End Loader                                         80\n Generator                                               82\n Gradall                                                 85\n Grader                                                  85\n Paver                                                  85\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 64 of 114",

### J37502be8cd1d4198

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part III: Occupational Health and Welfare|SHE vol3_part3]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 70 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/source_page_context/6`)

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          254\n                  ii)   Keep noise to the lowest reasonably practicable level.  Appropriate measures\n                     will be taken to ensure that construction works will not cause any unnecessary\n                or excessive noise, which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings,\n                schools, hospitals, or premises with similar sensitivity to noise. Use equipment\n                with  effective  noise-suppression  devices and employ  other  noise  control\n             measures as to protect the public.\n\n                  iii)   Schedule and conduct operations in a manner that will minimize, to the greatest\n                extent  feasible,  the  disturbance  to  the  public  in  areas  adjacent  to  the\n                construction  activities and  to occupants  of  buildings  in the  vicinity  of the\n                construction activities.\n\n             iv)   The Contractor shall submit to the Employer a Noise Monitoring and Control\n              Plan (NMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan.   It shall include\n                       full and comprehensive details of all powered mechanical equipment, which he\n              proposes to use during daytime and night - time, and of his proposed working\n             methods and noise level reduction measures. The NMCP shall include detailed\n               noise calculations and vibration levels to demonstrate the anticipated noise\n               generation and vibrations by the Contractor.\n\n           v)   The NMCP prepared by the Contractor  shall guide the implementation  of\n                construction  activity. The NMCP  will be reviewed on a regular basis and\n              updated  as  necessary  to  assure  that  current  construction  activities  are\n               addressed.  It may appear as a regular agenda item in project coordination\n               meetings, if noise is an issue at any location in the contract.\n\n\n43.4     Occupational Noise\n\n\n                i)     Protection  against  the  effects  of  occupational  noise exposure should be\n               provided when the sound level exceeds the threshold values as provided in\n                Project SHE Manual.\n\n                  ii)   When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in the\n                Table, feasible administrative or engineering controls should be utilized as given\n                   in this document and BMRC’s Project SHE Manual.\n\n                  iii)      If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal\n                 protective equipment shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within\n                the levels of the table.\n\n             iv)   When the daily noise exposure is composed of two or more periods of noise\n              exposure of different levels, their combined effect should be considered, rather\n               than the individual effect of each. Exposure to different levels for various periods\n                 of time shall be computed according to the formula and sample computations,\n              as given in project SHE Manual.\n\n\n43.4      Vibration Level\n\n\n43.4.1    In locations where the alignment  is close to  historical  / heritage structures, the\n          contractor shall prepare a monitoring scheme prior to construction at such locations.\n          This scheme for monitoring vibration level at such historical / heritage sites shall be\n         submitted to Employer for his approval. This scheme shall include:\n\n                i)     Monitoring requirements  for  vibrations  at  regular  intervals  throughout  the\n                construction period.\n\n                  ii)    Pre-construction  structural  integrity  inspections  of  historic  and  sensitive\n                structures in project activity.\n\n                  iii)    Information dissemination about the construction method, probable  effects,\n                 quality control measures and precautions to be used.\n\n             iv)   The vibration level limits at work sites adjacent to the alignment shall conform to\n                the permitted values of peak p velocity as given in article project SHE Manual.\n\n\n44.0      Ventilation and illumination\n\n\n44.1      Ventilation\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 66 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n251\n          43.1.3   The noise monitoring requirements including monitoring locations are given in the\n                     project SHE Manual.\n\n\n          43.2    NOISE MONITORING\n\n          43.2.1   The activities which are expected to cause noise during the construction of Bangalore\n                   metro, include noise from construction equipment, construction activities such as portal\n                     construction, boring for piling, earthwork excavation, concreting, viaduct, station, depot\n                    construction (including shifting of launching truss  / girder) and removal of spoil and\n                movement of construction vehicles and delivery vehicles, traveling to and from the\n                    construction and disposal sites.\n          43.2.2   The level of impact of these noise sources depends upon the noise characteristics of\n                    the equipment and activities involved the construction schedule, and the distance from\n                   noise sensitive receptors.\n\n          43.2.3   The Noise Monitoring and Control Plan (NMCP) in contract specific site Environmental\n                    Quality Management Plan prepared by the Contractor shall establish procedures to\n                   monitor construction noise and determine when to apply measures to control noise\n                      pollution due to construction activities at work sites.\n\n          43.2.4   The NMCP will provide site description, define acceptable noise monitoring equipment,\n                    provide siting and operating procedures for noise equipment, indicate reports and record\n                   keeping on noise monitoring data.\n\n\n\n          43.2.5   The NMCP will provide guidance for construction activity.   It shall also address noise\n                  performance criteria used in the selection of construction equipment.\n\n          43.2.6   The Noise Monitoring and Control Plan shall provide for:\n                       a) Definition of noise-sensitive uses in the zones affected by construction.\n                       b)   Calculation of future noise levels at the closest noise-sensitive receptors to the\n                            construction activity based on construction activity and ambient noise levels.\n                        c)   Evaluation and specification of the noise abatement measures that can be\n                           applied to meet the noise objectives.\n                       d)   Monitoring construction activity and providing adjustments to noise abatement\n                             controls that may be required to increase their effectiveness.\n                       e)  regular reporting\n                                 f)   Requirements of NMCP:\n                                            (i)     It shall specify the nighttime and daytime construction activities, monitoring\n                                    locations, equipment, procedures, and schedule of measurements and\n                                   reporting methods to be used.\n                                                (ii)    It shall contain a scaled plan indicating monitoring locations, including\n                            measurements to be taken at construction site boundaries and at nearby\n                                     residential zones.\n                                                  (iii)  a record of the noise characteristics of powered mechanical equipment\n                             proposed to be used during day time and night time and of proposed\n                               working methods and of potential noise level reduction measures.\n                                      (iv)  Provisions for immediate notification when measured noise levels exceed\n                                 allowable limits,\n                                  (v)  Provide a reporting procedure whereby noise-monitoring data is furnished\n                                     to the Engineer on a weekly basis.\n\n          43.2.7    In defining the requirements of the NMCP, available measures for noise control, such\n                    as, the use of equipment with special exhaust silencers or enclosures, and the\n                    construction of temporary enclosures or noise barriers around specific construction\n                       site activity areas shall be considered.  It should also specify the measures to be\n                  adopted to counter the impact of noise pollution for public and workers working at site\n                    during construction.\n\n          43.2.8      If the measured noise levels exceed the noise limits, the noise levels shall be reduced\n                 by appropriate abatement measures.\n\n         43.2.9    The NMCP will be reviewed on a regular basis and updated as necessary to assure\n                    current construction activities are addressed.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 63 of 114",

>       "text": "41.0     Physical fitness of workmen\n\n\n41.1    The contractor shall ensure that his employees/workmen subject themselves to such\n         medical examination as required under the law or under the contract provision and\n        keep a record of the same.\n\n\n41.2    The contractor shall not permit any employee/workmen to enter the work area under\n          the influence of alcohol or any drugs."

>       "text": "47.0 ENVIORNMENTAL MANAGEMENT\n\n             47.1 ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING\n\n              47.1.1 The  Contractor’s  Environmental  Team  shall  carry  out  the  monitoring  of\n                     environmental impacts during construction. Representative sensitive receivers in the\n                           vicinity of the works shall be monitored for noise and air quality impacts.\n              47.1.2  For carrying out impact monitoring for noise and air, equipment shall be provided,\n                    operated and maintained by the Contractor. The equipment shall be kept in a good\n                       state  of  repair  in accordance  with  the  manufacturer’s recommendations and\n                    maintained in proper working order with sufficient spare equipment available in the\n                     event of breakdown to maintain the planned monitoring program.\n              47.1.2 The calibration of monitoring instruments and their respective calibrators shall be\n                       carried out in accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements to ensure they\n                    perform to the same level of accuracy as stated in the manufacturer’s specifications.\n              47.1.3 Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) levels shall be measured by following the\n                     standard high volume sampling method as set out in High Volume Method for\n                  Suspended Particulate, BIS: 5182-1981\n              47.1.4  24-hour average SPM concentration shall be measured by drawing air through a\n                    High Volume Sampler (HVS) fitted with pre-weighted Glass Fiber filter paper at an\n                   average flow rate not less than 1.1m3 per minute.\n              47.1.5 The minimum requirements to the specifications of sound level meter    should be\n                   as given in IS: 9779-1981\n              47.1.6  Engineer will undertake baseline monitoring to establish background levels. Action\n                      Level of the Contractor shall be based on the results of baseline monitoring\n                    program, which will be made available to him prior to start of construction.\n               47.1.7 The Contractor’s monitoring program is summarized in Table –1.\n\n                                       TABLE-1\n\n                SUMMARY OF CONTRACTOR’S MONITORING PROGRAMME\n                Parameter                   Noise                              Air\n\n          Sampling                Day Time (6.00 to 22.00 hrs):   RSPM, SPM\n                                             Lmax, Leq, L10, L90, L50            24-hours of the day\n                                        Night Time (9 PM – 6AM):      CO: 12 hrs from 8.00 to 20.00\n                                             Lmax, Leq, L10, L90, L50, Ldn          hrs.\n\n\n          Frequency               Once a week (when noise     Two 24-hour Samples every\n           At each location              generating activities are           fifteen days at uniform intervals.\n                                      underway).\n           Locations                To  be  determined  by  the  To be determined by the\n                                        Contractor  based  on  noise  Contractor based on air sensitive\n                                           sensitive receptors.              receptors.\n         Number of Locations        4 Locations                  2 Locations\n           Duration  of  Monitoring by  During Civil Construction        During Civil Construction\n           Contractor\n            Additional Requirements     Adhoc monitoring as required.   Ad hoc monitoring as required\n\n\n        47.2EVENT CONTINGENCY PLAN\n        The Contractor shall prepare an Event Contingency Plan under his Site Environmental Plan. The\n         purpose is to provide, in addition to monitoring activities, procedures for ensuring that  if any\n          environmental  exceedance  of  limiting  values  (either  accidental  or  through  inadequate\n          implementation of mitigation measures on part of the Contractor) does occur, the cause is\n          quickly identified and remedied, and that the risk of a similar event recurring is reduced.\n\n\n          47.3      Air Quality\n\n\n          47.3.1   The  Contractor  shall  take  all necessary  precautions  to minimise  fugitive  dust\n                  emissions from operations involving excavation, grading, and clearing of land and\n                    disposal of waste. He shall not allow emissions of fugitive dust from any transport,\n                    handling, construction or storage activity to remain visible in atmosphere beyond the\n                    property line of emission source for any prolonged period of time without notification to\n                    the Employer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "text": "47.3.2   The Contractor shall use construction equipment designed and equipped to minimise\n          or control air pollution. He shall maintain evidence of such design and equipment and\n       make these available for inspection by Employer.\n\n\n47.3.3      If  after  commencement  of  construction  activity,  Employer  believes  that  the\n          Contractor’s equipment or methods of working are causing unacceptable air pollution\n         impacts then these shall be inspected and remedial proposals shall be drawn up by\n          the Contractor, submitted for review to the Employer and implemented.\n\n\n47.3.4    In developing these remedial measures, the Contractor shall inspect and review all\n          dust sources that may be contributing to air pollution. Remedial measures include use\n           of additional / alternative equipment by the Contractor or maintenance / modification of\n           existing equipment of the Contractor.\n\n           In the event that approved remedial measures are not being implemented and serious\n         impacts persist, the Employer may direct the Contractor to suspend work until the\n        measures are implemented, as required under the Contract.\n\n\n47.3.5    Contractor’s  transport  vehicles and  other equipment  shall conform  to emission\n         standards  fixed by  Statutory  Agencies  of Government  of  India  or  the  State\n        Government from time to time. The Contractor shall carry out periodical checks and\n         undertake remedial measures including replacement,  if required, so as to operate\n           within permissible norms.\n\n\n47.3.6   The Contractor shall establish and maintain records of routine maintenance program\n            for internal combustion engine powered vehicles and equipment used on this project.\n       He shall keep records available for inspection by Employer.\n\n\n47.3.7   The Contractor shall cover loads of dust generating materials like debris and soil being\n          transported from construction  sites.  All trucks carrying loose material should be\n         covered and loaded with sufficient free- board to avoid spills through the tailboard or\n          sideboards.\n\n\n47.3.8   The Contractor shall promptly transport all excavation disposal materials of whatever\n          kind so as not to delay work on the project. Stockpiling of materials  will only be\n         allowed at sites designated by the Employer. The Contractor shall place excavation\n          materials in the dumping/disposal areas designated in the plans as given in the\n           specifications.\n\n\n47.3.9   The temporary dumping areas shall be maintained by the Contractor at all times until\n          the excavate is re-utilised for backfilling or as directed by Employer. Dust control\n            activities shall continue even during any work stoppage.\n\n\n\n\n47.3.10  The Contractor shall place material in a manner that will minimize dust production.\n          Material shall be minimized each day and wetted, to minimize dust production. During\n          dry weather, dust control methods must be used daily especially on windy, dry days to\n         prevent any dust from blowing across the site perimeter.\n\n\n47.3.11  The Contractor shall water down construction sites as required to suppress dust,\n          during handling of excavation soil or debris or during demolition. The Contractor will\n       make water sprinklers, water supply and water delivering equipment available at any\n         time that it is required for dust control use. Dust screens will be used, as feasible when\n           additional dust  control measures are needed  specially where the work  is near\n          sensitive receptors.\n\n\n47.3.12  The Contractor shall provide a wash pit or a wheel washing and/or vehicle cleaning\n             facility at the exits from work sites such as construction depots and batching plants. At\n         such facility, high-pressure water jets will be directed at the wheels of vehicles to\n        remove all spoil and dirt."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "text": "47.3.13  The Contractor shall design and implement his blasting techniques so as to minimise\n                     dust, noise, vibration generation and prevention fly rock.\n\n\n          47.3.14   Blasting technique should be consistent not only with nature and quaintly of rock to be\n                    blasted but also the location of blasting.\n\n          47.3.15  The  contractor  shall  give  preference  to  explosives  with  better  environmental\n                      characteristics.\n\n          47.3.16  The Contractor shall protect structures, utilities, pavements roads and other facilities\n                  from disfiguration and damage as a result of his activities. Where this is not possible,\n                    the contractor  shall restore the structures,  utilities, pavements, roads and other\n                          facilities to their original or better, failing which the rectification/restoration work shall\n                be carried out at the risk and cost of the contractor.\n\n\n          47.3.17  The Contractor shall submit to the Employer an Air Monitoring and Control Plan\n               (AMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan to guide construction activity\n                     insofar as it relates to monitoring, controlling and mitigating air pollution.\n\n\n          47.4    AIR MONITORING\n          47.4.1    Construction activities that will generate dust impacts include excavation (including\n                     related activities), material handling and stockpiling, vehicular movement, and wind\n                   erosion of unpaved work areas.\n\n          47.4.2 The impact of fugitive dust on ambient air pollution depends on the quantity generated, as\n                     well as the drift potential of the dust particles injected into the atmosphere. Large dust\n                      particles will settle out near the source and smaller particles are likely to undergo\n                    dispersal over greater distance from the sources and impeded settling. SPM levels will\n                be monitored to evaluate the dust impact during the construction phase of the Project.\n\n          47.4.3   The  Air  Quality  Monitoring and  Control Plan (AMCP)  in  contract-specific  Site\n                   Environmental Plan prepared by the Contractor shall establish procedures to monitor\n                  impact air quality and measures to control air pollution including dust suppression due\n                      to construction activities at work sites. This plan shall contain description of activities\n                      that  will cause degradation  in  air  quality, environmental procedures  to manage\n                     pollutants to minimise the  air  pollution, monitoring program, record keeping and\n                      reporting.\n\n          47.4.4   The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance of tasks specified, and will inspect\n                  necessary records, reports and procedures related to the control of air quality given in\n               AMCP.\n          47.4.5    Information gathered during the AMCP  will be catalogued and maintained by the\n                    Contractor and shall be available for review by the Engineer.\n\n          47.4.6   The exact location of the air monitoring stations located near air sensitive receptors\n                    adjoining the construction sites, such as residences, schools, hotels and hospitals and\n                  placement of monitoring equipment thereat shall be agreed with the Engineer prior to\n               commencement of air monitoring program.\n\n          47.4.7   Impact monitoring during the course  of the Works  shall be carried out  at the\n                    monitoring stations for two days (continuous twenty-four hours) every fifteen days and\n                 where there is a perceived air quality problem.\n          47.4.8   The Contractor shall construct suitable fence, lockable gate, 220V AC power point and\n                     suitable access at each air monitoring station.  Monitoring stations shall be free from\n                      local obstructions or sheltering.\n\n\n          47.4.9   Should impact monitoring record dust levels which are:\n\n\n                       indicative of a deteriorating situation such that closer monitoring is reasonably\n                          indicated, or\n\n\n                      when in the opinion of the Engineer additional measurements are required in view\n                          of deteriorating air quality,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 76,
>       "text": "Then the Engineer may require the Contractor to increase the frequency of impact\n          monitoring at any one or more of the monitoring stations until the results indicate an\n         improving and acceptable level of air quality.\n\n\n47.4.10  The Contractor shall keep records of air quality monitoring (including location, date,\n           time). The Contractor shall submit a copy of monitoring results to the Engineer. The\n           results should represent a  statistical evaluation of data by calculating maximum,\n        minimum, mean, standard deviation, geometric mean and percentile calculations for\n          evaluation of frequency distribution, trends, and comparison with emission standards.\n\n\n47.4.11  The National Ambient Air Quality Standards given in Air (Prevention and Control of\n           Pollution) Act, 1981 may be referred by the Contractor for Limit Levels of SPM in\n         ambient  air which may be followed  in estimating the  pollution  level caused by\n          Contractor’s activities.\n\n47.4.12  Where  the  Engineer  determines  that  the  recorded  dust  (TSP)  level  is\n          significantly  greater  than  the  Limit  levels,  the Engineer may  direct  the\n         Contractor to take effective remedial measures including, but not limited to,\n         reviewing dust sources and modifying working procedures.\n\n47.4.13  Where the recorded baseline levels exceed the ambient air quality standards, then at\n         such locations the action level is the recorded base line. Contractor shall take all\n           effective remedial measures to contain the levels to their baseline value as a result of\n           his activities. The action level may be varied by and at the sole discretion of the\n         Engineer.\n\n47.4.14 The Contractor shall inform the Engineer of  all steps taken to investigate cause of\n        exceedance and immediate action taken to avoid further exceedance through written\n         reports and proposals for action under an Event Contingency Plan."
