>       "text": "9.0      COMPOSITION OF TENDER SUBMITTALS\n\n  9.1       The Tenderer's tender submittals shall comprise of (a) Technical Bid (Cover) containing the\n           documents listed in sub-clause 9.2 of Instructions to Tenderers (ITT)) and (b) Financial Bid\n             (Cover) containing the documents listed in sub-clause 9.4 of Instructions to Tenderers (ITT).\n\n  9.2      TECHNICAL BID\n\n  9.2.1     The Tenderer shall upload soft copies (in .pdf format) of the duly completed Technical Bid on\n             the e-Procurement Portal under the “Technical Cover.” The Technical Cover shall comprise\n             the documents and information specified herein.\n\n               (a)   Copy of Tender Security (EMD) in accordance with Clause 13 of Instructions to\n                  Tenderers (ITT).\n\n               (b)   Copy of Power  of Attorney authorizing the signatory to commit the Tender,  in\n                 accordance with sub clause 14.1 of Instructions to Tenderers (ITT).\n\n                (c)   The Letter of Technical Bid (including all Attachments) shall be complete without any\n                      alterations to their content/format."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 14,
>       "text": "(d)   Documentary evidence/ qualification documents required to establish the Tenderer’s\n                             qualifications under Eligibility and qualification criteria.\n\n                       (e)    ‘Tenderer’s Brief of Technical Details’ for performing the assignment/work as per\n                        Attachment 14 to Letter of Technical bid.\n\n                             (f)   Any other documents requested in the Bid document as a part of the Technical Bid.\n\n          9.2.2     The technical bid must have all pages sequentially numbered, with an index sheet indicating\n                    the corresponding page numbers. Tenderers should note that submitting a copy of the\n                  tender documents downloaded from the e-Procurement portal is not required.\n\n         9.3      No information relating to Financial Terms of Service, Conditions, or Prices should be\n                  included in the Technical bid. Any such violation will result in the rejection of the Tender.\n\n         9.4      FINANCIAL BID\n\n          9.4.1     The Tenderer shall upload soft copies (.pdf/ .xls) of Financial Proposal duly completed/filled\n                 on the e-Procurement Portal in the ‘Financial Cover’ which shall comprise of following:\n\n                         (a) The Letter of Price Bid shall be completed without any alterations to their content/\n\n                          format.\n\n                         (b) Price Bid (.xls format) shall be completed as per clause 10.1 of ITT.\n\n          9.4.2      Bidders shall submit their Price bid only in the format (.xls format) provided and no other\n                    format is acceptable. If the Price bid format is found to be modified by the bidder, the bid may\n                 be rejected.\n\n         9.5      The  list of documents to be submitted, as described under Clauses 9.2 and 9.4 of the\n                      Instructions to Tenderers (ITT), has been provided solely for the convenience of the Tenderer.\n                Any omission or oversight in this list shall not relieve the Tenderer of the responsibility to\n                    thoroughly review all provisions of the Tender Documents and to submit all information and\n                 documents specifically required or implied therein.\n\n             BMRCL shall not take cognizance  of, nor be bound by, any additional information or\n                 documents submitted by the Tenderer if, in the opinion of BMRCL, such information is not\n                    required or is likely to materially affect the tendering process."

### J96c0758e1616249f

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 43.0 — Noise|SHE 43.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 66 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/2/fragments/0`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 66,
>   "text": "43.0     Noise\n\n\n43.1    The Contractor shall consider noise as an environmental constraint in his design,\n          planning and execution of the Works and provide demonstrable evidence of the same\n        on Employer’s request. The Contractor shall, at his own expense, take all appropriate\n        measures  to ensure  that work  carried out by the Contractor and by  his sub-\n          Contractors, whether on or off the Site, will not cause any unnecessary or excessive\n         noise which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings, schools, hospitals, or\n         premises with similar sensitivity to noise.\n\n\n43.1.1    Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, noise level reduction measures\n           shall include the following:\n\n\n                i)    The Contractor shall ensure that all powered mechanical equipment used in the\n             Works shall be effectively sound reduced using the most modern techniques\n                available including but not limited to silencers and mufflers.\n\n                  ii)   The Contractor shall construct acoustic screens or enclosures around any parts\n                 of the Works from which excessive noise may be generated.\n\n\n43.1.2   The Contractor shall ensure that noise generated by work carried out by the Contractor\n        and his sub-Contractors during daytime and night time shall not exceed the maximum\n          permissible noise limits, whether continuously or intermittently, as given in the project\n       SHE Manual. The same may be varied from time to time by and at the sole discretion\n           of the Employer, In the event of a breach of this requirement, the Contractor shall\n         immediately re-deploy or adjust the relevant equipment or take other appropriate\n        measures to reduce the noise levels and thereafter maintain them at levels which do\n          not exceed the said limits. Such measures may include without limitation the temporary\n          or permanent cessation of use of certain items of equipment."
> }

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol1/secB#Clause 20.0 — Clarification of Tenders|ITT 20.0]], `Vol1DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 20 (`parsed_json/vol1/section_b_itt/itt_clauses.json#/clauses/19`)

> {

>     {
>       "pdf_page": 20,
>       "text": "20.0     CLARIFICATION OF TENDERS\n\n         20.1       Evaluation of Technical Bids submitted by Tenderers shall be undertaken based on details\n                   submitted in the Technical Bids only. Employer may at his discretion ask any Tenderer for\n                        clarification on his submittals through eProcurement portal. The Tenderer, in response to the\n                         clarification, is not permitted to submit additional document not pertaining to the clarification\n                    sought. The request for clarification and the response shall be in writing only through\n                  eProcurement Portal and no response leading to material change in the submittals will be\n                   taken into consideration.  It is not mandatory for Employer to seek clarification. Employer\n                   reserves the right to evaluate the bids based on documents submitted by the bidders.\n\n         20.2       Notwithstanding the provision in Para 20.1 above, the Tenderer must take care that all\n                    required documents  to  establish  their  Eligibility &  Qualification and other mandatory\n                   requirements must be submitted before the deadline for submission.\n\n         20.3      During the evaluation of financial bid, the Employer may ask Tenderers individually for\n                        clarification regarding their price bids, including the breakup of prices. The request for\n                        clarification and the response shall be in writing and no change in the price or substance of\n                    the Price bid shall be sought, offered, or permitted except as required to confirm the correction\n                      of arithmetical errors discovered by the Employer during the evaluation of Tenders in\n                  accordance with Clause 22.2.5.\n\n         20.4           If a Bidder does not provide clarifications of his bid by the date and time set in the Employer’s\n                    request for clarification, their bid shall be evaluated as per the available information in the\n                   submitted bid."
>     }
>   ],

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n207\n          11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable the Employer to\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions of Contract, the\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE Plan.\n\n\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines.  The\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\n                      invited to attend.\n\n\n          11.2.4   Timing\n\n\n                The Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\n                       prior to the scheduled date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\n\n\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\n\n\n          11.2.5.1  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\n                        their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\n                    the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\n                    applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\n                  achieved by:\n\n\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\n\n                                  Maximum Possible Score\n\n\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\n                      classified as:\n\n\n                          Sl.                                       hours\n\n                 2    < 75%   Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\n                                Necessary               confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable    Contractor rectification within one month\n                                                    and confirmed                ii)   Adequacy of power generation and power requirements\n\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission system in place\n\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the current condition of power\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\n\n                      v) >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n209\n          11.4.5   Audit Documents:\n\n\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by\n                  the Audit team.\n\n\n                                 i)   SHE policy\n\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\n\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\n\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\n\n                          vi)   Accident / near miss statistics and analysis\n\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records for all personnel\n\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments\n\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears\n\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\n\n                          xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\n\n                             xii)   Environmental management reports\n\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records including mock drill\n\n\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\n\n\n                                 i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\n                           interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\n\n                                    ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\n                           rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\n\n                                     iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\n                      gaps and weakness.\n\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion.\n\n\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\n\n\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\n                   conducting the audit with a copy to the contractor.\n\n\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\n\n\n                                 i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\n                        concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\n\n                                    ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\n                     and post-audit activities).\n\n                                     iii)    Principal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\n                       observed by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\n                   may warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\n                        achievement.\n\n\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\n\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally be\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\n\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\n                                    injury or business loss.\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "block_number": 3,
>       "text": "11.4.5 \nAudit Documents: \n \n11.4.5.1   Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by \nthe Audit team. \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.55968475341797,
>         107.69955444335938,
>         438.24700927734375,
>         334.4921875
>       ],
>       "block_number": 4,
>       "text": "i) \nSHE policy \nii) \nSHE manual \niii) \nSHE Rules and Regulation \niv) \nSHE organization chart \nv) \nAnnual SHE objectives / programs \nvi) \nAccident / near miss statistics and analysis \nvii) \nSHE Training program / records for all personnel \nviii) \nOperating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments \nix) \nSafe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears \nx) \nMedical fitness record for all personnel \nxi) \nRisk identification, assessment and control details \nxii) \nEnvironmental management reports \nxiii) \nEmergency management records including mock drill  \n \n11.4.6 \nAudit Preparation: \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.56017303466797,
>         339.65972900390625,
>         520.3269653320312,
>         539.9319458007812
>       ],
>       "block_number": 5,
>       "text": "i) \nAudit team members are required to gather information by observations through \ninterviews and by checks of hardware and documentation. \nii) \nAudit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations \nrules and regulations and BMRC requirements. \niii) \nAudit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified \ngaps and weakness. \niv) \nAudit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion. \n \n11.4.7 \nReporting: \n \n11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of \nconducting the audit with a copy to the contractor. \n \n11.4.8 \nReport contents: \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         130.55857849121094,
>         545.0994873046875,
>         515.88671875,
>         704.4518432617188
>       ],
>       "block_number": 6,
>       "text": "i) \nExecuting summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to \nthe Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader will compile a \nconcise and accurate summary of observations and findings. \nii) \nIntroduction - this will contain basic information regarding the facilities or \norganization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation \nand post-audit activities). \niii) \nPrincipal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as \nobserved by the auditors.  It will also contain highlights of those issue, which \nmay warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or \nachievement. \n \niv) \nAudit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be \ngrouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing. \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.5599594116211,
>         707.7802124023438,
>         85.82657623291016,
>         708.681640625
>       ],
>       "block_number": 7,
>       "text": " \n"
>     },

>       "bbox": [
>         130.5598907470703,
>         711.8602294921875,
>         130.82650756835938,
>         712.7616577148438
>       ],
>       "block_number": 8,
>       "text": " \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [

>         717.899169921875,
>         515.8870849609375,
>         790.7316284179688
>       ],
>       "block_number": 9,
>       "text": "a) \nPriority 1: Actions to rectify gaps or weakness should generally be \nimplemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable. \nb) \nPriority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a \nmaximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor \ninjury or business loss. \n \n"
>     },

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          208\n              vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\n\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\n\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance system and register.\n\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\n\n             xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\n\n11.4   External SHE Audi\n\n\n11.4.1    External SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors with the prior approval of the Employer.\n\n\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\n\n\n11.4.2.1  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\n         health/medical and welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\n        and control, traffic management, electrical safety, rigging, safety of construction\n        equipment and environment management.\n\n\n11.4.2.2  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\n         standards. Audit report shall also be presented as per the above formats.\n\n\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted on a quarterly basis throughout the\n         currency of the contract.\n\n\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE Audit:\n\n\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\n\n\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\n\n\n                i)     Organization\n\n                  ii)    Communication and Motivation\n\n                  iii)   Time office\n\n             iv)    Inspection\n\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\n\n             vi)   Budget allocation\n\n              vii)   Education and Training\n\n               viii)  Work permit system\n\n\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\n\n\n                i)     Building and Structure\n\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\n\n                  iii)    Material safety\n\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\n\n           v)     Electrical system\n\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\n\n              vii)   Fire prevention and control\n\n               viii)  Housekeeping\n\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery safety\n\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\n\n             xi)   Welfare measures\n\n              xii)   Environmental Management\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n213\n                 such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\n\n\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\n\n\n          14.3     Accident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.1   General\n\n\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\n\n\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\n\n\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\n                management system.\n\n\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\n\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\n\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\n                          conditions\n\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\n\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\n\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\n\n\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\n\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\n\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\n\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\n\n\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\n\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\n\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\n\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\n\n\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\n\n\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\n                  about the accident.\n\n\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\n                  completes the investigation.\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 25 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          212\n14.2.1    In addition to the above verbal and written reporting to the Employer, as per Rule 210\n           of BOCWR, notice of any accident to a worker at the building or construction site that:\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\n                 following the accident;\n\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\n\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\n                     the firm/work\n\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\n\n                             iii)    Director General and\n\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\n\n\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\n\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\n\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\n\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\n\n\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\n          treatment.\n\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\n\n\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\n\n\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\n         namely:\n\n\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\n               work;\n\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\n\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\n            means of access including formwork;\n\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\n                 building material;\n\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\n                 building workers are employed;\n\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\n\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\n\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\n\n\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 24 of 114",

>       "text": "a) \ncauses loss of life; or \nb) \ndisables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to \ni) \nthe officer-in-charge of the nearest police station; \nii) \nthe District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to \niii) \nthe Sub-Divisional Magistrate \n \n14.2.3 \nIn case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the \ninjured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical \ntreatment. \n14.2.4 \nWhere any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in \nwriting of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and \n14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death. \n \n14.2.5 \nReporting of dangerous occurrences:  \n \n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector \nhaving jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker, \nnamely: \n \n"

>       "text": "57.0     Stoppage of work\n\n\n          57.1    The Employer shall have the right to stop the work at his sole discretion, if in his opinion the\n                 work is being carried out in such a way that  it may cause accidents and endanger the\n                    safety of the persons and / or property, and / or equipments. In such cases, the contractor\n                      shall be informed in writing about the nature of hazards and possible injury / accident.\n\n\n          57.2    The contractor shall not proceed with the work until he has complied with each direction to\n                    the satisfaction of Employer.\n\n          57.3    The Contractor shall not be entitled for any damages / compensation for stoppage of work,\n                due to safety reasons and the period of such stoppage of work shall not be taken as an\n                   extension of time for Completion of the Facilities and will not be the ground for waiver of\n                    levy of liquidated damages."

>   "text": "56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\n\n\n   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\n              of seven years. Any reportable accident (fatality / injury) results in loss of life and/or\n             property damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\n             reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\n              to contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\n             contractors for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\n\n\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\n            executed just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe act  / unsafe condition observed by\n              public further damages our reputation. Because of the non-voluntary compliance of\n             contractors to the condition of contract on SHE and project SHE manual, BMRC has\n           been forced to establish safety-enforcing organisation.
